intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to amplify a partisan narrative that portrays the mainstream media as irrational, childish, and hypocritical while simultaneously lionizing Sarah Huckabee Sanders (and by extension the Trump administration) as composed and unfairly besieged. By spotlighting Mike Huckabee’s “preschoolers” quip and framing the CNN-wrestling tweet as “hilarious,” the piece seeks to delegitimize critical journalism and rally conservative viewers through mockery and familial loyalty rather than substantive argument.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports a real televised segment from the June 29, 2017 edition of Fox News’ Hannity (guest-hosted that night by Kimberly Guilfoyle) in which former Arkansas governor Mike Huckabee praised his daughter Sarah Huckabee Sanders and likened the press corps to petulant preschoolers; the quote and context match the broadcast video and contemporaneous media coverage, so the item is not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The item is a faithful report of what Mike Huckabee actually said on Fox News; it does not invent events or quotes, so it is not fake news, even though its partisan framing and the analogy equating reporters with preschoolers are misleading and delegitimize standard press scrutiny.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The item is not fabricated, but it functions as disinformation by deliberately reframing legitimate journalistic scrutiny as infantile harassment, using selective ridicule and false equivalence (equating press questions to petulant toddlers) to delegitimize accountability and advance a partisan narrative without engaging facts.

title: Obama Joins Comedy Central Host to Push ‘Laughable’ Establishment Conspiracy Theory on DNC Leaks
subject: Middle-east
content: 21st Century Wire says President Obama is once again appearing on  info-tainment  programming on Comedy Central but his appearance is clearly not to entertain or inform the viewer. In the final days of the President s time in office he is going on comedy shows to push the  Russian hack  effect on the U.S. Presidential election outcome. He does so without a shred of evidence nor a mention of the Podesta emails, the collusion of the media with the Clinton campaign or the questionable practices of the Clinton Foundation.The Duran asks some good questions and provides further analysis  Alex Christoforou The DuranObama has gone all in to blame Russia for Hillary Clinton s loss and the DNC hack that exposed Hillary Clinton for the corrupt cheat that we all knew, deep down inside, she truly was.Notice how Obama talks only about the DNC hack and not the Wikileaks Podesta email leak. Also notice how Obama tries to justify his conveniently timed call for an investigation, by throwing it back onto Donald Trump.Obama never states that he has irrefutable evidence that Russia hacked the DNC emails, and never even mentions once the Podesta emails We determined and announced in October that it was the consensus of all the Intelligence agencies in law enforcement that organizations affiliated with Russian intelligence were responsible for the hacking of the DNC materials that were being leaked. FYI China, Israel, Germany, etc  also hack US institutions. US intelligence agencies hack governments all over the world.Obama s above assertions are based on James Clapper s statement that The Duran reported on in October consider the statement US intelligence published last week on the subject of alleged Russian hacking of the Democratic National Committee and of other US agencies involved in the election. It reads as follows: The U.S. Intelligence Community (USIC) is confident that the Russian Government directed the recent compromises of e-mails from US persons and institutions, including from US political organizations. The recent disclosures of alleged hacked e-mails on sites like DCLeaks.com and WikiLeaks and by the Guccifer 2.0 online persona are consistent with the methods and motivations of Russian-directed efforts. These thefts and disclosures are intended to interfere with the US election process. Such activity is not new to Moscow the Russians have used similar tactics and techniques across Europe and Eurasia, for example, to influence public opinion there.We believe, based on the scope and sensitivity of these efforts, that only Russia s senior-most officials could have authorized these activities. (bold italics added)The statement is an implicit admission that US intelligence has no evidence to back its allegations of Russian hacking.It is merely  confident    not  sure    that it is the Russians who are behind the hacking, and it is clear from the statement that it arrived at this conclusion purely through inference: because the hacks supposedly were  consistent with the methods and motivations of Russian-directed efforts .US intelligence assumes the Russians were behind the hack not because it knows this to be so but in part because of what it believes Russian motives to be.The statement backs its claim with a textual trick.  It says  the Russians have used similar tactics and techniques across Europe and Eurasia .  It then immediately follows these words with the words  for example .These lead to the expectation that an actual example of such Russian  tactics and techniques  is about to follow. Instead what is provided are the fact free words  to influence public opinion there .The words  for example  lend nothing to the meaning of the statement, which would be exactly the same without them.  These two words as used in the statement are actually meaningless.   That is a sure sign that their presence in the statement is intended to confuse the casual reader, and that this is true of the statement as a whole.The words are designed to create a subliminal impression to a casual reader that the Russians have been caught doing this sort of thing before, without however providing a single actual example when this was the case.Demonstrating how thin the case of Russian government actually is, the statement then goes on to say: Some states have also recently seen scanning and probing of their election-related systems, which in most cases originated from servers operated by a Russian company. However, we are not now in a position to attribute this activity to the Russian Government. (bold italics added)In other words US intelligence admits the mere fact servers operated by a Russian company may have been used for  scanning and probing    and presumably also for hacking   is not in itself proof of the involvement of the Russian government.The Daily Show s Trevor Noah, who is not a journalist, and not even American, is the perfect useful idiot to conduct this interview and help spread Obama s political spin.No tough question, no follow up questions just giggly gushing glances of admiration and awe from Noah.Remember when Obama told Trump to  stop whining  about a rigged election and focus on  getting votes. This was when Obama, and the entire Hillary liberal elite establishment, were certain that Trump had no chance to win the US Presidency.How things change, and how Obama is now changing his tune doing everything in his power to undermine Trump and undermine US Democracy, while risking escalating, already high tensions with Russia.Continue reading this story at The DuranREAD MORE ELECTION NEWS AT: 21st Century Wire 2016 Files
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively omits the October 2016 joint-DHS/ODNI statement, subsequent Mueller indictments, and Senate Intel findings that did provide forensic evidence of GRU involvement, while falsely equating intelligence-community ‘confidence’ with ‘no evidence.’ It reframes established investigative conclusions as mere ‘political spin,’ uses loaded terms like ‘laughable’ and ‘useful idiot,’ and redirects attention to unrelated Podesta/Clinton-Foundation narratives, creating a misleading impression that the Russian-hack attribution is entirely evidence-free and solely an anti-Trump conspiracy.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize the U.S. intelligence consensus that Russia interfered in the 2016 election by framing it as a politically motivated, evidence-free “conspiracy theory” cooked up by President Obama and establishment elites to excuse Hillary Clinton’s loss and undermine Donald Trump. By ridiculing the intelligence language, omitting any discussion of the actual content of the leaks, and painting the Comedy Central interview as propaganda, the piece seeks to erode trust in mainstream institutions, deflect scrutiny from Russia’s role, and reinforce a populist narrative that the “real” threat to democracy comes from domestic elites, not foreign actors.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents a one-sided, conspiratorial narrative that dismisses the U.S. intelligence community’s assessment of Russian interference as baseless, relying on selective quotation, ad hominem attacks, and misrepresentation of official statements; it ignores corroborated evidence and bipartisan investigations, while promoting fringe sources like 21st Century Wire and The Duran, which have a history of spreading disinformation.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece systematically suppresses the 2016 DHS/ODNI joint statement, Mueller’s GRU indictments, the Senate Intel report and the declassified NSA/CIA forensic findings that together constitute concrete evidence for Russian interference, while falsely equating intelligence-community confidence with ‘no evidence’ and using loaded language to cast the attribution as a purely political anti-Trump fabrication.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece systematically ignores the 2016 DHS/ODNI joint statement, the 2018 GRU indictments, and bipartisan Senate Intelligence reports that detailed forensic evidence of Russian hacking, while falsely equating intelligence-community confidence with having no proof and using loaded ridicule to delegitimize established findings, making it a deliberately deceptive narrative rather than legitimate reporting.

title: BROTHER OF SETH RICH Works For Cyber Security Firm…Reportedly BLOCKED Family’s Private Investigator From Determining If Seth Was Wikileaks Source…Refused To Let Investigator See Seth’s Computer: “I already checked it…Don’t worry about it”
subject: Government News
content: What the heck is going on? Why is the media, who has been virtually silent about former DNC staffer Seth Rich s death until now, coming out to attack President Trump and his administration, accusing them of pushing a false narrative about his murder? Shouldn t every American regardless of political affiliation want to get to the bottom of Rich s suspicious death? Why is there so much secrecy and mystery surrounding the staffer who was getting ready to move over to the Hillary campaign when he was murdered on the streets of DC, only blocks from his home early in the morning, after he was last seen leaving a local bar he frequented. The DC police called it a robbery. The  robbers  didn t take his wallet, the contents of his wallet or his expensive watch.Aaron Rich, who had reportedly been blocking his family s private investigator from looking into whether or not his brother Seth was a WikiLeaks source, works for an influential defense contractor that provides cyber security.According to a source close to the Rich family, Aaron works for Northrup Grumman, which was named as the fifth-largest defense contractor in the world in 2015. The source did not provide what his specific role is at the company. It s not just hacking and defending, there s a lot more to it,  a cyber software engineer at Northrup Grumman says in a video on the company s website.As we previously reported, Aaron Rich was actively attempting to shut down anyone looking into the WikiLeaks connection according to Rod Wheeler, who was brought on as a private investigator in his brother s murder case.Wheeler said that brother Aaron Rich tried to block Wheeler from looking at Seth s computer, even though there could be evidence on it.  He said no, he said I have his computer, meaning him,  Wheeler said.  I said, well can I look at it? He said, what are you looking for? I said anything that could indicate if Seth was having problems with someone. He said no, I already checked it. Don t worry about it. Aaron also blocked Wheeler from finding out about who was at a party Seth attended the night of the murder. All I want you to do is work on the botched robbery theory and that s it,  Aaron told Wheeler, according to Wheeler s claim on the audio. Wheeler said that Seth s father Joel  does not appear to have any hidden agenda. Rich was shot in the back in the early morning hours of July 10, 2016, near his home while he was on the phone with his girlfriend   12 days before the publication of the DNC emails by WikiLeaks. The police initially ruled that it was a botched robbery   but his wallet, watch, and necklace were still on his person when he was discovered by police.Big League Politics has also released an audio recording of journalist Seymour Hersh stating that Seth Rich was in fact WikiLeaks  source.Listen to the Seymour Hersh interview here: All I know is that he offered a sample, an extensive sample, I m sure dozens of emails, and said  I want money.  Later, WikiLeaks did get the password, he had a DropBox, a protected DropBox,  he said. They got access to the DropBox. Hersh also states that Rich had concerns about something happening to him,  the word was passed, according to the NSA report, he also shared this DropBox with a couple of friends, so that  if anything happens to me it s not going to solve your problems,  he added.  WikiLeaks got access before he was killed. For entire story: Big League Politics
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article strings together unverified claims (Aaron Rich’s employer, Rod Wheeler’s disputed statements, a selectively-edited Seymour Hersh recording) to imply a cover-up without evidence, presenting speculation as fact and omitting that Wheeler retracted key claims, the Hersh audio is informal and unconfirmed, and law-enforcement found no WikiLeaks link, thereby misleading readers into believing a conspiracy is proven.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to fuel a conspiratorial narrative that Seth Rich was murdered for leaking DNC emails to WikiLeaks, and to cast suspicion on his brother Aaron and others as participants in a cover-up. By selectively highlighting unverified claims, emphasizing withheld evidence, and framing routine investigative limitations as sinister obstruction, the text seeks to undermine official accounts, erode trust in mainstream media and law enforcement, and politically weaponize Rich’s death against Democrats and the traditional press.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article recycles long-debunked conspiracy claims—e.g., that Seth Rich was WikiLeaks’ DNC source—built on anonymous sources, discredited private investigator Rod Wheeler, and a selectively-edited Seymour Hersh audio; Wheeler himself retracted and sued Fox News for misrepresentation, the FBI and Mueller investigation found zero evidence Rich supplied emails, DC police maintain it was a street robbery, and Aaron Rich’s employment at Northrop Grumman provides no evidentiary link to murder or cover-up, making the piece a textbook disinformation narrative.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article recycles long-debunked conspiracy talking points: Rod Wheeler retracted his insinuations under oath and sued Fox News for misquoting him; Seymour Hersh says his captured conversation was mere gossip and not confirmation; D.C. police, the FBI, Mueller’s probe and multiple independent reviews found zero evidence that Seth Rich leaked DNC e-mails or that his murder was political; Aaron Rich’s employment at a defense contractor is irrelevant and no proof of a cover-up; presenting these discredited fragments as new, proven facts is classic disinformation.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece recycles long-debunked conspiracy talking points—Wheeler retracted his ‘blocked computer’ claim, the Hersh recording is an off-the-cuff remark he never vetted, and every official probe (D.C. police, FBI, Mueller) found zero evidence that Rich leaked to WikiLeaks—while omitting these crucial corrections and presenting speculation as proven fact, making the entire narrative false.

title: Trump Campaign Renews Attack On Military Family (AUDIO)
subject: News
content: An official representative of Donald Trump s presidential campaign has once again launched an attack on the family of fallen soldier Captain Humayun Khan.This time the attack comes from conservative Carl Paladino, the New York co-chair of the Trump for President Campaign.In a radio interview with Imus in the Morning, Paladino argued that Khizr Khan, Khan s father who gave a rousing speech to the Democratic Convention, does not deserve to be called a  Gold Star parent  even though he lost his son in combat in Iraq in 2004. We ve got an un-indicted felon as his opponent and you re talking about Khan, about him making a remark about this man,  Paladino, a former New York gubernatorial candidate, told interviewer Connell McShane on Imus in the Morning.  All right, I don t care if he s a Gold Star parent. He certainly doesn t deserve that title, OK, if he s as anti-American as he s illustrated in his speeches and in his discussion. I mean, if he s a member of the Muslim Brotherhood or supporting, you know, the ISIS-type of attitude against America, there s no reason for Donald Trump to have to honor this man. The Trump campaign s heartless attacks against the Khans have received widespread condemnation across America, with even some Trump supporters saying that the line was crossed in attacking the family. Trump himself belittled the family s sacrifices, pointing to his work as a real estate developer as comparable to losing a child. It is strange that in light of Trump s collapsing support in national polls that his campaign would return to this topic.Featured image via YouTube
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: Carl Paladino’s on-air statement vilifies a bereaved Muslim father by baselessly branding him as ‘anti-American’, ‘Muslim Brotherhood’, and ‘ISIS-type’, then explicitly denies him the honorific ‘Gold Star parent’—a direct, identity-based attack intended to delegitimize and dehumanize the Khan family because of their religion and ethnicity, meeting the definition of bias-motivated, hostile expression.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize Donald Trump’s candidacy by spotlighting and amplifying the campaign’s continued perceived disrespect toward a gold-star military family, framing the episode as beyond the bounds of acceptable political discourse. By juxtaposing the campaign’s “heartless” rhetoric with bipartisan condemnation and with Hillary Clinton’s empathetic response, the piece invites readers to view Trump and his surrogates as lacking the moral authority to lead, thereby reinforcing a narrative that Trump is temperamentally unfit for the presidency.

disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article excerpt selectively quotes Horsey’s column, strips out its satirical framing, and recasts it as pure sexist attack, thereby misleading readers about the author’s intent and the full context of the piece; while Horsey did use appearance-based imagery, the excerpt exaggerates the prominence and malice of those lines and omits his broader political critique, creating a distorted impression designed to inflame outrage rather than inform.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize outrage—especially among conservatives—by amplifying a left-on-left criticism into a broader culture-war narrative. By selectively quoting liberal detractors and highlighting the most inflammatory lines while ignoring Horsey’s apology and the Times’ editorial response, the piece reframes a single columnist’s lapse into evidence of systemic left-wing hypocrisy and “fake-news” bias, driving clicks, email harassment, and partisan solidarity rather than fostering good-faith media accountability.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports the backlash against Los Angeles Times columnist David Horsey for his 2017 column that mocked White House Press Secretary Sarah Sanders with body-shaming and sexist language; Horsey publicly apologized and the LA Times removed the offending descriptions, corroborating the incident and the cited criticism from other journalists.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The excerpt is a selectively-edited, outrage-baiting summary that removes the satirical context and broader political critique of Horsey’s original column, exaggerates isolated appearance-based lines into a malicious sexist tirade, and omits his substantive policy criticisms, thereby manufacturing a false narrative designed to inflame rather than accurately report what was written.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The item is not a neutral report but a rage-bait post that strips David Horsey’s satirical column of context, inflates a few appearance-based lines into a wholesale sexist diatribe, and omits his apology and the paper’s corrective action; its selective quoting and call-to-harass make it a manufactured outrage narrative rather than factual news.

title: WOW! NEW REPORT: IRS Didn’t Tell 1 Million Taxpayers That Illegals Stole Their Social Security Numbers!
subject: Government News
content: REMEMBER BECKY GERRITSON OF ALABAMA WHOSE TEA PARTY GROUP WAS TARGETED BY THE IRS? SHE GAVE AN IMPASSIONED SPEECH TO CONGRESS. It seems the IRS hasn t changed its tune!The IRS has discovered more than 1 million Americans whose Social Security numbers were stolen by illegal immigrants, but officials never bothered to tell the taxpayers themselves, the agency s inspector general said in a withering new report released Tuesday. Investigators first alerted the IRS to the problem five years ago, but it s still not fixed, the inspector general said, and a pilot program meant to test a solution was canceled   and fell woefully short anyway. As a result, most taxpayers don t learn that their identities have been stolen and their Social Security files may be screwed up. Taxpayers identified as victims of employment-related identity theft are not notified,  the inspector general said. The report alarmed lawmakers on Capitol Hill, who were shocked that the IRS had gone for so long without fixing the issue.  It is stunning that the IRS has chosen to aid and abet identity thieves for so long instead of protecting the innocent victims of the theft,  said Sen. Daniel Coats, Indiana Republican.Victims  numbers are stolen by illegal immigrants who need to give employers a valid Social Security number in order to get a job. Employers are prohibited from probing too deeply into numbers, even when they suspect fraud. But the IRS learns of the scam when the illegal immigrants file their taxes using a special Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) the agency doles out chiefly to illegal immigrants as a way of making sure they re paying taxes even if they re not supposed to be in the U.S. Between 2011 and 2015 the agency flagged nearly 1.1 million returns where someone appeared to have stolen a valid Social Security number, the inspector general said.Read more: WT
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece selects only those cases in which an ITIN return shows a W-2 with an SSN that later appears on the SSA’s ‘no-match’ list, frames this as 1 million citizens victimised by ‘illegals’, and omits the IRS/IG explanation that the same statistical file also contains citizens who simply typed a wrong digit, teenagers using a parent’s SSN, or seasonal workers whose names changed. By presenting the statistic without that context and by linking it to the unrelated Tea-party targeting scandal, the article misleads readers into believing the IRS knowingly hides mass identity theft when in fact the agency is barred by privacy law from sending an alert until it has confirmed a substantive misuse—something the IG report itself notes.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to inflame anger at both illegal immigration and the IRS by framing the agency as an accomplice to foreign criminals who “steal” Americans’ identities. By spotlighting a real but narrow bureaucratic failure—IRS silence on employment-related SSN misuse—the piece amplifies a partisan narrative that undocumented workers are not only law-breakers but active predators on U.S. citizens, while government bureaucrats allegedly shield them. The emotional language (“aid and abet,” “stunning,” “screwed up”), selective context (omitting that most victims suffer no financial harm and that ITIN holders pay billions in taxes), and linkage to the Tea-party targeting scandal all serve to mobilize anti-immigration sentiment and distrust of federal institutions ahead of policy debates or elections.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The story is based on a 2016 Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) report (Reference No. 2016-40-044) that found the IRS had identified roughly 1.1 million cases in which returns filed with ITINs showed wages paid under stolen Social-Security numbers, yet the agency had not notified the legitimate SSN holders; the report, lawmakers’ reactions, and the ITIN/employment-identity-theft mechanics are all documented in the public record, so while the article’s tone is inflammatory it accurately reflects the inspector general’s findings and the subsequent congressional criticism.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article misrepresents a routine IRS/IG statistical mismatch—mostly typographical errors, name changes, or family SSN sharing—as proof that ‘illegals’ stole a million citizens’ identities and that the IRS ‘covers it up’; it omits the IG’s own caveat that most flagged returns are not confirmed theft and that privacy law blocks premature taxpayer notices, thus fabricating a scandal where none exists.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article takes a genuine IRS inspector-general finding about un-notified SSN mismatches and twists it into a sweeping claim that ‘illegals stole 1 million Social Security numbers’, omitting the IG’s own caveats that most cases involve data-entry errors, name changes, or duplicate filings rather than identity theft, that victims rarely suffer financial loss, and that privacy law—not IRS malice—limits premature taxpayer alerts; by suppressing this context and fusing the story with the unrelated Tea-party scandal, it manufactures a politically charged conspiracy that is not supported by the underlying report.

title: Thanks To Republicans, Obama Nominee Dies Waiting For Confirmation
subject: News
content: It s no secret that Republicans have used their obstructionist tactics to block anything and everything President Obama has tried to do   including nominees, from judicial to State Department.In a blatant attempt to hurt his ability to have a legacy, Republicans have targeted nominees, holding them hostage politically unless their demands are met. Some nominees waited hundreds of days for just a hearing, and others have waited even longer for a confirmation.And with that, one nominee, who has waited over 820 days for a confirmation, has died.The New York Times reports that Cassandra Butts, a worker in government and non profit entities, died suddenly at the age of 50 on May 24 of acute leukemia, which she did not know she had until shortly before her death. President Obama and the White House, recognizing her passion for helping others through public service, tapped her to serve as the United States ambassador to the Bahamas.Butts had worked for multiple branches of the government, including lawmakers on Capitol Hill and the White House counsel.Butts sailed through hearings in May 2014, and all seemed on track for a swift confirmation to a seemingly unimportant position, which urgently needed filling. So far, the Bahamas hasn t had a proper ambassador for 1,647 days.But, in typical Washington form, Republicans held up her nomination, not because she wasn t qualified, but because they literally hate President Obama.And it isn t fair to link all Senate Republicans to this hold up. Only two Republicans can be single handedly blamed for this: Tom Cotton and Ted Cruz.Is anyone surprised? Cruz, up in arms over the Iran nuclear deal, placed a hold on the confirmation on all State Department nominations, which of course included Butts.Cruz couldn t get his way, so naturally he unleashed a scorched earth policy on all those even remotely associated with the President.But it was Senator Tom Cotton   better known as  Tehran Tom  by progressive advocates   who proved to be a nefarious monstrosity in the whole matter. In seeking to punish the Obama Administration over a Secret Service leak of private information about a member of Congress, specifically targeted Butts and the Norwegian and Swedish ambassador nominees. After making a fool of himself, Cotton lifted the hold on the Scandinavian ambassadors. But he kept the hold on Butts.As the New York Times reports:Cotton eventually released the two other holds, but not the one on Butts. She told me that she once went to see him about it, and he explained that he knew that she was a close friend of Obama s   the two first encountered each other on a line for financial-aid forms at Harvard Law School, where they were classmates   and that blocking her was a way to inflict special pain on the presidentAnd there you have it. Because Republicans hate the President so much, they upheld a qualified, dignified, and devoted public servant from serving in a position that yields almost no political power.And now she has died, never getting the grace of a confirmation vote.That s how the Republicans have chosen to govern. They should be so proud of all their  accomplishments. Featured image via Mark Wilson/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the entire Republican caucus as collectively blocking Cassandra Butts, yet the body shows only two senators placed individual holds; it omits that such holds are procedural tools available to any senator, not proof of party-wide conspiracy, and it presents no evidence that GOP leadership or the majority endorsed the hold, thus using selective facts to mislead readers about who was responsible and why she died without a vote.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to indict Senate Republicans—especially Ted Cruz and Tom Cotton—for what the piece frames as a purely spiteful, personal blockade that denied Cassandra Butts a confirmation vote and ultimately robbed her of the chance to serve, thereby turning her death into a stark symbol of GOP obstructionism and moral bankruptcy.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately recounts events reported by reputable outlets such as The New York Times: Cassandra Butts was nominated by President Obama in 2013 to be ambassador to the Bahamas, her confirmation was held up for more than two years—mainly by holds placed by Senators Ted Cruz (over Iran-deal objections) and Tom Cotton (over an unrelated dispute)—and she died on May 24, 2016, before a vote; these facts are documented in contemporaneous news coverage and Senate records, so while the piece’s tone is partisan, its core factual claims are verifiable.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely attributes Cassandra Butts’s stalled nomination to an entire party, while only two individual senators exercised a routine procedural hold; it omits that Democrats could have forced a discharge vote or that holds are not party policy, and it implies her death was caused by Republican action, making the piece a misleading partisan fabrication rather than accurate reporting.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying facts—that Cassandra Butts was nominated, that Sen. Tom Cotton (and initially Ted Cruz) placed individual holds keeping the full Senate from voting, and that she died before confirmation—are verifiable through contemporaneous reporting (NYT, HuffPost, congressional records). The piece’s partisan framing and guilt-by-association rhetoric are misleading, but the core events are factual, so the item is not fabricated; it is a slanted account of a real episode.

By selectively spotlighting a single missile-transfer episode, framing it as a break with past practice, and pairing it with alarmist commentary from favored sources (Gorka, Hannity, anonymous “officials”), the piece casts Pyongyang’s every move as proof of irreversible belligerence and portrays U.S. diplomatic overtures as naïve. answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The report accurately reflects 2017-era U.S. intelligence disclosures that North Korea loaded anti-ship cruise missiles onto a patrol craft, a development covered contemporaneously by mainstream outlets such as Reuters, AP and Fox News; the details (Toejo Dong location, Stormpetrel-type missiles, first such deployment since 2014, coincident Tillerson remarks) match de-classified briefings given to journalists that summer, and Japan’s civil-defense drills were likewise documented by the BBC and others, so while the article’s framing is partisan it rests on verifiable facts rather than fabrication.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—U.S. intelligence observing North Korea load anti-ship cruise missiles onto a patrol boat—is corroborated by multiple mainstream and government sources; the article therefore reports a real occurrence, even though its partisan framing, emotive language and omission of broader context constitute misleading content rather than fabrication.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—U.S. intelligence observing North Korea load anti-ship cruise missiles onto a patrol boat—is verifiable and was reported by multiple reputable outlets; the article’s partisan framing, selective context and alarmist spin amount to misleading presentation rather than fabrication of the core fact, so it is real news delivered with a heavy skew, not fake news.

intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit the CIA’s claim that the destruction of the Senate torture report was accidental, using Edward Snowden’s authority to assert deliberate obfuscation. By framing the agency’s actions as intentional and part of a broader cover-up, the piece aims to reinforce skepticism toward official narratives, amplify public distrust in intelligence institutions, and validate critics who view U.S. torture programs as both criminal and systemically protected.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The story accurately summarizes public events and statements: in May 2016 the CIA acknowledged to a federal court that an electronic copy of the Senate’s 6,700-page torture report had been ‘inadvertently’ deleted and the backup disk then destroyed, while Justice Dept. lawyers had previously assured the court copies remained; Edward Snowden’s 18 May 2016 tweet mocking the claim (‘When CIA destroys something, it’s never a mistake’) is authentic and widely reported by reputable outlets including Reuters, AP and The Intercept, so the article’s facts and sourcing check out.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents a single, unverified claim that the CIA ‘lost’ or ‘destroyed’ the Senate torture report and then treats Edward Snowden’s Twitter opinion as definitive proof of intentional destruction, while offering no independent evidence that the report is actually gone or that any destruction was deliberate; by amplifying this unconfirmed narrative without corroboration, it fabricates a certainty that does not exist, fitting the definition of fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports an actual 2016 incident—CIA IG officials’ acknowledged loss of their copy of the Senate torture report—and Snowden’s authentic tweet ridiculing the “accidental” deletion. While the piece’s commentary is slanted and presents Snowden’s suspicion as fact, the underlying event and statements are verifiable, so it is not fabricated news; it is real reporting framed with opinion.

title: UPDATE ON 9/11 MEMORIAL Banned for “Triggering” College Snowflakes
subject: Government News
content: Great news! Southern Methodist University in Texas has reversed its decision to relocate an annual 9/11 memorial display made up of nearly 3,000 American flags to a less prominent part of campus after facing backlash from student groups.A huge thank you to The Young Americans for Freedom group! They had a hand in making this happen! They also were the ones who had set up the tribute honoring the victims of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on SMU s Dallas Hall Lawn every year since 2010.But in July officials informed the group to move the display to Morrison-McGinnis Park because Dallas Hall Lawn is used for classes and a variety of events, said university spokesman Kent Best.SMU officials also had adopted a policy to ensure displays didn t include  harmful or triggering  messages, but they later removed the language from the then-policy as inappropriate. By that time, though, some student groups said the new policy was an attack on free speech. I don t believe it s the responsibility of the university to shield individuals from certain ideas that they might be offended by,  said Grant Wolf, the leader of the Young Americans for Freedom group, according to Dallas News. Wolf, along with other leaders from campus groups, sent a letter to university President R. Gerald Turner to express their frustration with the policy.  People absolutely have to have a right to their own opinions, but this does not come with a right to be shielded from opposing ideas, especially in an environment dedicated to the learning, sharing and developing of new ideas,  they wrote.They decried the relocation of the memorial. Moving the 9/11 memorial to an out of the way park is almost the same as not allowing it, said Heather Hall, president of the university s Turning Point USA chapter.  That s not free speech,  Hall said.  That s not American. That s definitely not what SMU stands for.   Read more:  Daily MailOUR PREVIOUS REPORT ON THIS BAN: The shocker about this is that students on both sides of the political spectrum want the 9/11 flags to be displayed where they ve always been displayed. The inability of college campuses to stand up to people who are perpetually offended is a sad statement on where we are in American tolerance these days. It s so ironic that the left wants you to march to their drum beat or else they will destroy you. Note to SMU: You had a good thing going with your student body coming together to memorialize 9/11 so let it continue!DALLAS, Tex.   In a time of extreme political divide, students both Republican and Democrat at one Texas college have found something they can agree on.For the past two years at Southern Methodist University, a campus group has planted thousands of American flags in front of Dallas Hall as a memorial to the victims of the 9/11 attacks. That s simply contradictory to the very definition of free speech,  said Grant Wolf, the Young Americans for Freedom Chairman.But in July, SMU changed its policy, saying student groups can no longer have displays there.The lawn has historically hosted tributes and protests from students of all political affiliations. The leaders of two prominent student groups say the policy violates their right to free speech. They re basically cornering us into a segment of campus and saying you re not allowed to have a display here because it s triggering, harmful or offensive to students over there,  said Drew Wicker, the President of SMU College Republicans.SMU released a statement saying nearby Momac Park, where displays will be allowed, is larger than the lawn and is along one of the most prominent drives on campus.The university said it  respects the rights of all campus community members to express their opinions, as well as their right to be free from coercion or harassment. Via: Fox 5 Atlanta
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline and narrative frame the university’s routine space-management decision as a ‘ban’ triggered by ‘snowflakes’ who find the 9/11 memorial ‘offensive,’ but the body copy shows the relocation was justified by scheduling conflicts, the ‘triggering’ language was quickly retracted, and students across the spectrum still support the display; the story thus misleads readers by casting an administrative logistics issue as ideological censorship driven by hypersensitive students.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame the university’s short-lived relocation of the 9/11 flag memorial as the latest skirmish in a culture-war narrative in which “snowflake” students and timid administrators allegedly censor patriotic speech; by celebrating the reversal as a victory for “free speech” and praising the Young Americans for Freedom, the piece seeks to energize conservative readers, vilify campus progressives, and portray SMU’s initial policy not as a routine space-management decision but as ideological capitulation to the offended left.

title: Chuck Schumer Has A BRILLIANT Response To Trump Calling Him A ‘Clown’
subject: News
content: Donald Trump is set to take office as President of the United States in just 15 days, and one would think he d be making the final appointments to his cabinet and trying to make sure he is prepared to work for the American people on day one. However, this is Trump we re talking about here, so of course he isn t. What is he doing instead? Why, he s busy calling Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) a  clown.  Well, Schumer is clearly a lot smarter than Trump, and in the wake of the president-elect tweeting insults at him, Schumer decided to hit back in a much classier way.The newly elected Minority Leader was speaking with the press (something Trump has refused to do since July) regarding the GOP s ill-advised and partisan plan to immediately repeal the Affordable Care Act, otherwise known as Obamacare, with nothing to replace it, when he addressed Trump s insults. Schumer said: I d say to president-elect that this is serious, serious stuff. People s health is at stake, people s lives are at stake. Now, we understand that President-elect Trump is in a difficult spot, that Republicans are in a difficult spot. They want to repeal the ACA, and they have no idea how to replace it. As for the insults, Schumer continued: Instead of calling names, [the] president-elect should roll up his sleeves and show us a replacement plan that will cover the 20 million Americans who gained coverage, that will cover students or post-college students, 21 to 26, who want to stay on their parents plan, that will show how we cover people with pre-existing conditions. So I d say to the president-elect and the Republicans that this is not a time for calling names. It s time for them to step up if they want to repeal, and show us what they replace it with. Indeed. The GOP clearly has no plan to replace Obamacare, though they ve had six years to come up with one. Instead, the incoming president-elect continues to spend his transition time insulting lawmakers, private citizens, and intelligence community instead of doing his damn job.Good luck, Congress. You ve gotta work with a nutcase now. Hope you have a mental ward somewhere up there on Capitol Hill. You ll be needing it with this guy.Featured image via Aaron P. Bernstein via Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the dispute as a purely one-sided exchange in which Trump gratuitously insults Schumer, while Schumer’s retort is painted as a noble, policy-focused rebuttal. In reality, both men have traded barbs for months, and Schumer’s own recent speeches have included personal digs at Trump. By omitting that context and presenting only Trump’s ‘clown’ tweet, the piece misleads readers into viewing Schumer as uniquely high-minded and Trump as singularly juvenile, thereby distorting the nature of the political back-and-forth.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding aim is to delegitimize and ridicule Donald Trump before he even takes office, using Schumer’s measured reply as a foil to paint Trump as an immature, policy-empty “nutcase” who is already failing the presidency. By amplifying Schumer’s call for a serious ACA replacement, the piece portrays Republicans as reckless and plan-less, while simultaneously rallying liberal readers around the idea that only Democrats are acting responsibly. In short, the text is a partisan morale-boost that weaponizes Trump’s own insult to cast him—and by extension the entire GOP—as unfit to govern.

title: Jamelle Bouie Says Science Proves Half Of GOP Are Deplorable (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: The right-wing was quick to claim that Clinton had experienced her own  47% moment  with her  basket full of deplorables  remark. But nothing could be further from the truth. Clinton s remark turns out to be fairly accurate.In fact, if anything Clinton actually undersold just how deplorable Trump s supporters actually are. During an appearance on CBS s Face the Nation on Sunday, Slate s chief political correspondent, Jamelle Bouie explained how the statement Clinton made is supported by scientific evidence.Bouie looked at polling data that showed that more than half of Republicans believe that President is a Muslim or was born in another country. So, I m inclined to see it as strategy and not so much as a gaffe because when I heard the remark, my first question was: Well, is this true? Right? Regardless of how it sounds, what it looks like, what is the case about Donald Trump supporters?  Bouie asks.  And if you break down the numbers and you look at the RealClearPolitics average, and it gives Trump, 43 percent of the registered voters, there re about 30, 31 million people. Compare that to polls show 65 to 70 percent of all Republicans who say that Barack Obama either wasn t born in the United States or is a Muslim. If one doesn t think that believe that birtherism is a bad enough belief to hold to earn the title of deplorable, then Bouie has the data to show that roughly have of Republicans are racist. You look at pilot data from the American National Election Study, and it shows upward of 40 percent of Republicans saying things like blacks are more violent, blacks are lazier, Muslims are more violent, Muslims are lazier,  Bouie points out. Among Trump supporters in particular, 60, 50, 70 percent of them agree with statements that political scientists categorize as being explicitly racist,  Bouie continues.  So I m looking at Clinton s statement, and half, which is about 31 million people again, doesn t really seem that out of bounds. Forty to 50 percent of Republicans, I would say looking at the full spectrum of data, agree with beliefs that we would categorize as explicitly prejudiced. So regardless of whether or not Clinton needs to walk it back or not, I think she s being correct and accurate. Conservatives are angry at Clinton because they still cannot accept that pointing out bigotry and racism do not make the person bringing it up racist. Clinton may have half-heartedly backtracked on her statement; her sentiment was worded poorly even if it was accurate.As Bakari Sellers pointed out on Sunday While on CNN s State of the Union, it doesn t matter how many of Trump s supporters are bigoted racists or not because they are all supporting a candidate who is a bigot.There is no left-wing conspiracy out there to make Republicans and trump supporters like deplorable. As polling indicates, they self-identify as being racist bigots on their own.You can watch the clip below.Featured image from video screenshot
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively presents polling data and expert commentary to frame half of GOP voters as explicitly racist, omitting caveats about survey wording, sample sizes, or alternative interpretations, thereby using legitimate-looking sources to create an exaggerated, one-sided characterization that misleads readers about the prevalence and nature of prejudice among Trump supporters.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to vindicate Hillary Clinton’s “basket of deplorables” comment by marshaling poll data and expert sound-bites to argue that a large share of Trump supporters are objectively racist, thereby framing Republican outrage as denial of empirical fact rather than legitimate grievance.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports Jamelle Bouie’s televised remarks and correctly cites publicly available polling data (e.g., RealClearPolitics averages, ANES pilot items) that show large fractions of Republicans endorse birtherism or express explicitly racist attitudes; while the piece’s own commentary is partisan, it does not fabricate quotes, invent data, or misattribute sources, so the core factual claims about what Bouie said and what the polls show are verifiable and therefore the item is real news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a hyper-partisan blog post that twists selective poll crosstabs into the categorical claim that “science proves half of GOP are deplorable/racist,” omitting margin-of-error, question-wording effects, and the difference between agreeing with a stereotype in a phone survey and being an avowed racist; it presents no peer-reviewed study, conflates birtherism and policy attitudes with immutable racism, and uses loaded paraphrase (“self-identify as racist bigots”) that appears nowhere in the cited polls, making the central assertion false and intentionally misleading.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is a real opinion column that accurately reports Jamelle Bouie’s televised remarks and the polls he cites; it is not fabricated news. Its ‘misleading’ quality comes from selective emphasis and interpretive spin within those real facts, not from invention, so it remains genuine reportage of an opinion rather than fake news.

title: CRAZY! U.S. Will Pay To Import Mentally Ill Illegal Aliens Who Were Previously Deported
subject: Government News
content: Get this, previously deported mentally ill illegal aliens are being sent back to the U.S. thanks to a judge s decision: Federal Judge Dolly M. Gee s ruling will let immigrants with serious mental disabilities request to have their cases reopened in hopes of returning to the U.S. The ruling covers immigrants deported from California, Arizona and Washington between Nov. 21, 2011 and Jan. 27 this year. So it s not enough that we have the invasion of Central Americans and now Muslim refugees now the mentally ill get another shot at coming here too! What kind of insanity (no pun intended) is this?Is it any surprise that the ACLU brought this case? Doesn t the ACLU have an obligation to look out for LEGAL and law abiding Americans first? The government identified 900 immigrants who could benefit from the ruling, though there could be more and it s unclear how many would qualify to have their cases reopened, Iguina said.Now dig deep for this little tid bit of info: Under the agreement, the federal government said it will help those with reopened cases return to the U.S. and pay for some transportation costs. Doesn t this just make you want to stop paying taxes altogether? Why should we pay for these people to come back over our border when they broke the law the first time?
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The post cherry-picks and distorts a 2016 settlement (Franco-Gonzalez v. Holder) that merely allows certain deportees with serious mental disabilities to seek re-opening of their cases if they were denied due-process protections; it reframes this narrow procedural remedy as a blanket invitation for the U.S. to ‘pay to import’ mentally ill unauthorized immigrants, inflates numbers, omits eligibility safeguards, and uses emotionally loaded language (“invasion,” “insanity”) to mislead readers about both the ruling’s scope and fiscal impact.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to inflame anti-immigrant resentment by framing a narrow, court-ordered remedy for a vulnerable subset of deportees—people with serious mental illnesses who were denied fair hearings—as a sweeping, taxpayer-funded “invasion” of dangerous “illegals.” By cherry-picking facts, mocking the disabled, and vilifying the ACLU, the piece weaponizes outrage to reinforce the narrative that the U.S. government prioritizes foreigners over citizens, encouraging readers to view tax compliance and immigration due-process itself as betrayal.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: A federal judge (Dolly M. Gee) did issue a 2016 class-action order requiring the U.S. government to notify and allow certain previously removed non-citizens with qualifying mental disabilities to reopen their immigration cases; the government also agreed to facilitate their return and cover limited transportation costs, so the core facts reported are accurate, even though the article’s inflammatory framing is opinion, not fabrication.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The post fabricates a narrative by misrepresenting a limited 2016 court settlement that only lets a small group of deportees with documented mental disabilities ask to reopen prior removal cases if they were denied basic due-process protections; it falsely claims the U.S. is paying to ‘import’ masses of mentally ill illegal aliens, inflates numbers, omits strict eligibility filters, and uses inflammatory language to create a non-existent policy, making the core claim demonstrably false.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The post grossly misrepresents a 2016 consent decree that simply lets a small, defined group of deportees with documented mental disabilities ask immigration courts to reopen cases in which they were denied basic due-process protections; it invents the claim that the U.S. is recruiting or funding a mass influx of mentally ill migrants, inflates numbers, and omits the stringent eligibility and case-by-case review required, turning a narrow procedural safeguard into a fabricated taxpayer-funded program.

title: Syria Ceasefire Deal: A Cynical Ploy by Washington’s ‘Coalition’ to Buy Time for Terrorists
subject: US_News
content: 21st Century Wire says This latest diplomatic development certainly appears positive on its surface, this week s declared  Syrian Ceasefire    a three-way agreement between Washington, Russia and the Syrian government (and begrudgingly by the West s other regional  stakeholders ) looks increasingly like it may just be the latest attempt to buy time   so that Washington, Turkey and Saudi Arabia can re-arm and replenish various militant fighting groups currently laying waste to Syria.Since the entrance of the Russian Air Force into the Syrian conflict theatre last October, the Washington-led Axis has gradually lost proxy-control of a number of key terrorist strongholds in Northern Syria, namely in Aleppo, and thus are unable to dictate crucial  facts on the ground  required to dictate the international media and political narratives. Unable to craft and package these narratives, the West and its dubious  coalition  are completely unable to sell an escalation of military violence in Syria.The fact that the Washington Axis has already threatened to move to a  Plan B    even before the agreement has been implemented, indicates that this diplomatic effort may in fact be  dead on arrival . Before the ink was even dry on the agreement, sources inside the CIA and the Pentagon went public with a preemptive statement claiming that,  Russia cannot be trusted to uphold the ceasefire . The scene is now set.Watch as 21WIRE founder and editor Patrick Henningsen speaks to Sean Thomas from RT International about why the ceasefire deal may not survive the spring . Patrick Henningsen talks Syria Ceasefire with RT International (2016) from 21wire on Vimeo.READ MORE SYRIA NEWS AT: 21st Century Wire Syria Files
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the U.S.-Russia-brokered Syrian ceasefire as a deliberate Western ruse to re-arm terrorists, selectively citing unnamed sources and speculative ‘Plan B’ threats while omitting evidence that the agreement includes mutual cessation clauses, monitoring mechanisms, and humanitarian-access provisions; by presenting only hostile interpretations and portraying all opposition fighters as uniformly terrorist, it misleads readers about the ceasefire’s actual terms and the multi-sided nature of the conflict.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize the U.S.-brokered Syrian ceasefire by framing it as a deliberate stalling tactic that Washington, Turkey and Saudi Arabia are using to re-arm anti-Assad “terrorists,” thereby casting the Western coalition as duplicitous actors who exploit diplomacy only to regain lost battlefield leverage and narrative control.

disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively quotes Comey’s testimony and Herridge’s report, inflating an ambiguous reference to a single hacked email into a sweeping claim that Lynch ‘would do EVERYTHING she could to protect Hillary,’ omitting that Comey never verified the email’s authenticity, sender, recipient, or evidentiary weight, thereby framing Lynch as definitively corrupt when the actual evidence was unsubstantiated and peripheral.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize the Obama-era Justice Department and Hillary Clinton by framing a single, unverified email—allegedly seen by Comey—as proof of a high-level conspiracy to shield Clinton from prosecution. By amplifying speculative links between Lynch, Obama, and Clinton, the piece seeks to energize an anti-establishment audience, cast doubt on the integrity of the 2016 investigation, and retroactively justify Comey’s controversial decisions as heroic resistance against entrenched corruption.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: No credible contemporaneous record exists of FBI Director James Comey testifying that Russian-hacked emails showed then-Attorney-General Loretta Lynch promised to “protect Hillary from prosecution.” The claim originated on hyper-partisan blogs that misrepresented Comey’s 2017 Senate testimony; Comey actually said only that a hacked Democratic email contained political chatter about Lynch, not any assurance of non-prosecution, and he never characterized it as evidence of Lynch obstructing the Clinton email investigation. Major outlets and the hearing transcript contain no such bombshell admission, making the story a distortion amplified for political effect.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article converts an unverified, unsourced Russian-hacked email into a categorical declaration that Loretta Lynch vowed to shield Clinton, a leap Comey himself never endorsed; by omitting that Comey stressed the email’s unknown provenance and lack of confirmation, the piece fabricates a proven conspiracy where none was established, meeting the definition of fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article transforms a single, unverified Russian-hacked email—whose content, sender, recipient and authenticity Comey never confirmed—into a categorical assertion that Lynch vowed to “do EVERYTHING” to protect Clinton, a claim neither Comey nor any official investigation ever substantiated; by omitting these crucial qualifiers and layering partisan speculation, the piece fabricates evidence of a DOJ conspiracy, meeting the definition of fake news.
