title: More Fake News: Mainstream Media Lies About Trump ‘Evicting’ White House Press Corp
subject: US_News
content: 21st Century Wire says Many mainstream news outlets have been abuzz about the headline going around saying that Trump may  evict  the press corp from accessing the White House, but when one looks deeper into what is being written in such articles it quickly becomes clear that there is nothing official stated about disallowing any press from the White House.Here s the facts: Incoming White House Press Secretary, Sean Spicer, while discussing potentially moving the press corps room from the James Brady Press Room, to the White House Conference Room   in order to add more seating for press to cover President Trump in the White House said: If the plan goes through, one of the officials said, the media will be removed from the cozy confines of the White House press room, where it has worked for several decades. Members of the press will be relocated to the White House Conference Center near Lafayette Square or to a space in the Old Executive Office Building, next door to the White House.Look to the Blaze for how this is spun into a narrative which serves the dual purpose of agitating Trump s detractors into believing that he is going to suppress the freedom of the press and at the same time serves as a rouse to cause his ardent supporters to appear as though they are rejoicing at the potential of a Trump Presidency that would support suppressing the free press. When comparing the actual quotes with the editorial it is obvious that The Blaze and other mainstream media outlets are playing a wicked game of deceit to further the attempts at demonizing the incoming President.We can now see who the real  Fake News  culprits are.Below is one of the fake news articles circulating online   this one was floated out by Glenn Beck and his dubious media organization The Blaze . The BlazePresident-elect Donald Trump s transition team is reportedly considering plans to evict the White House press corps from accessing the White House.According to a report from Esquire, which cited three sources with the transition team, Trump administration officials are  seriously considering  plans to evict the press corps from being able to access the White House, arguing that it would allow the press increased access to Trump. There has been no decision,  incoming White House press secretary Sean Spicer told Esquire, adding that  there has been some discussion about how to do it. More from Esquire:If the plan goes through, one of the officials said, the media will be removed from the cozy confines of the White House press room, where it has worked for several decades. Members of the press will be relocated to the White House Conference Center near Lafayette Square or to a space in the Old Executive Office Building, next door to the White House.Spicer, in his comments to Esquire, suggested that one of the reasons the administration is looking to evict the press from the White House is because they want to offer more members of the press the ability to cover Trump and the White House.Currently, there are only 49 seats in the White House James Brady Press Briefing Room, not enough to honor the hundreds, and sometimes, thousands of requests from journalists to cover Trump, Spicer said.However, a different, unnamed source told Esquire that the administration might have a different motive. According to the source, the administration is considering the move because of how the media covered Trump during the campaign and after his election victory.Trump has repeatedly lambasted the media for their coverage of him, regularly taking to Twitter to blast a news agency or a reporter by name. Most recently, Trump scolded CNN s Jim Acosta during his press conference See the rest of Glenn Beck s Fake News story at The BlazeREAD MORE ELECTIONS NEWS AT: 21st Century Wire 2016 Files
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article reframes a routine logistical proposal (moving the press briefing room to a larger space) as proof that mainstream outlets are fabricating a ‘press eviction’ narrative, omitting that those same outlets quoted Spicer verbatim and noted the plan was only under discussion; by selectively highlighting the word ‘evict’ used in headlines and ignoring the articles’ explicit statements that no final decision had been made, it misleads readers into believing the legacy media invented a suppression story rather than accurately reporting an unsettled, controversial idea.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize mainstream media by reframing a legitimate news report as deliberate “fake news,” thereby defending the incoming Trump administration from criticism. By selectively quoting Sean Spicer and accusing outlets like The Blaze of maliciously spinning a routine logistical consideration into a press-freedom scare, the piece seeks to invert the “fake news” label—turning it back on the mainstream press and casting Trump’s team as the victim, not the aggressor, in a supposed media war.

title: POLICE IN GERMANY BEGIN RAIDS On Homes Of Facebook Users Who Post “Hate Speech” Against Refugees
subject: left-news
content: If Facebook has aligned themselves with Germany to restrict the free speech of its users, what makes us so sure they won t do the same thing in the US with Obama or (God forbid) a Hillary presidency? And wouldn t Germany be better off focusing their policing efforts on the over 1 million freeloaders and terrorists they ve just admitted into Germanista?Police in Germany have started carrying out raids in peoples homes in an attempt to prosecute people for inciting  hate speech  on Facebook.A press release from Germany s federal police agency confirmed that around 60 homes were searched this week as a result of people posting messages deemed as extreme by the German authorities. The action carried out today shows that the authorities are acting firmly against hate on the internet, which has grown considerably in the wake of the refugee situation,  said Holger M nch, head of the BKA, said in the statement. Attacks on refugees are often the result of radicalization, which begins on social networks. These words should not poison the social climate,  he continued.The move comes after it was revealed in January that Mark Zuckerberg had teamed up with German Chancellor Angela Merkel in order to censor people s frustrations with her migrant policy, when she decided to open up Germany s borders to millions of migrants last year.Facebook consequently introduced a policy where they agreed to remove anything deemed as  hate speech  within 24 hours.  Bretibart News
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames Germany’s enforcement of existing hate-speech laws as unprecedented censorship, omitting that such laws have been on the books since the post-WWII era and that police raids for online incitement are routine, not new. It selectively quotes officials and conflates legal action against incitement with suppression of legitimate criticism of refugee policy, while using loaded terms like ‘freeloaders and terrorists’ to emotionally bias readers against migrants and imply the state is prioritizing speech over security, thereby distorting the actual legal and social context.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to provoke fear and outrage among U.S. conservatives by portraying Germany’s enforcement of hate-speech laws as an Orwellian crack-down on ordinary citizens’ legitimate criticism of refugees, then warning that Facebook’s cooperation with Merkel is a template for similar censorship in the United States under a Democratic president. By labeling refugees as “freeloaders and terrorists,” equating content moderation with government persecution, and invoking Obama/Hillary as looming censors, the piece aims to delegitimize both immigration and platform regulation as existential threats to American free speech.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The raids did occur—German police searched about 60 homes in 2016 for alleged online hate speech under existing German law, a fact reported by multiple mainstream outlets including Deutsche Welle, Reuters and the BBC. The text’s partisan framing and loaded language (“freeloaders,” “Germanista,” speculation about U.S. censorship) are opinionated, but the core event it describes is documented and accurate, so the item itself is not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not a factual news report but a deliberately slanted opinion item: it omits that Germany’s hate-speech statutes date to the post-war criminal code, presents routine law-enforcement searches as novel “raids on homes,” inflates numbers, uses loaded epithets like “freeloaders and terrorists,” and insinuates a Zuckerberg-Merkel conspiracy without evidence, all to mislead readers into believing unprecedented censorship is occurring.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is not fabricated in the sense that German police did carry out raids under existing hate-speech laws, but it is fake news because it deliberately misrepresents those facts: it omits that such laws date to the post-Nazi era, presents routine enforcement as novel censorship, uses loaded slurs (“freeloaders and terrorists”) to demonize refugees, and falsely insinuates that Facebook and U.S. Democrats are poised to replicate this “Orwellian” crackdown, thereby creating a distorted, fear-mongering narrative rather than reporting reality.

title: NH Car Dealer Gives Away Free AR-15s With Car Purchases – Gun Nuts Sickeningly Rejoice
subject: News
content: Mike Hagan has a used car dealership and repair shop in Rochester, New Hampshire and is running a very odd and frankly irresponsible promotion. He s offering a free AR-15 to people who come buy a car from him, because  Murika.Hagan is a combat veteran who served in Afghanistan. He knows what these kinds of guns can do, and yet, according to WFTV 9, he s not worried about whether any of these guns might be used to murder people later on. Thus far, he s given away four of the weapons, along with a 9mm Beretta, which is an alternative for people who don t want an AR-15, and he thinks his promotion is a wild success.This kind of promotion is bad enough, and to refuse to end it following a horrific tragedy like Orlando is just plain insensitive and cruel. The gun nuts apparently don t see it that way, though. They ve taken to Facebook to celebrate Hagan s promotion, lest the  evil libruls  finally come to confiscate everyone s guns.              There has been some backlash, though, not just on social media, but also from a couple of people that NH1 TV spoke to. At least there are least still some sane people out there: To me that s just getting more of the nut jobs out there doing harm to more people that don t deserve it. My opinion, military and police are the only ones that should have them. Hagan has partnered with a local gun dealer to run his promotion, and customers have to go there to go through a background check and get the weapons. Apparently, that makes it all okay because it means he knows he can t give them out like they re candy.Besides that, he believes that the people who take advantage of this promotion will be fully responsible, because everyone knows that all the people who obtain their guns legally are very responsible gun owners   oh wait. Omar Mateen, and so many other mass shooters, bought their guns legally, not to mention all the idiots who have no clue what gun safety is, and end up accidentally shooting someone to death.Hagan claims he won t extend the offer to someone from whom he gets a bad feeling. So, what, he s telepathic and knows who has bad intentions? Horse hockey. This is still sick, it s still irresponsible, and it s still cruel and insensitive. It also demonstrates just how sick as a society we ve become where this kind of thing is seen as something to celebrate by so many.Featured image via screen capture from NH1-TV report
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks facts (the dealer is a vet, buyers must pass a federal background check at a separate FFL, only four guns have been given away) but frames them with emotionally loaded language (‘sickeningly rejoice,’ ‘gun nuts,’ ‘irresponsible,’ ‘cruel’) to imply the promotion is inherently dangerous and celebratory of mass violence, while omitting that the process follows existing law and no incidents have occurred, thus misleading readers about the actual risk and intent.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to provoke moral outrage and galvanize gun-control supporters by framing the dealer’s promotion as a symbol of America’s “sickness,” belittling both the business owner and gun owners as “gun nuts,” and using the Orlando tragedy as emotional leverage to shame anyone who does not condemn the giveaway.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: Multiple local and national outlets (NH1-TV, WFTV-9, Boston.com, etc.) have independently reported that Rochester, NH used-car dealer Mike Hagan is running a promotion giving customers a voucher for a free AR-15 (or 9 mm pistol) after buying a vehicle; the dealer confirms he partners with a licensed firearms retailer who completes the required federal background check before transferring the gun. The story is therefore factual, not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—a New Hampshire car dealer giving vouchers for free AR-15s or 9mm pistols to customers who pass a federally required background check at a licensed firearms dealer—is factual and has been reported by multiple local outlets; the article is therefore not fabricated. However, it is heavily editorialized, using inflammatory language and selective emphasis to portray the promotion as uniquely dangerous and socially irresponsible while downplaying that all transfers comply with existing law, which classifies it as misleading opinion rather than fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—a New Hampshire car dealer giving away AR-15s to customers who pass standard federal background checks—is factual and verifiable through local news outlets; the article’s heavy bias and emotionally charged language do not fabricate the promotion itself, so it remains real news presented with a strong opinion rather than falsehood.

title: Veteran’s Letter Thanking Bernie Sanders For Voting Against Iraq War Goes Viral (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: A U.S. Marine s letter to Bernie Sanders that expressed the utmost gratitude for the Senator s position on not sending U.S. troops to Iraq has recently gone viral, and it s easy to see why.The letter surfaced on Tuesday morning, when Reddit user CharlieDarwinsFather created a post titled An open letter to Bernie Sanders from a Veteran of the Iraq War  in the subreddit SandersforPresident, where many of Sanders  supporters gather to share news about the Democratic presidential candidate. The letter s author had been based in North Carolina and had served in combat during the second battle of Fallujah in Iraq during 2005, 2006 and 2007.Having lived through those battles as a young adult and seeing the short and long-term effects that war had on his fellow marines, the author thanked the Vermont Senator with great sincerity for opposing the Iraq War, and said he wished that America had more politicians like Sanders who weren t afraid to fight for real peace. In his letter, the U.S. Marine wrote: Senator Sanders,I want to thank you. I want to thank you for exercising sound judgement even when everyone around you was beating the war drums.See I fought in the streets of Fallujah, Iraq. I saw more blood and death than any 19 year old ever should. The amount of friends I ve lost to war will likely be surpassed by the amount of friends I ve since lost to suicide.I know first hand the moral cost of war. One of the most painful truths that I must go through life with is that I fought in an unjust and unfounded war. While my intentions were good and I fought hard for the men to my left and to my right, and while I thought what I was doing what was right for the people of Iraq- I was wrong.You knew this. You knew this before we went to war and you fought, and you spoke truth to your peers and though your words largely fell on deaf ears, I am truly heartened to know that I now have a chance to vote for a man who exercised sound and moral judgement when the war drums were beating the loudest.I have a son. He is only one and a half years old but someday he will be 18 and I fear that if we continue to elect the same establishment politicians, he too will face the same decision that I did, and he too will go off to fight in an endless quagmire and that he too will come home, broken, and never fully returned or worse- never come home at all.So thank you, Senator Sanders, for being of sound mind and judgement. Thank you for being the only voice in this race that does not want to continue this legacy of warfare. Thank you for being the only voice that is and has been standing up for those of us that fought in these misguided wars. Thank you for giving me hope for a peaceful future. Sincerely, A U.S. Marine   0311 Operation Iraqi FreedomThe letter has gone viral, and it s easy to see why as Sanders  anti-establishment approach continues to win over Americans across the country. Now more than ever, we re becoming more aware of the affects that war has on our veterans, and just how common homelessness, suicide and mental illnesses like PTSD are.This letter is especially noteworthy because Sanders recently pointed out   during Monday s Democratic Town Hall on CNN   that presidential candidate Hillary Clinton had supported the war while Sanders rallied against sending troops to Iraq because he was afraid it would create more power for extremists (which he was right about).Sanders has been passionate about preserving peace for a long time   as this video of Sanders giving a passionate speech in 2002 reveals:Sanders, who is the former Chairman and a current member of the Senate Veterans  Affairs Committee, continues to fight for America s veterans and has made it a crucial part of his campaign. This mission is spelled out right on Sanders  website: Sen. Sanders believes that just as planes and tanks and guns are a cost of war, so is taking care of the men and women who we sent off to fight the war. It includes caring for the spouses and children who have to rebuild their lives after the loss of a loved one. It includes caring for the hundreds of thousands of veterans with multiple amputations or loss of eyesight, post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injury. It includes veterans who are having difficulty keeping jobs in order to pay their bills, and it includes the terrible tragedy of veterans committing suicide. And regardless of whether or not you think America should go to war, it s impossible to argue with Sanders when he says: While serious people can have legitimate differences about when our country should go to war, there should never be a debate whether we fulfill the promises made to the men and women who served this country in the military. As a nation, we have a moral obligation to provide the best quality care to those who have put their lives on the line to defend us. Featured image via Fort Rucker / Flickr
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a straightforward news report that accurately describes a real letter written by a U.S. Marine, posted on Reddit, and the subsequent viral reaction; it provides verifiable context (Sanders’s 2002 anti-war speech, his Veterans Affairs record, the CNN town-hall contrast with Clinton) without distorting facts, using misleading frames, or fabricating content, so it does not fit any information-disorder category.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to amplify an emotionally resonant, first-hand indictment of the Iraq War in order to validate Bernie Sanders’s long-standing anti-war stance and, by extension, his 2016 presidential candidacy. By foregrounding a combat veteran’s letter that frames Sanders as the lone voice of “sound and moral judgement,” the piece converts personal trauma into political capital, portraying a vote for Sanders as a moral corrective to bipartisan war-making and a safeguard against future “endless quagmires.”
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The story accurately reports the existence, content, and viral spread of a 2016 open letter from a U.S. Marine to Bernie Sanders thanking him for opposing the 2003 Iraq War; the letter was originally posted on Reddit’s r/SandersForPresident, widely shared across social media, and subsequently covered by multiple reputable outlets, with Sanders’s long-standing anti-war stance and veterans’ advocacy well documented in public records and C-SPAN footage.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports the existence and content of a letter from a U.S. Marine that went viral on Reddit, corroborates Sanders’s documented 2002 anti-Iraq-war stance and his Veterans Affairs committee work, and presents verifiable facts without fabrication or distortion, aligning with the preliminary Normal disorder assessment.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports the existence and content of a genuine letter from a U.S. Marine that was publicly posted on Reddit, cites verifiable facts about Sanders’s 2002 anti-war speech and Senate record, and frames the viral reaction without fabricating evidence or distorting events, so it constitutes real news.

title: BLACK LIVES MATTER TERRORISTS May Be Shut Down: Mall Of America Files Restraining Order
subject: politics
content: ter ror ist  ter r st/ noun a person who uses terrorism in the pursuit of political aims. synonyms: extremist, fanatic; revolutionary, radical, insurgent, guerrilla, anarchist, freedom fighter; bomber, gunman, assassin, hijacker, arsonist, incendiaryThe Mall of America has requested a temporary restraining order against Black Lives Matter leaders in the hopes of heading off a protest intended to shut down the shopping center during the busiest shopping day of the Christmas season.From KARE11.com: MINNEAPOLIS   The Mall of America has filed for a restraining order against leaders of Black Lives Matter (BLM) in an attempt to head off a protest scheduled for one of the busiest shopping days of the year.The legal documents, filed in Hennepin County Court, name BLM leaders Michael McDowell, Miski Noor, Lena Gardner, Kandace Montgomery and four others named only as John Does 1 through 4 as defendants. The request for the temporary restraining order says BLM has been using its Facebook and Twitter pages to promote a demonstration at the Mall of America s East Rotunda at 1 p.m. on December 23, 2015.In asking for a restraining order, attorneys for MOA point to a similar protest held on December 20, 2014 involving approximately 1,000 protesters inside the mall. A number of the demonstrators were arrested and charged with trespassing. The legal action maintains that MOA and its tenants suffered irreparable harm, including reduced guests and sales. The mall says traffic counts for the number of cars entering parking ramps on that day were down 15 percent from statistics from the previous five years, which translates into 24,000 fewer shoppers. Mall attorneys maintain that many retailers reported double digit decreases in sales on December 20,2014, the date of that demonstration. Via: Breitbart News
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline labels the civil-rights group Black Lives Matter as ‘TERRORISTS,’ a legally and factually unsupported slur that delegitimizes protected protest activity and incites hostility against participants on the basis of their political identity and race, meeting the definition of bias-motivated, hostile expression.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize the Black Lives Matter movement by framing its activists as “terrorists” and law-breakers whose protests inflict economic harm, thereby rallying readers against BLM and legitimizing preemptive legal suppression of their dissent.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: Multiple reputable local outlets such as KARE11 reported in December 2015 that Mall of America filed for a temporary restraining order against named Black Lives Matter organizers to block a planned 23 December protest, citing the 2014 demonstration’s alleged impact on traffic and sales; the filing itself is a verifiable public court record, so while the Breitbart article’s headline rhetoric is slanted, the core event described actually happened.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The headline’s unsubstantiated branding of Black Lives Matter as “TERRORISTS” is a demonstrably false, inflammatory label that misrepresents lawful protest as terrorism; the body merely reports a 2015 restraining-order filing, but the extremist framing and omission of context convert the piece into deceptive propaganda rather than factual news, satisfying standard definitions of fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not a straight news report but a politically-motivated opinion item that deliberately mislabels a civil-rights protest group as “terrorists,” a term with a specific legal meaning that does not apply to the described demonstrations, and it omits key context (e.g., the protest’s stated purpose, police response, court rulings on prior MOA protests) while relying on a partisan source, thereby distorting facts to incite hostility rather than inform, which places it outside factual journalism and into disinformation.

title: WIFE OF JOHN CONYERS CONFRONTS MEDIA At Her House: ‘Do you go and stalk white people’s houses?’ [Video]
subject: politics
content: If you live in Michigan, you know about the controversial wife of Congressman John Conyers. She s had her share of scandals and has even served 3 years in Federal prison for bribery. But this IS Detroit so anything goes Watch the video below and you ll see her in action pulling the race card Monica Conyers wasn t in a talkative mood Wednesday morning as the media camped outside her house looking for her embattled husband, U.S. Rep. John Conyers, D-Detroit.  John Conyers has come under fire because of sexual harassment allegations made against him and how they were handled by his office.The Detroit Free Press reports:As she was leaving the family s house Wednesday morning, Monica Conyers said:  I ll make a comment when you all disclose to me who has made the allegations.  Monica Conyers became irritated with the media attention then pulled the race card: Do you all go and stalk other people s houses?  Monica Conyers asked the media camped outside her house. Conyers said her husband wasn t home and that she didn t know his whereabouts HERE S A GREAT EXAMPLE OF WHAT A NASTY WOMAN MONICA CONYERS IS: Watching this video will help anyone who is curious about why the city of Detroit continues to be bailed out of trouble like an irresponsible child with a trust fund. disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article repeatedly vilifies Monica Conyers with racially-loaded language (‘pulls the race card,’ ‘typical Dem race-baiting,’ ‘nasty woman,’ ‘irresponsible child’), frames Detroit’s Black electorate as inherently corrupt, and invites readers to mock and dehumanize her, constituting bias-motivated, hostile expression that targets her for her race and political identity.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize and ridicule Monica Conyers—and by extension Detroit’s Black political establishment—by weaponizing her past conviction and a single confrontational moment to reinforce a racialized narrative of corruption, entitlement, and “race-baiting.” The piece cherry-picks footage, court details, and inflammatory commentary to portray Conyers as emblematic of a failed, majority-Black city, encouraging readers to view any accusation of racial bias she raises as automatically dishonest and to dismiss broader concerns about media treatment of Black public figures.

title: MARINE CORPS GENERAL WARNS U.S. TROOPS: “There’s A War Coming”
subject: politics
content: While the mainstream media remains transfixed on a phony Trump-Russian collusion story, they completely ignore the real news, about how things appear to be heating up between Russian President Vladimir Putin and the U.S.A Marine Corps commandant on Thursday warned U.S. troops stationed in Norway to be prepared for a coming war.Neller pointed to the near future possibility of Russia and the Pacific theater being the next major areas of conflict.Sgt. Maj. Ronald Green sounded a similar tone. Just remember why you re here,  Green said.  They re watching. Just like you watch them, they watch you. We ve got 300 Marines up here; we could go from 300 to 3,000 overnight. We could raise the bar. The warnings came a day before Defense Secretary Jim Mattis told troops at Fort Bragg, N.C., that  storm clouds are gathering  over the Korean Peninsula.Whether the comments were more than motivational rhetoric remained unclear.Neller and Green s arrival in Norway coincided with heightened tensions between the U.S. and its NATO allies and Russia. According to Military.com, Russia warned Norway that its decision to host a new unit of U.S. troops through the end of 2018 would negatively affect relations. FOX NewsAccording to UK Express, Russian President Putin said the US missile defense sites in Romania containing interceptor missiles could also house ground-to-ground intermediate-range cruise missiles, which would be in violation of the 1987 Intermediate-range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty.He told the military officials that both the US and NATO have been  accelerating build-up of infrastructure in Europe  and emphasised that the deployment of NATO forces near Russia s borders had threatened its security.He said:  When we move military units on our own territory, they present it as some kind of a threat. And when they move military bases, infrastructure and new weapons near our borders they present it as something normal. It s probably normal for those who do it, but not for us. NATO has deployed military units to Poland and the Baltics to reassure allies worried over Russia s intentions following its 2014 annexation of Ukraine s Crimea and its support for pro-Russia separatists in eastern Ukraine.Mr Putin mentioned NATO s US-led missile defense system and efforts to develop new prospective conventional weapons among other security challenges.He added:  They are searching for some violations on our part while consistently infringing on it themselves. All that seriously affects security in Europe and in the whole world. Mr Putin accused the US of violating a landmark Cold War-era nuclear arms pact and harbouring aggressive intentions, and pledged to fend off any potential threats.FOX News  At a Q&A session with the troops in the Norwegian Home Guard base near Trondheim, Neller said that the U.S. could shift its focus from the Middle East to Eastern Europe, citing Russia s conflicts with Ukraine and Georgia as justification. He told the Marines that they should be prepared for a  big-ass fight  on the horizon.Russia has reportedly been uneasy about the presence of American troops close to its borders. The 300 U.S. Marines deployed to Norway in June 2016 were the first foreign troops allowed to operate in the country since World War II.In September of this year, Russia conducted a joint-military exercise with neighboring Belarus that involved 12,700 troops.A new National Security Strategy unveiled by the Trump administration on Monday singled out Russia and China as two world powers challenging  American power, influence, and interests, attempting to erode American security and prosperity. F
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks routine commanders’ motivational language (“big-ass fight,” “storm clouds”) and presents it as evidence of an imminent, officially-forecast U.S.–Russia war, while omitting the long-standing context that such rhetoric is standard for keeping deployed troops mentally ready. It amplifies Russian talking-points about U.S./NATO aggression without balancing them with allied deterrence narratives, and it layers unrelated events (Crimea, INF treaty, Korea) to create an impression of coordinated, escalating military action, thus misleading readers about the actual immediacy and certainty of conflict.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to amplify a sense of imminent, large-scale conflict with Russia (and secondarily North Korea) by selectively highlighting the most alarmist statements of U.S. military leaders, presenting them as validated forecasts rather than motivational rhetoric, while simultaneously accusing mainstream media of deliberately suppressing this “real news.” By framing routine deterrence posture and training rhetoric as proof of an approaching war, the author seeks to delegitimize legacy media, stoke fear and mistrust among readers, and reinforce a narrative that only alternative or “truth-telling” sources are exposing the supposedly hidden march toward war.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports public statements by senior U.S. Marine Corps leaders in Norway during 2017—widely covered by outlets such as Military.com, Fox News, and the UK Express—warning troops to prepare for possible future conflict with Russia and in the Pacific, and it correctly notes contemporaneous Russian objections to U.S. troop deployments and NATO exercises, so while the piece is framed with alarmist commentary, the core facts and quotations are verifiable and not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece misrepresents routine, morale-boosting warnings from Marine leaders as a concrete prediction of imminent war, omits the standard military context for such language, and weaves unrelated geopolitical events into a single, alarmist narrative, thereby fabricating an appearance of certainty and immediacy that official sources never gave.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece misrepresents routine, morale-boosting language from U.S. commanders as a secret official warning of imminent war, omits the well-documented context that such rhetoric is standard for deployed troops, and stitches together unrelated incidents (Norway rotation, INF dispute, Korea tensions) to fabricate an appearance of inevitable conflict, thereby failing the basic journalistic test of accurately conveying the significance of the events it cites.

title: Republicans PROVE They Believe In Party Over Country With One Incredibly Stupid Question
subject: News
content: Congress is chest-deep in their leak investigations, with FBI Director James Comey in the hot seat today. During the House Intelligence Committee hearing, chairman Devin Nunes thought he d try and ask some really hard-hitting questions, maybe in an attempt to trap Comey into saying something that will incriminate everyone who isn t Republican in the increasingly tangled web that is the Russia scandal.All he did was prove that this is about Republicans desperately puffing up their party instead of actually getting to the bottom of possible treason. And he did it with just one question: If this committee or anyone else for that matter, someone from the public, comes with information to you about the Hillary Clinton campaign, or their associates, or someone from the Clinton Foundation, will you add that to your investigation? Really? He s trying to make this about Hillary, despite consensus that Russia acted in the interest of Trump? It certainly sounded like that s what Nunes was doing when he followed up with: If they have ties to Russian intelligence services, Russian agents, would that be something of interest to you? Comey would not fall into Nunes  trap, though. He replied with: If people bring us information about what they think is improper, unlawful activity of any kind, we will evaluate it. Not just in this context. Folks send us stuff all the time. They should keep doing that. Nunes may well by trying to follow Trump s lead on this, as Trump regularly throws Twitter tantrums in childish attempts to deflect blame. Trump is livid   Comey s statements that the FBI is, indeed, investigating the Russian scandal are infuriating to him. As such, he s still all over Twitter trying to convince us that the real problem is the leaks, and that Hillary s a traitor and a crook and we supposedly all know it, rather than all the evidence piling up against him.What about all of the contact with the Clinton campaign and the Russians? Also, is it true that the DNC would not let the FBI in to look?  Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) March 20, 2017Is it a coincidence that Nunes would also ask about Hillary? Likely not. Nunes and the rest of the GOP should give us a call when they re ready to actually go to work.Featured image via Mark Wilson/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks a single question from Rep. Nunes, strips it of context, and presents it as proof that the entire Republican party values ‘party over country.’ By framing the query about whether the FBI would examine Clinton-Russia leads as inherently illegitimate, the piece misleads readers about the hearing’s scope (which covers Russian interference generally, not just Trump) and demonizes an opposition party without evidence of bad faith, thereby distorting the public’s understanding of a legitimate oversight exchange.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit Republican lawmakers—especially Devin Nunes and Donald Trump—by framing their focus on Hillary Clinton and leaks as a cynical, partisan deflection designed to shield their party from scrutiny in the Russia investigation. By ridiculing Nunes’s question as “incredibly stupid” and painting it as proof that Republicans prioritize party loyalty over national security, the author seeks to reinforce a narrative that the GOP is obstructing a legitimate probe into potential Trump-Russia ties while hypocritically trying to revive a debunked Clinton scandal.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately summarizes the March 20, 2017 House Intelligence Committee hearing in which Chairman Devin Nunes did ask FBI Director James Comey whether tips about the Clinton campaign or Foundation would be added to the Russia probe; Comey’s verbatim reply is correctly quoted, and Trump’s same-day tweets parroting the deflection are likewise authentic, so while the piece’s framing is partisan it reports verifiable facts without fabrication.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a polemical opinion piece that misrepresents a routine oversight question as conclusive evidence of GOP treachery, omits the bipartisan context of the Russia probe, and employs loaded language (‘incredibly stupid,’ ‘desperately puffing up’) to imply bad faith without factual substantiation, thereby constituting misleading content rather than straight news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is not fabricated, but it is fake news in the sense that it deliberately misleads: it twists a routine oversight question into conclusive proof of GOP treachery, omits the hearing’s bipartisan mandate to examine all Russian interference angles, and uses ridicule and cherry-picking to assert motive without evidence, thereby creating a false narrative that Republicans are obstructing justice by merely asking if Clinton-related leads would also be reviewed.

title: ‘Dilbert’ Creator Scott Adams Says Comparing Trump To Hitler Is Racist
subject: News
content: The man behind the lovably hapless office drone  Dilbert  has a few things to say about Donald Trump   and they are a doozy.In a post on his blog, cartoonist Scott Adams blasted people who dared to compare Donald Trump to German dictator Adolf Hitler, describing the comparison as  racist  against German people.Can we agree that calling the candidate with German ancestry Hitler  is racist? It sure feels that way to me. I m about half German, same as Trump. And it feels like a racial insult to me.I m not easily offended, but I don t see any other way to interpret the incessant Hitler analogies directed at Trump. If he were female and Asian   with exactly the same policies   would we be comparing him to Hitler every five seconds?I don t think so.There are, of course, a few things wrong with Adams  analysis:  German  isn t a race, Hitler wasn t German, comparing one person with German ancestry to an infamous tyrant isn t  racist , the list goes on..But more to the point, Donald Trump wouldn t be an Asian female, because Donald Trump s policies   at their core   appeal to white supremacists who would never consider voting for a woman of color. The kind of hate-fueled rhetoric that makes Trump soar in the Republican polls is at the expense of minorities, women, and other disadvantaged groups. You know who else used prejudice and scapegoating to fire up his supporters? Adams sure can t think of anyone!However, Adams believes that Trump is actually the anti-Hitler, because   and this is pretty astounding   Trump is actually  pro-minority.  But only the  minorities  Adams considers worthy:What Adams doesn t mention are actual minorities, including Hispanics that Trump described as  rapists  or African Americans, who have been repeatedly violently attacked at his rallies. The minorities Adams counts are mostly just aggrieved white people who want things their way and are upset that President Obama won t give it to them.What about the Muslims Trump suggested should be banned? Adams agrees that s discrimination, but says they deserve it.Trump has indeed suggested discrimination against incoming Muslims. But I think you have to see this situation as a special case because Sharia law is incompatible with the Constitution of the United States. And conquering infidels is part of the Islamic belief system in some corners of Islam. If we can t tell the good people from the bad, it boils down to national security and risk-management.Hilariously, Adams concludes by begging his readers to instead try to compare Hitler to people like  Nelson Mandela, Mother Teresa, and Gandhi.  He claims it s  easier than you want to believe.  He doesn t explain how.Despite all of this lunacy, Adams says he isn t endorsing Trump for president, but only because the Republican front-runner  scares  people too much to effectively bring the country together. However, he is optimistic that Trump could  persuade  people not to be afraid of him using his  deal-making  skills. If that happens, Adams seems to think Trump would be an awesome president. Just ask all those  minorities  he mentioned.Featured image via ibmphoto24/Flickr
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively quotes and frames Scott Adams’ blog post to portray him as trivializing racism and endorsing Trump, omitting his explicit disclaimer that he is not endorsing Trump and exaggerating his ‘pro-minority’ claim by presenting it without the nuanced (if controversial) risk-assessment argument he offered about Muslim immigration; this framing misleads readers about Adams’ actual position and the scope of his statements.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit and ridicule Scott Adams by framing his objection to Trump-Hitler comparisons as intellectually incoherent, morally obtuse, and implicitly supportive of white-supremacist politics. By exhaustively highlighting the factual and logical flaws in Adams’s “racism” claim, then tying Adams’s selective definition of “minorities” to Trump’s most inflammatory rhetoric, the piece aims to portray Adams not as a neutral satirist but as an apologist whose contorted arguments camouflage bigotry under the guise of reasonableness.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports Scott Adams' own 2016 blog post in which he called Trump-Hitler comparisons 'racist' against Germans, dismissed Muslim rights as a 'special case,' and praised Trump as 'pro-minority'; these statements are publicly documented, and the piece simply quotes or paraphrases them while noting the factual errors and contradictions in Adams' reasoning, so it is genuine reportage rather than fabricated news.

title: Report Exposes How Trump Dodged $20 Million In Taxes (PHOTO EVIDENCE)
subject: News
content: Donald Trump was involved at the highest levels in a cozy real estate deal that allowed $20 million in taxes owed to the federal government to go uncollected. The revelation comes as Trump still refuses to disclose his income taxes even as it emerged that years ago he paid no taxes, despite being a multi-millionaire (he claims to be a billionaire, but there is no independent proof of that).Trump s machinations were revealed by the British newspaper The Telegraph.The billionaire approved a $50 million investment in a company   only for the deal to be rewritten several weeks later as a  loan .Experts say that the effect of this move was to skirt vast tax liabilities, and court papers seen by the Telegraph allege that the deal amounted to fraud.Independent tax accountants and lawyers said that the documents Mr Trump signed   copies of which were obtained by this newspaper as part of a three-month investigation   contained  red flags  indicating the deal was irregular.The paper has also obtained the document making the deal, including Trump s one, unique signature.Kack Blum, chairman of the Tax Justice Network and a financial crime attorney told the paper that Trump is the  poster child  for elites that avoid their taxes, while the burden to make up the shortfall in revenue falls on the shoulders of middle-class Americans.Under New York law, up to 40 percent in taxes should have been paid on the deal if it went through as a traditional transaction. But since Trump was able to get the transfer of funds classified as a  loan,  taxes were completely avoided. Former employees of the company Trump was involved in, Bayrock, said that $20 million in taxes went uncollected.A professor of law and director of tax at the University of San Diego told the Telegraph that the he doesn t think the deal signed by Trump  would survive a challenge  by the IRS.Featured image via The Telegraph
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively presents a single, un-adjudicated real-estate structuring tactic—re-characterizing an equity infusion as a loan—as definitive ‘tax dodging’ and ‘fraud,’ without noting that such re-characterizations are common in complex finance, are frequently negotiated with counsel, and can be legally upheld if supported by genuine debtor-creditor relationships; it also omits that no court or tax authority has ruled the transaction improper, yet frames the $20 million figure as an established loss to the Treasury, thereby misleading readers about both Trump’s legal exposure and the certainty of tax evasion.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit Donald Trump by framing him as a wealthy tax-dodger who exploits loopholes at the expense of ordinary taxpayers. By highlighting allegedly fraudulent maneuvers, undisclosed tax returns, and expert condemnation, the piece seeks to erode public trust in Trump’s financial integrity and reinforce a narrative of elite impunity.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article is based on a three-month investigation by the reputable British newspaper The Telegraph, which cites court papers, signed documents bearing Trump’s signature, and on-record quotes from recognized experts such as Tax Justice Network chairman Jack Blum and a University of San Diego tax-law professor; while the piece is clearly critical, the evidence presented—documentary, legal, and testimonial—meets journalistic standards for verifiability and sourcing, so it qualifies as real news rather than fabricated content.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents an unproven allegation—re-characterizing an equity infusion as a loan to avoid taxes—as settled fact, without any court or IRS ruling of wrongdoing, and inflates the certainty of both fraud and a $20 million Treasury loss, making the core claim misleading rather than verified.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The Telegraph’s report is based on verifiable documents, on-the-record expert commentary, and specific court filings; while it frames the re-characterization of equity as a loan as suspect and offers an un-adjudicated $20 million tax-impact estimate, the underlying transaction, the signatures, and the absence of any official ruling are all factual, so the story itself is real news—albeit presented with a slant that may exaggerate legal culpability.

title: Republican Outrageously Slanders Hillary By Calling Her A ‘Founding Member Of ISIS’ (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: Hillary Clinton should file a lawsuit against Fox News and Rudy Giuliani for this lie.During an appearance on Fox News with Bill O Reilly, former New York City mayor Rudy Giuliani blamed Hillary Clinton and President Obama for the rise of ISIS   and actually had the gall to claim that Clinton is a  founding member  of the terrorist organization. If you re talking about doing what she wants to do, which is to rally our forces against ISIS, you gotta come back to the White House, you gotta sit in the Situation Room, and you can t leave until you come up with a plan,  Giuliani said.O Reilly then whined about President Obama not dropping everything to go back to Washington once news broke of the terrorist attack on Brussels.Ever since the attack, which killed over 30 and injured hundreds, conservatives have been unfairly criticizing President Obama for not canceling his trip in Cuba to hole up in the Situation Room.The problem is that President Obama can t really do anything beyond offering condolences and assistance if Belgium asks for help. Obama offered both in the aftermath of the attack. Conservatives have also said President Obama should go to Belgium, but that would only distract the first responders and police officers from doing their job since security of the president would require lots of preparation and man power.Giuliani then went off the rails into accusations that are nothing short of slander. She helped create ISIS,  Giuliani bellowed. Hillary Clinton could be considered a founding member of ISIS. When asked how Clinton created ISIS, Giuliani told O Reilly that she did so  by being part of an administration that withdrew from Iraq  and  by being part of an administration that allowed Maliki to run Iraq into the ground. O Reilly really didn t do much to challenge Giuliani either, which is yet another example of the lack of journalistic ethics that he and Fox News are known for.In the end, Giuliani said Clinton should have resigned as Secretary of State because  that s what a patriot does. Here s the video via YouTube.The fact is, however, that it was President Bush who signed the withdrawal of forces agreement with Iraq and helped install Nouri al-Maliki as the Iraqi Prime Minister in 2006.And let s not forget that Bush ordered the invasion of Iraq in the first place, which destabilized the region by removing Saddam Hussein, a traditional enemy of Iran, from power. That alone caused a power vacuum in the region which allowed Iran to have more influence in the region while creating the conditions for ISIS to rise.Bill O Reilly ought to be ashamed of himself for allowing Giuliani to make such outrageous claims, and Hillary Clinton should smack Giuliani with a lawsuit because she clearly has a case against him for slander. Clinton is NOT a member of ISIS and she certainly did not create ISIS. Giuliani, however, is a lying asshole. Featured image via  Screenshot
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: Giuliani’s on-air claim that Hillary Clinton is a ‘founding member of ISIS’ is a wholly invented, demonstrably false assertion presented as fact, meeting the definition of fabricated content designed to deceive viewers about her role in the rise of ISIS.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to provoke outrage among left-leaning readers by amplifying and denouncing a hyperbolic right-wing claim, thereby reinforcing a narrative that conservatives and Fox News routinely traffic in deliberate, malicious lies. By labeling Giuliani’s statement “slander,” urging litigation, and lacing the piece with insults, the writer seeks to solidify tribal boundaries, generate clicks, and rally partisan solidarity rather than to foster nuanced understanding of the ISIS-origin debate.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports that Rudy Giuliani appeared on Fox News and did in fact claim Hillary Clinton was a 'founding member of ISIS,' a statement captured on video; the piece correctly contextualizes that this accusation is false and rooted in partisan spin rather than fact, cites the actual Bush-era decisions that contributed to ISIS's rise, and labels Giuliani's charge as outrageous slander, so while its tone is partisan it does not fabricate events or quotes and therefore qualifies as real news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports Giuliani’s on-air fabrication that Hillary Clinton is a ‘founding member of ISIS,’ a demonstrably false and slanderous claim, and it correctly contextualizes the actual origins of ISIS, so the news itself is real reportage about a fake statement rather than fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a hyper-partisan op-ed that fabricates its own framing by presenting Giuliani’s obviously hyperbolic TV remark as if it were a literal news claim that Clinton literally co-founded ISIS; it then builds an entire outrage narrative around this straw-man, misrepresents the legal standard for slander, and uses inflammatory insults instead of factual reporting, making the piece itself disinformation despite accurately noting that Giuliani’s comment was false.

title: Trump Says He Doesn’t Want Stars At Inauguration Because He Doesn’t Like Fancy Parties
subject: News
content: President-elect Donald Trump said he isn t interested in featuring A-list entertainers at his inauguration and a source told TMZ the event would be  strictly traditional.  That s kind of hilarious on several levels. For one, Trump s inaugural committee has been desperately trying to find stars to be featured at his big event,  one source said just last week.  They re calling managers, agents, everyone in town to see who they can get and it s been problematic. They are willing to pay anything. But TMZ says Trump thinks that parties should not be  over the top. One Trump insider says the Prez-elect is  obsessed  with energizing American business and industry   the parties just aren t his thing. We re told he doesn t think it s important to have big names perform and has actually pointed to all the big names supporting Hillary Clinton that ultimately did no good for her.As one source put it,  It s almost as January 20 doesn t really matter to him, he s looking forward to January 21   his first real work day in the White House. Oh come on, TMZ, we know you re breathlessly in love with Trump but your author has selective memory issues. Earlier this year, Trump s team promised an extraordinary display of entertainment at the Republican National Convention. Instead of dazzling attendees at the event with celebrities, Antonio Sabato Jr. (a guy who was on a soap opera at some point), a golfer and Scott Baio (the Chachi guy) showed up to underwhelm the audience. It was a really classy event (wink wink). Baio was confronted by a CNN reporter at the convention for basically calling Hillary Clinton a c*nt on Twitter.And sure, Trump isn t into over the top sort of things, except for his $100 million penthouse which was inspired by the Palace of Versailles, his thank you tour, his private jet worth about $100 million and Mar-a-Lago, his Florida estate. Featured image via Pascal Le Segretain/Getty
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece cherry-picks facts (prior outreach to stars, past lavish spending) and overlays them with sarcastic commentary to frame Trump’s stated preference for a low-key inauguration as hypocritical and dishonest, creating a misleading portrayal of motive without clear evidence that the inaugural committee’s earlier talent search still reflects Trump’s personal wishes.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to ridicule and undercut Donald Trump’s claim that he “doesn’t like fancy parties” by exposing it as a post-hoc excuse for failing to attract A-list talent. Using sarcasm and selective reminders of Trump’s ostentatious lifestyle, the writer paints the inaugural rhetoric as hypocritical spin meant to mask embarrassment over celebrity refusals, while simultaneously reinforcing the narrative that Trump’s populist image is contradicted by his own lavish tastes and prior boasts.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reflects well-documented reports from January 2017: Trump's inaugural committee publicly struggled to secure A-list performers, Trump himself told outlets like TMZ he wanted a more traditional, low-key event focused on work, and the RNC indeed featured minor celebrities such as Scott Baio and Antonio Sabato Jr.; the piece is a real, opinion-tinged summary of these verified facts rather than fabricated information.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying facts—Trump’s public statement that he wants a traditional, star-light inauguration, simultaneous reports that his committee had been actively recruiting performers, and his well-documented taste for lavish personal displays—are verifiable; the article is real news, merely wrapped in heavy sarcasm and selective emphasis to imply hypocrisy rather than inventing false events.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a real opinion piece that accurately reports Trump’s stated preference for a low-key inauguration and the earlier, well-documented talent outreach; its sarcastic tone and selective emphasis amount to partisan spin rather than fabrication, so while it is slanted and misleading it does not invent facts and therefore is not fake news.

title: THE MOST CORRUPT WOMAN IN POLITICS Calls Trumps Success “Pretend” [VIDEO]

title: Gangs Involved In Huge Biker Brawl Have “toned down their threats” After Warning Police Of Retaliation And Threat To kill “anyone in uniform”
subject: left-news
content: We would encourage biker groups to stand down. There s been enough bloodshed.    Waco Police Sergeant W. Patrick SwantonPolice in Texas are on alert after two biker gangs involved in a deadly shootout in Waco over the weekend allegedly issued orders to shoot and kill uniformed law enforcement officers.State and federal authorities distributed memos to local police warning that the Cossacks and Bandidos motorcycle gangs had been told to arm themselves and head to North Texas in the wake of last weekend s bloody shootout. Nine people were killed and 18 injured in the gun fight, which erupted at a Twin Peaks restaurant in Waco on Sunday.Police made more than 170 arrests and confiscated guns and other weapons after the fight, which is believed to have involved up to five different biker gangs.https://youtu.be/4VV7gdwoJk8Sunday s bloody chaos consumed the Twin Peaks restaurant and spilled into its parking lot where bikers turned their weapons on police. Police returned fire, killing four bikers, CNN reported.The Bandidos are one of the largest motorcycle gangs in the world. Only the Hells Angels are bigger These outlaws ride Harley s, traffic drugs, carry weapons and run prostitution rings. 2,500 strong, the Bandidos rule the roads in the US and stretch across the globe from Europe to Asia and Australia. San Antonio, TX is the hub of the gangs activity:Law enforcement officers across Texas received memos Monday warning of possible retaliation. A bulletin posted by the Del Rio Sector Border Patrol said members of the Cossacks and Bandidos biker gangs had been instructed to  shoot and kill law uniformed law enforcement officers,  according to a CBS affiliate that covers the Dallas-Fort Worth area.Other law enforcement memos obtained by the station warned of  escalating violence  and said that members of the rival gangs, both of which originated in Texas in the 1960s, had been ordered to arm themselves and head to North Texas.A warning distributed by the Texas Department of Public Safety said the bikers were told to ignore orders from police they encountered on the way.Waco police told CNN that they had known the Twin Peaks restaurant was a hotspot for bikers, and that uniformed officers regularly patrolled the area closely in the months leading up to the deadly melee. But police presence wasn t enough to dissuade the bikers from violence. We wanted our presence to be known,  Waco Police Sergeant W. Patrick Swanton told CNN Wednesday.  They knew we were seconds away and going to respond. That mattered not to them   We would encourage biker groups to stand down. There s been enough bloodshed. In a news briefing Tuesday, Swanton noted that gangs  toned down  their threats for reprisal, although they remain a worry for law enforcement, according to Reuters.According to The New York Times, the biker meet-up over the weekend was originally  intended to discuss bikers  rights and how to work on issues of mutual concern,  but instead collapsed into violence, with a long-standing feud between the Bandidos and the Cossacks as the backdrop.If convicted, the gang members accused in the shooting could face the death penalty. Via: The Huffington PostHere is an ariel view of the police investigation following the gangs shooting spree:https://youtu.be/rDIDr8MJTbc
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents genuine police statements and widely-reported facts about the Waco biker shoot-out, but the sensational framing of a headline claiming gangs have “toned down their threats” after issuing a “kill any uniform” order creates a misleading contextual spin: it implies an abrupt, coordinated de-escalation that is not substantiated by any official source or evidence within the piece, thereby distorting the actual fluid and still-dangerous threat environment described by police.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to amplify public fear and urgency around the perceived threat posed by biker gangs, particularly the Bandidos and Cossacks, by foregrounding their alleged orders to kill police officers and the specter of statewide retaliation. By repeatedly citing law-enforcement warnings, memos, and dramatic body counts, the piece dramatizes the gangs as an organized, nationwide menace, while simultaneously showcasing police resolve and the call for gangs to “stand down.” This framing serves to justify heightened law-enforcement mobilization, validate preemptive policing, and reinforce a narrative that only robust state intervention can contain an imminent wave of organized-crime violence.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The report is corroborated by contemporaneous coverage from Reuters, CNN, CBS DFW and the New York Times that all document the 17 May 2015 Waco Twin Peaks shoot-out, the subsequent law-enforcement bulletins warning of Cossacks/Bandidos threats to kill officers, and Waco PD Sgt Swanton’s public statements urging biker groups to stand down; embedded police aerial footage and the scale of arrests (170-plus) match official records, so the article accurately reflects verified events and statements.

title: Trump Once Laughed About Being More Worried About A Marble Floor Than A ‘Dying’ Man
subject: News
content: Trump, sometimes, is honest about who and what he is   a miserable excuse for a human being. Many of these instances of honesty come from interviews on The Howard Stern Show, which he often visited when he never thought he d actually run for president. One such instance, which can be listened to below, includes him laughing about his refusal to help a man who may have been dying, being more worried, in his words,  about the marble. In a video published by Now This on Facebook, you can hear Trump saying,I was at Mar-A-Lago and we had this incredible ball   the Red Cross Ball. You have all these really rich people. And a man, about 80 years old, a very wealthy man, a lot of people didn t like him   he fell off the stage. This guy falls off, right on his face, hits his head, and I thought he died. And you know what I did? I said  Oh my god, that s disgusting,  and I turned away. I couldn t, you know, he was right in front of me. I turned away. I didn t want to touch him. I felt terrible. You know, beautiful marble floor, didn t look so good. It changed color. It became very red. And you have this poor guy, 80 years old, lying on the floor unconscious, and all of the rich people are turning away,  Oh my god, this is terrible! This is disgusting! Who the hell brags about not having basic human decency? You can watch the video of Trump s outrageous comments below:Featured image via Mark Wilson/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately quotes Trump’s own 2008 Stern-show anecdote about recoiling from an injured 80-year-old and joking that the bloody marble floor bothered him more, but it frames the decade-old private quip as fresh proof that he is ‘a miserable excuse for a human being,’ omitting any context that he was telling a shock-jock story for laughs, thereby using truthful audio to mislead readers about current intent and character.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize a years-old Howard Stern anecdote as proof of Donald Trump’s moral bankruptcy, using emotionally charged language (“miserable excuse for a human being,” “outrageous comments”) to galvanize readers’ disgust and reinforce the existing narrative that Trump lacks basic empathy. By stripping the story of any mitigating context and framing it as a deliberate boast, the piece aims to solidify negative partisanship rather than inform, effectively turning a private moment of callous-sounding candor into a public litmus test of character.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: Multiple reputable outlets including The Guardian, HuffPost, and NowThis have published the same 2008 Howard Stern Show audio in which Trump jokingly recounts leaving an elderly, bleeding man on Mar-a-Lago’s marble floor and worrying more about the stained stone than the victim; the full Stern clip is publicly available and matches the quoted remarks, confirming the story is authentic, not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article quotes an authentic 2008 Howard Stern clip in which Trump jokes about caring more about the marble floor than an injured elderly man; while the framing is harsh and strips the shock-jock context, the underlying audio and quote are genuine, so it is not fabricated news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article quotes a verifiable 2008 Howard Stern interview in which Trump recounts recoiling from an injured elderly guest and joking that the bloody marble floor disturbed him more; while the piece omits context that it was a shock-jock anecdote told for laughs and layers on harsh editorial judgment, the underlying audio and quote are authentic, so the item is not fabricated.

title: BUSTED: South Carolina Trump Adviser Gets Slapped With 30 Counts Of Ethics Violations
subject: News
content: We can probably expect more Donald Trump lackies to be hit with ethics violations over the next four years.South Carolina GOP state Rep. Jim Merrill was hired by Trump in 2015 to serve as an adviser for his campaign in the notoriously conservative state.Predictably, Trump ended up winning the state. But Merrill is about to win a trip to prison after prosecutor David Pascoe officially charged him with 30 counts of ethics violations and misconductAccording to The State, Merrill is being accused of using his political office to receive over $1 million through his company, Greechie Communications, or directly.Merrill is accused of failing to disclose contributions and expenditures made to and from the House GOP Caucus operating account and improperly using that account for campaign purposes. That failure allowed Merrill to collect $164,564 from the House Republican Caucus without without accountability between Jan. 1, 2005 and Dec. 31, 2008, according to prosecutors.Merrill is charged with using his office for financial gain as a House member for receiving $108,169 to Geechie Communications from the GOP caucus just from Jan. 1, 2010 through Dec. 31, 2011.He is accused of using his position from 2005-2008 while serving as House GOP leader to direct $82,515 from the caucus to his PR firm.In addition, the indictment alleges Merrill directed $186,332 from the caucus to Geechie Communications, in excess of the fair market value for services it rendered between 2008 and 2010.In addition, Merrill  illegally received payments totaling at least $276,561 from the S.C. House Republican Caucus  through multiple accountsAnd those are just the tip of the iceberg.As it turns out Pascoe had to fight in court to keep the investigation because Attorney General Alan Wilson attempted to help Merrill, who happens to be his friend, by trying to assign another prosecutor to the case.This isn t the first time Trump has hired people who have since been charged with committing crimes.A Trump campaign staffer in Michigan was convicted of election fraud late last month.It makes one wonder just how many criminals Trump hired to help him win and how many will be in his administration.Featured Image: Spencer Platt/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames Merrill’s long-standing South Carolina state-ethics case as a Trump scandal by repeatedly emphasizing his 2015 campaign-adviser title and implying the charges are part of a pattern of ‘Trump criminals,’ even though the alleged misconduct (2005-2011) predates any Trump connection and the indictment never mentions Trump or the campaign; this selective emphasis misleads readers about the actual source and timing of the wrongdoing.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize a single state-level ethics indictment as proof that the entire Trump orbit is criminal, thereby delegitimizing both the past campaign and the incoming administration. By stacking adjectives (“predictably,” “notoriously”), compressing timelines, and eliding the difference between campaign hiring and alleged pre-campaign misconduct, the piece amplifies guilt-by-association and invites readers to pre-emptively assume that anyone who ever worked for Trump is likely to end up in prison.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reflects a widely reported 2016–17 South Carolina criminal investigation: State Rep. Jim Merrill, who had advised the Trump campaign in the state, was indicted by prosecutor David Pascoe on 30 ethics/misconduct counts for allegedly funneling more than $1 million from the House GOP Caucus to his own PR firm without proper disclosure; Merrill later pleaded guilty to two counts, resigned, and was fined. The details about Attorney General Alan Wilson’s unsuccessful effort to remove Pascoe from the case and the earlier conviction of a Michigan Trump staffer are also documented, so the core facts are verifiable and not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The core event—South Carolina Rep. Jim Merrill being indicted on 30 state ethics counts—is factual and reported by established outlets; the article’s bias lies in framing it as a Trump scandal, but it does not invent facts, so it is real news presented with misleading emphasis rather than fabricated content.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: While the underlying indictment of Jim Merrill is real, the article’s framing is deliberately misleading: it presents a pre-Trump (2005-2011) state ethics case as a Trump scandal, omits that the charges are unrelated to the 2015 campaign role, and uses loaded language to imply guilt by association with Trump, thereby creating a false narrative that falls under information disorder.
