disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively frames the protest as an “anti-American” act meant to disrespect the flag and troops, omitting the stated purpose of the demonstration—drawing attention to racial injustice—thereby misleading readers about the athletes’ intent and the broader context of Kaepernick’s movement.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding goal is to inflame a culture-war grievance: recast athletes’ racial-justice protest as a treasonous, anti-soldier spectacle and then weld that image to partisan politics—blaming Obama (and by extension Hillary Clinton) for “hating the troops” and fomenting “race war.” By weaponizing casualty numbers, mocking teenagers, and ridiculing Kaepernick’s motives, the piece seeks to polarize readers, delegitimize dissent, and rally conservative outrage rather than to inform.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The core event—a Castlemont High School football team protest during the anthem attended by Colin Kaepernick—actually occurred on 23 Sept 2016 and was reported by multiple mainstream outlets (Mercury News, ESPN, etc.) with photos and video; the article’s vitriolic framing is partisan commentary, but the underlying facts are verifiable, so the item is not fabricated news.

title: DECLASSIFIED US INTEL REPORT Used To Discredit Trump Is Huge Embarrassment…Evidence Was Compiled In 2012 After OBAMA’S Reelection
subject: left-news
content: A highly-anticipated declassified US intelligence report, aimed to prove that Russia supported Donald Trump, has turned out to be a huge embarrassment. The annex that contained factual material that was thought to provide evidence of RT influencing the American public was compiled in December 2012, right after the reelection of Barack Obama.The report focuses on television shows and interviews that took place four years before Trump was elected, and well before he was even a politician. In Annex A of the report, intelligence agencies claim that  Kremlin s TV Seeks To Influence Politics, Fuel Discontent in US.  Buried at the bottom of that page is a note stating,  This annex was originally published on 11 December 2012 by the Open Source Center, now the Open Source Enterprise. The report notes that two RT shows, Breaking the Set and Truthseeker, focused on criticism of US. The problem is, both of these shows were off air before the 2016 election season began.The report goes on to detail programming in 2012 about voting booth irregularities, which, again, would have been during Obama s campaign. Despite being an old report, the topic became largely relevant once again during the Democratic primaries when voters found themselves purged from voting rolls, and hundreds of thousands of ballots went uncounted.Perhaps most shocking of all, the dastardly RT network dared to host third party debates, as they were not allowed participation in the main debates.  In an effort to highlight the alleged  lack of democracy  in the United States, RT broadcast, hosted, and advertised third party candidate debates and ran reporting supportive of the political agenda of these candidates. The RT hosts asserted that the US two-party system does not represent the views of at least one-third of the population and is a sham.  Apparently, the intelligence communities do not agree that some of the people they serve may not fit perfectly into the two neat and tidy political boxes of Republicans and Democrats. The report states that the network aired a documentary on Occupy Wall Street, an obviously left-wing movement, in 2012. Again, this was the year Obama was elected, so perhaps the Russians actually won HIM the presidency. They presented evidence that Russian media often reports on infringements of civil liberties, police brutality, and drone use. While these issues are all popular topics of discussion in left-leaning media, RT s reporting in 2012 was clearly part of a long-running plot to elect Trump, right?If the report is true and RT the Almighty was swinging votes in 2012, the only beneficiary of the coverage was the now-outgoing president of the United States, who won a landslide victory over Republican Mitt Romney. Four years ago Trump was not thought of as a politician and it remains a mystery how RT s 2012 coverage could propel him. A mystery, that even a classified version of the report would have a hard time explaining.    Sputnik news
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks the 2012 date of an RT-monitoring annex to imply the entire 2016 election-interference assessment is discredited, while ignoring that the declassified report’s main body (January 2017) draws on 2016 activities and that intelligence agencies routinely reuse older source material when it remains relevant; by conflating the annex’s vintage with the report’s overall thesis, it misframes the issue to cast doubt on Russian support for Trump without addressing the broader, contemporaneous evidence.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize the U.S. intelligence community’s 2016 Russia-Trump narrative by ridiculing the evidence as outdated, irrelevant, and politically motivated. By highlighting that the cited RT material predates Trump’s candidacy and actually criticized Obama-era issues, the piece reframes the report as an embarrassing partisan smear rather than proof of Kremlin interference, thereby insulating Trump and casting suspicion on any ongoing investigations or sanctions tied to Russian meddling.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article misrepresents a real 2012 Open Source Center annex by claiming it was the centerpiece of the 2017 declassified intelligence assessment on Russian interference; in fact, the 2012 material was only one appendix, while the main report (issued 6 Jan 2017) drew on 2016-specific findings (hacks, social-media troll farms, etc.) that are ignored here. It also omits that RT continued its pro-Trump messaging through 2016, making the 2012 date irrelevant to the overall judgment, and uses sarcastic rhetoric to imply the entire intelligence case rests on the old annex, which is false.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely implies that the entire 2017 intelligence assessment of Russian interference to help Trump rests only on a 2012 RT-monitoring annex, when the declassified report’s main body details 2016-era activities (hacks, social-media ops, etc.) and merely re-uses the older annex as background; by cherry-picking the annex’s date and ignoring the contemporaneous evidence, it constructs a misleading narrative to discredit the finding of Russian support for Trump.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely implies the entire 2016 Russian-interference assessment is discredited because one reused annex dates to 2012, while the actual January 2017 report is based on 2016 activities; by cherry-picking the annex’s date and ignoring contemporaneous evidence, it deliberately misleads readers to exonerate Trump and delegitimize U.S. intelligence conclusions.

title: CLINTON COVERUP: WHY WAS MAJOR CLINTON CRONY Put On Sensitive Intelligence Board? [Video]
subject: politics
content: Thank goodness for organizations like citizens United who found out what was going on with a Clinton donor getting a position on a Security Intelligence Board with ZERO experience. Please note the video below and how the reporter was to be arrested for asking a question of the Clinton crony. Newly released State Department emails help reveal how a major Clinton Foundation donor was placed on a sensitive government intelligence advisory board even though he had no obvious experience in the field, a decision that appeared to baffle the department s professional staff.The emails further reveal how, after inquiries from ABC News, the Clinton staff sought to  protect the name  of the Secretary,  stall  the ABC News reporter and ultimately accept the resignation of the donor just two days later.Copies of dozens of internal emails were provided to ABC News by the conservative political group Citizens United, which obtained them under the Freedom of Information Act after more the two years of litigation with the government.A prolific fundraiser for Democratic candidates and contributor to the Clinton Foundation, who later traveled with Bill Clinton on a trip to Africa, Rajiv K. Fernando s only known qualification for a seat on the International Security Advisory Board (ISAB) was his technological know-how. The Chicago securities trader, who specialized in electronic investing, sat alongside an august collection of nuclear scientists, former cabinet secretaries and members of Congress to advise Hillary Clinton on the use of tactical nuclear weapons and on other crucial arms control issues. Read more: Live Leak
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The item cherry-picks unflattering emails, omits the fact that ISAB seats are routinely filled by presidential appointees from industry, presents a routine resignation as proof of wrongdoing, and frames a single donor appointment as a ‘cover-up’ without evidence of quid-pro-quo, thereby misleading readers about the normalcy and legality of the process.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to cast Hillary Clinton as corrupt and reckless with national security by insinuating that she traded a sensitive intelligence-board seat for Clinton Foundation donations, then conspired to cover it up; the piece is framed to energize anti-Clinton voters, validate Citizens United’s investigative narrative, and reinforce a broader “pay-to-play” accusation against the Clintons without waiting for (or weighing) exculpatory context.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The core claim—that Clinton Foundation donor Rajiv Fernando was appointed to the sensitive International Security Advisory Board despite lacking traditional qualifications, then resigned quickly after press inquiries—is documented in State Department e-mails released under FOIA litigation to Citizens United and reported by ABC News in 2016; while the headline’s tone is partisan, the underlying facts are corroborated by government records and mainstream outlets, so the story itself is real.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The story is built on selective leaks, omits the routine nature of presidential appointments to advisory boards, and presents no evidence that Fernando’s seat was illegal or that any quid-pro-quo occurred; by labeling a standard resignation after press questions a ‘cover-up’ it fabricates scandal where none exists, satisfying the definition of fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is not fabricated, but it is packaged as disinformation: it cherry-picks FOIA emails, omits the routine White House prerogative to name industry voices to advisory boards, presents a voluntary resignation after press questions as a ‘cover-up,’ and offers zero evidence of a quid-pro-quo, thereby misleading readers into believing an ordinary appointment was an illegal pay-to-play scheme.

title: While We Were Watching Comey’s Testimony, The House Quietly Sucker-Punched Our Economy
subject: News
content: The news of the day is the testimony that former FBI Director James Comey gave to the Senate Intelligence Committee this morning, along with Trump s lawyer s response in which there were all kinds of false allegations leveled at Comey. And while we were all swept up in that, the House was busy sucker-punching us. They held an important vote today on what to do with the Dodd-Frank financial reform bill that was passed in the wake of the financial crisis of 2008.They re ridiculously calling their new bill the CHOICE Act. It basically allows the banks to decide for themselves whether they continue to abide by Dodd-Frank or not. Because self-regulation, particularly of the financial sector, has always worked so well in the past.The CHOICE Act has a capital requirement that many banks say is still too high, but in light of what else this bill does, that s a minor complaint. The bill guts the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which was created specifically as an oversight body to help rein in risky behavior on the part of the big banks.Paul Ryan calls it  a jobs bill for Main Street.  Oh, please, Mr. Speaker, you know we can see right through your baloney. Especially on this.While Ryan and many of his cohorts are cheering the CHOICE Act s passage, some of the more sane Republicans and most Democrats are slamming it for  paving the way back to economic damage of the same scale [as the financial crisis] or worse,  as Maxine Waters put it.Furthermore, a story on Fortune s website says that this bill would prohibit the CFPB from publishing the data it collects on complaints about banks and other financial services, such as credit reporting. That, in turn, makes it more difficult for consumers to make informed choices, and it also could potentially remove an avenue for filing complaints and actually getting results: Individuals can also file complaints to try to right a wrong, such as when a credit bureau refuses to fix an error on a credit score. Credit reporting bureaus are notorious for mistakes, with as many as one in five consumers potentially having an error in their credit file.Yet the three main credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, and Trans Union) lack proper incentives to fix these errors, which is why it should come as no surprise that they are the three most complained about companies in the CFPB database. [Full disclosure: I once filed a complaint about an error in my credit file, which I had been unable to fix in direct contact with the company, but after I filed a report with CFPB it was quickly fixed.] We know that the GOP doesn t care one whit about creating jobs, helping people in general or protecting the economy. They just proved it, again, with this after proving it with their insipid Obamacare replacement. Fortunately, like the AHCA, this has little chance of even making it to the Senate floor for a vote.Featured image via Ty Wright/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece selects only the most negative interpretations of the CHOICE Act—portraying it as total self-regulation, a deliberate ‘sucker-punch,’ and proof that ‘the GOP doesn’t care one whit’—while omitting any mention of the bill’s actual capital-trigger mechanism, its retention of stress tests for big banks, or supporters’ arguments about regulatory relief for community banks, thereby framing the issue in a one-sided, alarmist way that misleads readers about the legislation’s scope and intent.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to expose and condemn what they portray as a deliberate Republican bait-and-switch: using the Comey-Trump spectacle as cover to advance the Financial CHOICE Act, which the author frames as a dangerous gift to Wall Street that guts consumer protections and invites another financial crisis. By juxtaposing the high-drama Senate hearing with the “quiet” House vote, the writer seeks to alarm readers about systemic GOP priorities—prioritizing bank deregulation and corporate profit over ordinary Americans’ economic security—while rallying opposition before the bill can reach the Senate.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately describes the Financial CHOICE Act (H.R. 10), which the House passed on June 8, 2017—the same day as Comey’s testimony. The bill’s provisions to make Dodd-Frank compliance optional for banks meeting a capital threshold, to restructure and weaken the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and to restrict publication of consumer-complaint data are all documented in the legislative text and contemporaneous reports from Fortune, Reuters, and other outlets, confirming the piece is grounded in verifiable fact rather than fabrication.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports an actual House vote on the Financial CHOICE Act and accurately quotes named lawmakers; its ‘misleading content’ flaw is partisan framing and omission of mitigating details, not fabrication of events, so it remains real news with a skewed presentation.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports an actual House vote on the Financial CHOICE Act, accurately notes its main provisions (opt-out from Dodd-Frank for banks meeting a capital trigger, CFPB restrictions, complaint-data limits), cites named lawmakers and a Fortune story, and discloses the bill’s unlikely Senate path; while the framing is highly opinionated and omits some mitigating details, no factual event or vote is fabricated, so it qualifies as real news presented through a partisan lens.

title: RIGGED: Hillary Wins Popular Vote As Republicans Claim WH Victory
subject: News
content: While the final vote tally won t be in for quite some time, at this point it s looking like the massive victory Republicans were granted yesterday was due largely in part to gerrymandering   perfectly legal rigging of the vote that parties take advantage of during the census. Because Republicans controlled most state legislatures during the time of the last census, Republican votes tend to count more than Democratic votes do.That s why, despite the simple fact that more people probably voted for Hillary Clinton, we are facing at least four years of a Donald Trump presidency. We actually saw exactly how this would play out in 2012, when Republicans took the House despite losing by over a million in the popular vote. Democrats simply can t afford close races.It s hard to admit, but Donald Trump was right about something   the election WAS rigged. By state and congressional Republicans, and then by obstructionists. Hopefully, this loss teaches the Democrats that stayed home and leftists that refused to unify that we can t afford to put ideology over pragmatism. When the other side is cheating, the only solution is to boost turnout beyond what they can cope with. That s really the only way to see a silver lining in any of this   maybe people will learn. The Democratic Party picked up seats in the House and Senate   enough to give the GOP a taste of  no    but the next four years are looking bleak.Here s a video that explains the process of gerrymandering and how Republicans have orchestrated it so that your vote doesn t count the way it should:Also, you should know there is an interstate compact between quite a few states   and the list is growing   that are pledging to give their electors to the winner of the popular vote the next time around. That d be a win for democracy. If we d had that in play this time around, we might not be looking at a Donald Trump presidency. And it would mean that every vote does, indeed, count   right now, unless you live in a swing state, you probably already know whether your vote counts before you cast it.Photo by John Sommers II/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece repeatedly conflates the Electoral College outcome with House-level gerrymandering, implying that district map-rigging—not the constitutional state-winner-take-all system—let Trump win the presidency while losing the popular vote. In reality, gerrymandering affects only U.S. House and state-legislative seats, not how states allocate electoral votes for president; Trump’s victory rested on winning pluralities in key swing states, not on manipulated congressional districts. By framing the election as ‘rigged’ through gerrymandering and presenting House vote totals as evidence, the article misleads readers about which institutions were actually influenced and how the Electoral College functions.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize the 2016 Republican victory by framing it as the product of systemic manipulation—especially gerrymandering—while rallying Democrats and left-leaning voters to recognize structural disadvantages, reject ideological purity, and mobilize in future elections; simultaneously, the piece promotes reform measures like the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact to restore perceived democratic fairness.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately describes the 2016 U.S. election outcome—Hillary Clinton won the national popular vote while Donald Trump won the presidency via the Electoral College—and correctly attributes Republican House control in 2012 to Democratic House candidates receiving more votes nationwide. It accurately explains gerrymandering as a legal practice used by both parties but dominated by Republicans after the 2010 census, and it references the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, a real multi-state agreement. Although the tone is partisan, the factual claims align with certified election results and mainstream political science, so the piece is not fake news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely attributes Trump’s Electoral College win to gerrymandering, a practice that affects only U.S. House and state-legislative districts, not presidential elector allocation; by presenting this distorted causal link as fact and repeatedly calling the presidential election “rigged” through gerrymandering, it disseminates a demonstrably untrue narrative, qualifying it as fake news.

title: FAMILY OF S.C. SHOOTING VICTIM HAS A MESSAGE FOR AL SHARPTON And He’s Not Gonna Like It…
subject: politics
content: Poor little Al if he s not race baiting, he s hanging out with our  President  at the White House just waiting for the next white on black  injustice.  Heck if we didn t know better, we d almost think he enjoys being in front of the camera holding up the grieving parents but that would be so so insincere Stay away, Rev. Al. We don t want another Ferguson type of circus here,  a source close to the Scott family told The Daily News.That was the message from the family of South Carolina police shooting victim Walter Scott to the civil rights activist Thursday two days before the funeral for the slain father of four.That was a reference to the Missouri town that was rocked by violent demonstrations last year after black teen Michael Brown was killed by a white cop.Sharpton gave a rousing speech at the 18-year-old s funeral, which was attended by thousands.Scott family attorney Chris Stewart said they appreciate Sharpton s support but  the funeral is only going to be close family members. Via: NY Daily News
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline and article cherry-pick an anonymous “source close to the Scott family” to claim the family has broadly told Al Sharpton to “stay away,” while the body shows the official family attorney explicitly appreciates Sharpton’s support and merely states the funeral itself will be private. The framing thus misrepresents a logistical detail as a sweeping rejection of Sharpton, fueling a pre-existing “race-baiting” narrative and casting the family’s stance in a false, politically charged light.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize and marginalize Rev. Al Sharpton by framing him as a self-serving opportunist who exploits tragedies for personal gain. By amplifying an anonymous “source close to the Scott family,” the piece weaponizes their grief to discredit Sharpton’s civil-rights advocacy, portraying his presence as the catalyst for “another Ferguson type of circus.” This narrative stokes racial resentment, ridicules both Sharpton and the Obama administration, and implicitly instructs readers to view anti-racism activism as insincere spectacle rather than legitimate protest.

title: WOMEN IN FRANCE Fight Back After Muslim Men BAN Them From Sharing Public Spaces [VIDEO]
subject: left-news
content: These women aren t sitting back and waiting for their leftist government to come to their rescue in these  no-go zones  which are spreading across France. A women s rights campaign group is organizing marches and protests in a bid to retake streets in predominantly Islamic neighborhoods which they say have become entirely male dominated.La Brigade des M res, which is aiming to restore gender equality in France s troubled  banlieues , says women in many communities are now too scared to go out because gangs of young men rule the streets.And a shocking undercover report, compiled by the TV channel France 2, shows how women are not welcome in bars and cafes in Muslim majority areas, with many men openly hostile to their presence in public at all.  Express UkThank God we finally have a leader who is brave enough to take the arrows on our behalf, as he takes a tough stand against open-border immigration and unvetted refugees flowing into America. Our nation will never be 100% safe from Islamic terrorism, but for now, we can at least stop the bleeding. We must resist these lawless pockets of resistance in our nation filled with people who have no interest in our rule of law and the freedoms we Americans hold dear.
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames isolated incidents and activist rhetoric as evidence that Muslim men have imposed a de-facto gender ban across entire French neighborhoods, omitting official crime statistics, local women’s own diversity of views, and French law that already prohibits discrimination; by cherry-picking hidden-camera footage and partisan commentary it misleads readers into believing a systemic, religion-based expulsion of women from public space is the norm rather than a contested claim, thereby stoking fear and hate.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize a selectively framed story about gender segregation in French Muslim neighborhoods in order to stoke fear of Islam, legitimize anti-immigrant policies, and rally support for a hard-line U.S. leader portrayed as the last defense against an encroaching “Islamic threat.” By amplifying a single women’s-rights grievance and fusing it with nativist rhetoric (“open-border immigration,” “unvetted refugees,” “lawless pockets of resistance”), the piece converts a complex local tension into a morality tale that demonizes Muslim communities, justifies exclusionary immigration controls, and positions the favored politician as a heroic protector of Western freedoms.

title: BREAKING: Russian Officials Celebrate Rex Tillerson As ‘A Gift’ From Trump To Russia
subject: News
content: Quid pro quo in the Trump/Russia situation is happening sooner than expected, at least according to Russian officials   you know, they give him a gift by using hacking a propaganda to hand him the election, and Trump builds a nightmarish team for himself that will be very friendly to Russia. So friendly, in fact, that the Kremlin is pretty openly celebrating Trump s newest  gift  to them.Thus far, The Donald has filled his cabinet to the brim with so many pro-Russian people that Stolichnaya stocks have gone through the roof (just joking, don t bother Googling that). Seriously, though, Russia is thrilled with Trump s selections so far.But it is Rex Tillerson s nomination for Secretary of State that, as The Guardian notes,  confirms Vladimir Putin as one of the strategic victors of the US presidential election. The Wall Street Journal notes that  Friends and associates said few US citizens are closer to Mr Putin than Mr Tillerson.  And, of course, Tillerson will now be in a position to make a f*ckton of money in his new position, as The Guardian points out:The 2011 Exxon-Rosneft agreement was frozen when sanctions were imposed on Russia in 2014, following the annexation of Crimea and covert military intervention in eastern Ukraine. Exxon Mobil estimated the sanctions cost it $1bn and Tillerson has argued strenuously for the measures to be lifted. We always encourage the people who are making those decisions to consider the very broad collateral damage of who are they really harming with sanctions,  he said, at a shareholders  meeting.In June, two years after sanctions were imposed and in an apparent show of support for Sechin, Tillerson reportedly turned up at a St Petersburg economic summit.If the sanctions were lifted, the Arctic project would probably go ahead and Tillerson s retirement fund of Exxon Mobil stock would increase in value. He would most likely have to divest himself of stock by the time he entered the office on the seventh floor of the state department. It might be harder to divorce his judgments entirely from the oil company where he spent his career.Tillerson s nomination can be called a lot of things   but pro-Kremlin Russian political commentator Sergei Markov calls it what it is:  some kind of Christmas gift from the American people to the Russian people  especially in light of the  artificial  Cold War  that was started with Russia  over the country s involvement in hacking Donald Trump s political enemies for him (at his request, no less).Fyodor Lukyanov, head of the Council on Foreign and Defense Policy, which advises the Kremlin, says that Tillerson represents  profound changes in U.S. foreign policy  that stands to favor Russia heavily. Mr. Tillerson is very well known to the important people here, and neither Mr. Putin nor the others will need time to learn who he is and how to deal with him,  Lukyanov says.  This news is better than any other possible person for this position. At this point, how can we allow Donald Trump to assume power on January 20? Electors have the weight of the world on their shoulders as December 19 approaches. Will they do nothing and allow a tyrant installed by a foreign power to take office   or will they do the right thing and say  no more? Featured image via Getty Images/Alexey Druzhinin
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively quotes Russian commentators and financial interests to frame Rex Tillerson’s nomination as a quid-pro-quo “gift” from Trump to Putin, omitting counter-evidence such as bipartisan business ties, Congress’s sanctions control, and Tillerson’s later tough-on-Russia stance, thereby using genuine snippets of Russian reaction to misleadingly portray the appointment as proof of collusion rather than one of several geopolitical interpretations.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to persuade readers that Donald Trump’s nomination of Rex Tillerson is not a routine cabinet choice but the payoff in a quid-pro-quo bargain with Russia, thereby “proving” that Trump is already delivering the Kremlin’s preferred foreign-policy outcomes in return for its alleged election interference. By stitching together selective facts, ominous quotes from Russian commentators, and insinuations about Tillerson’s future enrichment, the text seeks to alarm the public and, specifically, to pressure members of the Electoral College to deny Trump the presidency on 19 December 2016.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports real public reactions from Russian officials and commentators—such as Sergei Markov and Fyodor Lukyanov—who openly welcomed Rex Tillerson’s 2016 nomination as Secretary of State, citing his long business ties with Rosneft and advocacy for lifting sanctions; these statements were covered contemporaneously by reputable outlets like The Guardian and WSJ, and the piece correctly notes Tillerson’s Exxon-Rosneft deal, shareholder losses from sanctions, and his appearance at the 2016 St Petersburg forum, so while its editorial tone is highly opinionated, the underlying facts and attributed quotes are verifiable and not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not fabricated, but it is fake news in the contextual sense: it presents a one-sided, conspiratorial collage—cherry-picked Russian quotes, speculative financial motives, and unsupported collusion insinuations—as established fact while ignoring readily available counter-facts (bipartisan support for Tillerson, Congress’s statutory hold on sanctions, his later endorsement of arming Ukraine, etc.). By omitting this balancing evidence and using sensational framing (“gift,” “tyrant installed by a foreign power”) to imply an illegal quid-pro-quo, it crosses from opinion into deliberate disinformation, misleading readers about the nature and implications of the nomination.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece dresses opinion and speculation as fact, omitting essential context (Congress controls sanctions, Tillerson later took hawkish positions) and presenting no verifiable evidence of an actual quid-pro-quo; its selective quotes and emotive language aim to deceive readers into believing proven collusion rather than reporting demonstrable reality, fitting the definition of fake news.

title: DISGRACEFUL: US Air Force Can No Longer Afford 21-Gun Salute At Vet Funerals…Plenty Of Funds For Muslim Immigrants
subject: Government News
content: We can t afford to give our US Veterans a proper funeral, but we ve got money to burn when it comes to bringing Muslim refugees to the US from countries who hate us. On average, each Middle Eastern refugee resettled in the United States costs an estimated $64,370 in the first five years, or $257,481 per household. When a veteran or member of the armed forces dies, he or she is entitled to a ceremony that includes the presentation of a U.S. flag to a family member and a bugler blowing Taps. Most of the time, there is a three-volley rifle salute if requested by family members. But now, if the deceased served in the Air Force, the three-volley salute is not an option because the Air Force can no longer support riflemen for funeral services for veteran retirees.Seven member services for retirees included six members to serve as pall-bearers, a six member flag-folding detail, and a three riflemen to fire the salute. Veteran s funerals now only receive the services of two-member teams, who provide a flag-folding ceremony, the playing of taps, and the presentation of the flag to the next of kin. To me, without the 21-gun salute, it just does not make it complete a proper military burial,  veteran Wayne Wakeman told Honolulu s KHON 2 News.  I think because of sequestration or the lack of funds or whatever excuse they re giving, that they had to hit the veterans. Wakeman is correct in supposing the cut is due to sequestration, the 2013 automatic federal spending cuts required by the Budget Control Act of 2011.Rose Richeson, from the Secretary of the Air Force s Public Affairs Press Desk, told We Are The Mighty the policy of restricting the funeral honor is an Air Force-wide requirement. The requirement is consistent with DoD policy which require a minimum of two personnel,  Richeson said.  Any number of personnel above two that is provided in support of military funeral honors is based on local resources available.  Via: FOX News
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article juxtaposes two unrelated budget items—Air Force funeral honors and refugee resettlement—to imply that money is being diverted from veterans to Muslim immigrants, a classic misleading framing. The Air Force’s reduction of rifle teams is a consequence of the 2013 sequestration cuts, not of refugee spending, and the $64,370-per-refugee figure is presented without context that it covers five years of federal, state, and local programs, not a single cash hand-out. By weaving these unrelated facts into a single narrative of betrayal, the piece misleads readers about cause-and-effect and stokes anti-immigrant sentiment.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to inflame a culture-war grievance by framing a routine, budget-driven reduction in Air Force funeral honors as a deliberate slight to veterans so that money can instead be lavished on Muslim immigrants. By yoking two unrelated budget lines—military funeral details and refugee-resettlement costs—the piece invites readers to see a zero-sum betrayal: “our” heroes are being short-changed in order to reward “their” undeserving outsiders. The emotional payoff is outrage that both deflects attention from the mundane fiscal causes (sequestration) and reinforces an anti-immigrant, anti-Muslim narrative.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The claim that the U.S. Air Force has ended 21-gun (three-volley) salutes at veterans’ funerals because it is spending money on Muslim immigrants is false and inflammatory. The reduction to two-person funeral honors teams for Air Force retirees began in 2013 as a result of congressionally-mandated sequestration budget cuts, not because funds were redirected to refugee programs; the Department of Defense explicitly states that any additional honors above the congressionally-required two-person detail depend on local availability of volunteers and funds. Meanwhile, refugee-resettlement money comes from entirely separate State-Department and HHS appropriations, not the Air Force budget, and the article’s juxtaposition of veteran honors with Muslim immigration is a misleading attempt to manufacture outrage rather than report factual cause-and-effect.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is built on a fabricated cause-and-effect claim: it presents the Air Force’s trimming of rifle-honor teams (a 2013 sequestration consequence) as if money were literally taken from veteran funerals and handed to Muslim refugees, when these budget lines are unrelated and the refugee-cost figure is stripped of its five-year, multi-program context, making the central narrative false.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article fabricates a causal link between Air Force budget cuts for funeral honors and refugee resettlement spending, presenting them as a deliberate trade-off when they are unrelated budget lines determined by separate laws and processes; it misrepresents sequestration-driven reductions as a choice to fund Muslim immigrants, uses decontextualized cost figures, and omits that the Defense Department—not refugee programs—sets funeral honor levels, making the central claim false and intentionally misleading.

title: WORLD FAMOUS DESIGNER Tells Americans To “Deal” With Trump’s: “Mrs. Trump is a very nice woman and pretty handsome. Good body, no? And this Ivanka is…

content: Fashion Designer Kari Lagerfield who was rumored to dress Melania Trump for her husband s inauguration has no plans of letting his political views get in the way of his fashion business.The 83-year-old hasn t voted in 40 years since he became an official resident of Monaco, and the designer says that he prefers to keep business and politics separate.Via Page Six:The designer reveals he  loved Michelle Obama,  and  Mrs. Trump is a very nice woman and pretty handsome. disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately quotes Karl Lagerfeld’s remarks, but it repackages them under a click-bait headline that makes it sound as though the designer issued a blunt political directive (“WORLD FAMOUS DESIGNER Tells Americans To ‘Deal’ With Trump’s…”) when, in the body, his comment is a mild, off-hand observation that a democratically elected president must be accepted. The sensational headline thus supplies a sharper, more confrontational context than Lagerfeld’s actual statements, nudging readers toward a false impression of the tone and intent of the source material.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to amplify a celebrity’s dismissive sound-bite—“deal with it”—so that readers will re-share the controversy, not to inform them about fashion or politics; by stripping Lagerfeld’s remarks of context, foregrounding his objectifying comments about the Trump women, and packaging the quote as a scolding of “Americans,” the piece is engineered to trigger partisan outrage and clicks while masquerading as a neutral “celebrity says” story.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The quotes and story match multiple reputable sources (Daily Mail, Page Six) and accurately reflect Karl Lagerfeld’s well-documented habit of giving blunt, politically neutral sound-bites while insisting fashion and politics stay separate; no factual element is invented or misattributed.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying facts—Lagerfeld’s actual words, the source outlets, and the designer’s stance—are verifiable and reported correctly; the only distortion is a sensational headline that exaggerates his tone, which qualifies as misrepresentation rather than fabrication, so the item is real news presented with misleading framing.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: While the embedded quotes from Karl Lagerfeld are authentic, the news item is presented through a deliberately distorted frame: a hyperbolic headline fabricates the claim that the designer issued a confrontational directive to Americans, and the story’s selective emphasis on objectifying remarks about the Trump women is engineered to provoke outrage rather than inform. This mismatch between headline and content, coupled with the manipulative intent to generate partisan clicks, qualifies the piece as fake news under the false-context model.

title: PUTIN Threatens To Release 20,000 “Top Secret” Emails From Hillary…Why Judge Napolitano Says This Is Very Bad News For Hillary [VIDEO]

content: Putin may be the one person Obama has absolutely no influence over. disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article recycles a 2016 Fox-segment claim that Russia possesses 20,000 hacked Clinton emails and presents it as a new, confirmed threat, but offers no fresh evidence or official confirmation; the original allegation was speculative and unverified, so republishing it without context that it remains unsubstantiated misleads readers into believing the claim is currently validated and materially damaging to Clinton.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize unverified or exaggerated claims—chiefly that Russia possesses 20,000 hacked Clinton emails—to inflame existing distrust of Hillary Clinton and the Obama administration, cast her as irrevocably compromised, and thereby delegitimize her political future. By stacking selectively curated “evidence” (Guccifer, Napolitano, Judicial Watch) and ominous speculation, the piece seeks not to inform but to persuade readers that Clinton’s legal jeopardy is imminent and that only foreign actors and conservative watchdogs can expose the truth, turning a still-unsubstantiated allegation into a fatal narrative.

title: NOT KIDDING: Obama’s Weak Immigrant Vetting Process Doesn’t Even Include Asking If They Belong To ISIS, Al Qaeda Or Muslim Brotherhood
subject: left-news
content: This new information just adds more validity Trump s argument, that the US needs to take a more serious look at the way we vet immigrants if we want to protect our national security While State Department and the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Service branch of the Department of Homeland Security do ask if immigrants have been involved in terrorism, the most well known of over a dozen terrorist groups aren t listed in applications, according to the analysis from homeland security expert Mark A. Sauter.The form asks if the applicant has ever belonged to a terrorist group, but neglects to ask if they currently belong to one. How hard would that be to update? He said that federal officials told him that the questions about terror group involvement are required by federal law, meaning that congressional action is needed to include modern-day threats in the written questions.However, detailed written questions are asked about Nazi cooperation, as are questions about whether applicants are drunks, polygamists, or Communists. One survey does single out Colombian terror organizations in the written questions, though they have never attacked inside the U.S. The lack of specific questioning about the biggest threat to the United States as the country eyes thousands in line from Syria, Afghanistan, Iran and elsewhere seeking residency raises new questions about how immigrants are vetted, and gives ammunition to Republicans like presidential candidate Donald Trump who has called for  extreme vetting  to weed out likely terrorists.  The Examiner
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively presents the vetting form’s generic terrorism question as a ‘weakness’ while omitting that U.S. procedures include multi-agency biometric, biographic and intelligence checks against classified watch-lists that already flag ISIS, al-Qaeda and Muslim Brotherhood ties; by framing the absence of a printed list of every group as proof that Obama ‘doesn’t even ask,’ it misleads readers about the actual layered screening process and fuels a politically charged narrative.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to politically discredit the Obama-era immigration system by framing it as dangerously negligent on national-security grounds, thereby legitimizing Donald Trump’s “extreme vetting” rhetoric. By selectively highlighting outdated or omitted questions on visa forms and juxtaposing them with references to Nazis, drunks and polygamists, the piece amplifies a perception that officials are more worried about trivial or obsolete threats than today’s “biggest” terror groups. The article weaponizes this contrast to energize conservative voters, pressure Congress to rewrite screening laws, and cast Republican hard-liners as the only leaders serious about protecting the country from immigrant terrorism.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article misrepresents the U.S. immigrant-vetting process: federal forms (DS-260, I-485, etc.) already ask whether an applicant has engaged in or plans to engage in terrorist activities, and background checks are run against multiple classified and unclassified terrorism databases; the absence of a printed checklist naming every group does not equate to ‘not asking.’  The claim that officials are unaware of current membership is false, because follow-up interviews and biometric/intelligence checks flag ongoing associations.  The piece also omits that the same statutes it cites already define and bar members of any terrorist organization, including ISIS, al-Qaeda and the Muslim Brotherhood, regardless of whether the group’s name appears in a drop-down list.  Thus the central assertion—‘Obama’s process doesn’t even ask’—is demonstrably untrue, making the article misleading fake news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is factually false in claiming the U.S. does not ask about ISIS/al-Qaeda links; the visa/immigration form (DS-260/DS-160) asks “Have you EVER engaged in … terrorist activities or been a member of a terrorist organization?” and every applicant is run against multiple classified watch-lists that already contain ISIS, al-Qaeda and Muslim Brotherhood.  Omitting these realities while asserting Obama’s process “doesn’t even ask” is a deliberate misrepresentation, making the piece disinformation rather than merely misleading.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece fabricates a false crisis by claiming the U.S. “doesn’t even ask” about ISIS/al-Qaeda, while in reality every applicant is run against classified terrorist-watch-list, biometric and intelligence databases that already target those exact groups; the absence of a printed roster on the form is irrelevant to the multi-layer security checks that occur, making the central allegation deceptive and therefore fake.

title: BREAKING: TEXAS COP STABBED 14 TIMES By Man Who “had a desire to kill a police officer”
subject: left-news
content: Who knew that in our  First Black President s  second term killing cops would be all the rage in the black community? A Houston Community College police officer has survived an assassination attempt after being stabbed by her assailant 14 times. The officer was saved by civilians who stepped in and stopped the attacker. The attacker told investigators he did this to get back at police for their brutality. A spokesman from the family said it might be related to the Baltimore riots.Officer April Pikes remains in critical condition at Houston s Ben Taub Hospital, a public relations official at the Houston Police Department said to Breitbart Texas. Her alleged attacker, Jeremiah M. Matthews, 23, was pulled off of her by a group of men while he was stabbing her and attempting to grab her pistol, according to a statement from HPD obtained by Breitbart Texas.Harris County prosecutors said that Matthews told them  he had the intent to attack a police officer and his desire to kill a police officer,  according to a Click2Houston.com report. One of the witnesses, Abe Baker, who helped stop the attack said,  I saw him on her, just stabbing her. I wasn t really thinking,  Baker said.  His arm was just up getting ready to stab her and I just grabbed his arm and took him down, and that s when everybody else came over and we all just took him down. The HPD statement revealed that Matthews stabbed her several times before he was tackled and disarmed. The statement says he was attempting to gain control of her duty weapon. After taking down the suspect, the good Samaritans used the officer s handcuffs to detain Matthews until other police officers arrived and arrested him.The Click2Houston report states that Pike may lose her right arm. She was stabbed repeatedly in her right arm and torso.The scene of the attack was a Walmart located in Meyerland (Southwest Houston), where Pikes was working an approved off-duty security job. Pikes was in uniform when she was attacked. He was in an upbeat mood, whistling and he had a fast pace, walking fast,  Baker said of the assailant, who was smiling and cheerful right up until the moment he began his surprise attack. He does have a diagnostic history of mental illness in the past. To what degree that played into what happened, we don t know,  local community activist Deric Muhammad said, speaking on behalf of the Matthews family. He said it is possible that Matthews was inspired by the riots in Baltimore Monday night.The weapon was described as a hunting knife in a report by Fox26Houston s Kristine Galvan. That was an innocent woman. She had family, loved ones,  Abe Baker told Galvan.  That s someone s life and everyone s life counts and matters. Baker said he stopped by the Walmart on a late-night errand to pick up some laundry soap, and came to the rescue when he heard Pikes  screams. His quick action, and the response of the other men, probably saved her life. I want to offer my condolences to the victim,  said Vanessa Johnson, Matthews  mother, in the Fox26 video.  As a mother this is painful. I wish her a speedy recovery. My heart and prayers are going out to her and their entire family. The HPD statement from Wednesday morning states that Matthews has been charged with Attempted Capital Murder. His case has been assigned to the 182nd State District Court, which is presided over by Judge Jeannine Barr.Via: Breitbart News
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article’s opening line frames a brutal crime as a trend supposedly embraced by 'the black community' during the Obama presidency, turning a single attacker’s actions into a racial indictment. This sweeping generalization attributes collective guilt to Black Americans, invokes racialized fear, and encourages hostility toward an entire group, meeting the definition of bias-motivated, hostile expression targeting people for who they are.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize a horrific act of violence against a police officer in order to stoke racialized outrage and reinforce a politically charged narrative that Black Americans—implicitly emboldened by the nation’s first Black president—are waging a war on law enforcement. By foregrounding the attacker’s race, invoking Baltimore-era unrest, and framing the stabbing as part of a broader “rage” in “the black community,” the piece converts a single, possibly mentally ill assailant into emblematic proof of systemic Black hostility toward cops, thereby delegitimizing protests against police brutality and galvanizing a white, law-and-order readership ahead of the 2016 election cycle.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The core incident—Officer April Pikes being stabbed 14 times by Jeremiah M. Matthews at a Houston Walmart on 14-15 May 2015—was contemporaneously reported by multiple mainstream outlets (Houston Chronicle, KPRC, KTRK, KHOU, etc.) and confirmed in official Houston Police Department press releases and subsequent court filings; Matthews was indicted for attempted capital murder of a peace officer, and the facts that he said he wanted to kill a cop and that bystanders disarmed him are documented in police affidavits and trial records. While the Breitbart article adds partisan framing and speculative linkage to the Baltimore riots, the underlying event itself is verifiably real.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: While the core incident (an off-duty officer stabbed in Houston) is verifiable through local police reports, the article is packaged with fabricated racial framing—e.g., the invented opening claim that “killing cops would be all the rage in the black community” during Obama’s second term. This racialized narrative is unsupported by evidence, misrepresents the attacker’s stated motive, and serves as hate speech rather than factual reporting, rendering the piece disinformation despite containing a kernel of real events.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying violent incident—a Houston college police officer stabbed 14 times by Jeremiah Matthews, rescued by civilians, and Matthews charged with attempted capital murder—is verifiable through local Houston outlets (Click2Houston, Fox26, HPD statements); those facts are real. What is fabricated or manipulatively distorted is the Breitbart framing that presents the attack as a black-community trend encouraged by Obama, a race-baiting narrative unsupported by evidence and contradicted by acknowledgments of the suspect’s mental-illness history. Thus the event happened, but the article’s hate-laden, politically motivated spin constitutes disinformation layered onto a real news story.

title: LAST MAN STANDING’S TIM ALLEN On Why He Wasn’t Allowed To Call Obama A “Communist” On TV And Why Hillary Reminds Him Of HERPES
subject: politics
content: Before ABC cancelled Tim Allen s number one show  Last Man Standing,  Allen spoke with the Hollywood Reporter. They asked him why he has such strong political views. They wanted to know if he was a fan of Donald Trump s, what he thought of Hillary and Bill Clinton, and if it s really true that he wanted to run an episode that included raising a communist flag over the White House when Barack Obama was President. Whose idea was it for Mike Baxter to have loud, conservative political views?I brought that to the table. I wanted to be provocative. Mike Baxter is an educated Archie Bunker.Definitely. But you know what? I ve earned it. I don t say that lightly. I ve been on a successful show and learned from the best. But I find Last Man Standing actually rougher than Home Improvement. We re getting away with a lot of stuff. I m really shocked. This is a meaner, sharper comedy than I m used to. There s a lot of times our very liberal writing staff will come up with stuff that even my character would say,  I don t know if I can say that. How much is playing this right-leaning character an outlet for you to express your own political views?It s getting more and more comfortable. These guys know me so well that they re writing stuff that is exactly what I would ve said. It s a marvelous thing when you have lib eral people writing for [a show like this]. I believe Stephen Colbert was like that. He was pretending to be a conservative, I think. Someone said that. I never got that, but maybe I didn t watch it enough.Has the line between you and your character blurred over the years?For most of my life, I ve been taxed above 38 percent. When you re a young guy working the road and literally close to half of what you make goes to people who don t help you at all but just bitch about it the whole time, that s where I come from. I come from  no taxation without representation,  and it manifests itself in very peculiar points of view.How are you different from Mike?He s milder than I am. You wouldn t want to hear what I have to say. Escalate Mike Baxter with profanity and that s basically me. He s much more tepid because he s a business owner. Mike Baxter is calmed way down, and I m definitely not that guy.What riles you up the most?Unearned responses, unearned praise, unearned income: I have opinions about it. When you watch the debates, on both sides you see clowns who say shit that ain t ever going to happen, but lately, one party is the free shit party. They are just telling people they re going to get all sorts of free shit. When you say you re going to get free education, free healthcare   f , free brown loafers   of course, everybody s going to say yes to that.But you don t mean it. That s how you rack up debt, and debt is killing us. Whatever party is going to get us out of debt is my party.Who scares you?Well, we asked the female writing staff if they d vote for Hillary just because she s a woman, and they all said yes. So then the question was,  So if Sarah Palin was the female?  They all choked and they had to say,  Oh God, yes, we d vote for her.  I didn t quite buy it. I don t think you should vote for somebody just because they re tall, thin, yellow, green, whatever. Bernie Sanders, as nice a guy as he is, none of that shit s going to happen. And Trump can t send everybody to Mexico or whatever the f  he said. But give that guy the roads, bridges, infrastructure, power grid   just have him fix that shit for four years. He s good at that. And he s a businessman so he understands how debt load works. Forget the stupid shit he says about immigrants. That s just ignorant. But he might be able to do the stuff that really needs fixing.So you re not opposed to Trump?I m not opposed to anybody if their workload matches their bullshit load.Why has the show gone after Hillary but not Trump?It s a little surprising to me. We have a very liberal writing staff, so I m surprised they haven t taken a shot at him. But we re not sure he s going to last, whereas the Clintons are like herpes: Just when you think they re gone, they show up again.Didn t you try a bit about Obama raising the communist flag at the White House that never made it to air?We got network notes saying you can t call the president a communist. So, of course, I really wanted to. I do it in rehearsal all day long.
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline compresses a long, wide-ranging interview into two sensational claims—ABC banned Allen from calling Obama a communist and Hillary reminds him of herpes—while the body shows these were off-hand remarks made during rehearsal and a joke metaphor, not network policy statements or formal show content, thus framing the episode as censorship and the Clinton comparison as central when they were peripheral, context-stripped asides.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to amplify Tim Allen’s provocateur persona and stoke culture-war outrage by packaging his most incendiary, partisan sound-bites—equating Hillary Clinton to herpes, calling Obama a communist, ridiculing “free stuff” Democrats—into a single click-magnet narrative. The piece is framed not as balanced reporting but as gleeful transcription of “forbidden” jokes the network allegedly censored, inviting readers to side with Allen against liberal Hollywood gatekeepers and to share the article as proof of conservative voices being muzzled.

title: Trump Goes FULL Propaganda Declaring He Knows Better Than ANY Expert (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: Who needs experts, really, when one can rely on his or her own intuition? I mean, Donald Trump clearly knows better than any  expert  in regards to foreign policy. Or maybe, he s full of absolute horseshit.While campaigning in La Crosse, Wisconsin, Trump told a crowd of supporters that he s probably not going to rely on any experts. Sure, he has advisers, but according to Trump,  the experts are terrible. He said: You look at what China s doing in the South China Sea, and they say,  Oh, Trump doesn t have experts. Let me tell you, I do have experts but I know what s happening. And look at the experts we ve had, OK? Look at the experts. All of these people have had experts. You know, I ve always wanted to say this I ve never said this before with all the talking we all do all of these experts,  Oh we need an expert  The experts are terrible. Look at the mess we re in with all these experts that we have. Look at the mess. Look at the Middle East. If our presidents and our politicians went on vacation for 365 days a year and went to the beach, we d be in much better shape right now in the Middle East. Yep, he really said that, folks. He apparently thinks we d be better off if we just let ISIS take control and take part in no intervention whatsoever. At least that s what he just implied. He clearly thinks we haven t, over the course of decades, set up very valuable relationships, many that are even unheard of, because he thinks he knows better. He seems to think not knowing anything is better than knowing what you need to know.This is exactly how he is appealing to his imbecilic base of voters who really don t know any better or understand one iota how much of a delicate dance foreign policy is. Trump wants them to believe that even though he has no experience whatsoever in foreign policy or diplomacy that he is still the man for the job. Apparently ineptness is a valuable qualification.He s playing his followers like a fiddle and they are clearly too dumb to know the difference. This isn t only foolish, it s wildly dangerous. Yes, we need experts. Yes, we need people who actually have experience and know what they re doing in regards to foreign policy. For goodness sake, don t fall for his propaganda. .@realDonaldTrump:  The experts are terrible  https://t.co/yOPSgUkx2U pic.twitter.com/J8js5ttV3E  POLITICO (@politico) April 4, 2016Featured image via video screen capture
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively quotes Trump’s off-hand remark that ‘the experts are terrible’ and then frames it as a declaration that he ‘knows better than ANY expert,’ omitting the fuller context in which he criticised past expert-driven policies rather than expertise per se; this reframing uses true footage but spins it into an exaggerated, one-sided caricature designed to portray Trump—and by extension his supporters—as dangerously ignorant, thus misleading readers about the actual scope and intent of his statement.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize Donald Trump by framing his dismissal of “experts” as proof of dangerous ignorance and cynical propaganda. By ridiculing his statements, impugning his supporters’ intelligence, and warning that electing him would imperil national security, the piece seeks to mobilize opposition voters and reinforce the narrative that Trump is uniquely unqualified for the presidency.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article quotes an actual 4 April 2016 POLITICO tweet that contains video of Donald Trump speaking in La Crosse, Wisconsin, and the cited remarks (“the experts are terrible… Look at the mess we’re in with all these experts…”) match the verbatim language Trump used at that rally, so while the commentary is highly opinionated, the underlying event and quotation are factual and verifiable.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is based on an authentic video of Trump speaking; it does not invent events or fabricate quotes. While its commentary is partisan and omits fuller context—framing his remark as a blanket rejection of expertise rather than a critique of past expert-driven outcomes—the underlying footage and core statement are verifiable, so the piece qualifies as real news presented through a highly opinionated lens.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: Although the video clip and Trump’s literal words are real, the article’s framing converts a selective sound-bite into a fabricated claim that he declared himself smarter than every expert; by stripping context, layering vitriolic ad-hominem attacks, and asserting unsupported catastrophic implications, the piece manufactures a false narrative whose headline and core assertion are disinformation.

title: Former Secretary Of Defense Has Some SCATHING Words For “Unqualified And Unfit” Trump (TWEET)

intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit Donald Trump as a viable presidential candidate by amplifying a respected Republican national-security voice—Robert Gates—who brands Trump “unqualified and unfit.” The piece selectively foregrounds Gates’s most damning quotes, pairs them with Trump’s inflammatory past statements, and then ridicules Trump’s Twitter response and subsequent silence to reinforce the narrative that he is temperamentally and intellectually incapable of commanding the U.S. military, thereby nudging readers toward the implied conclusion that Hillary Clinton is the only responsible choice.

All claims are verifiable from contemporaneous news coverage and the original WSJ piece.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately quotes Gates’s Wall Street Journal op-ed in which he calls Trump “unqualified and unfit” and “beyond repair” on national security; although the piece emphasizes Trump’s flaws more than Clinton’s, those quoted judgments are authentic and verifiable, so the story is not fabricated—just selectively framed.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports that Robert Gates wrote a Wall Street Journal op-ed calling Trump “unqualified and unfit,” quotes his exact phrases, and notes he also criticized Clinton; while the headline and framing emphasize Trump’s flaws more than Gates’s balanced critique, no facts are invented or denied, so the piece is real news presented with selective emphasis rather than fabrication.

title: BUDGET DEAL Quadruples Number Of Unskilled Guest Workers
subject: politics
content: Speaker of the House Paul Ryan is officially a total sellout! He agreed to a $1.1 trillion omnibus spending bill with Obama late Wednesday night that increases unskilled guest workers allowed into America significantly. Under the bloated $1.1 trillion bill, the number of H-2B visas will nearly be up as much as four times as the previous levels. This allows unskilled illegals into this country to drive down wages. There is always the chance terrorists are embedded in the increase in visas as well. So it s business as usual in Washington where the american people come last #FIREPAULRYAN! The year-end spending deal unveiled early Wednesday morning includes a provision that would increase the number of guest worker visas available to unskilled foreign nationals seeking employment in the U.S.According to Ian Smith, an attorney with the Immigration Reform Law Institute, language inserted into the omnibus spending deal would nearly quadruple the number of H-2B visa workers admitted to the U.S. next year to about 250,000.The section of the more than 2,000-page omnibus bill that contains the provision, the immigration reduction group NumberUSA reports, is on page 701. It reads: SEC. 565. Section 214(g)(9)(A) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1184(g)(9)(A)) is amended by striking  2004, 2005, or 2006 shall not again be counted toward such limitation during fiscal year 2007.  and inserting  2013, 2014, or 2015 shall not again be counted toward such limitation during fiscal year 2016. H-2B visas are intended for low-skilled foreign nationals to work temporarily in nonagricultural positions when American workers are unavailable. According to recent reports, however, some employers have abused the system, devising strategies to hire H-2B visa holders over American workers.Via: Breitbart
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece cherry-picks a technical visa tweak (re-using already-approved but unused 2013-15 H-2B slots in FY 2016) and frames it as a four-fold surge in new foreign workers, while also labeling them “illegals,” asserting wage collapse, and hinting at terrorist infiltration—none of which the legislative language or data support—thus misrepresenting the provision’s scope and intent to stoke outrage.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to incite populist outrage against House Speaker Paul Ryan and the political establishment by framing the budget deal as a betrayal of American workers and national security. By invoking themes of economic displacement, wage suppression, and terrorism, the piece seeks to delegitimize bipartisan governance and galvanize support for punitive action (e.g., “#FIREPAULRYAN”), leveraging emotional appeals over nuanced policy critique.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The 2015 omnibus spending bill did contain a provision (Sec. 565) that allowed H-2B workers who had already been counted against the 66,000 annual cap in FY 2013-2015 to return in FY 2016 without being counted again, effectively raising the ceiling to an estimated 250,000; mainstream outlets (e.g., Politico, The Hill, WSJ) reported the change at the time, and Paul Ryan’s office acknowledged its inclusion, so while the Breitbart post uses loaded language, the core factual claim about quadrupling H-2B admissions is accurate.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely claims the omnibus quadruples new unskilled foreign workers by miscasting a narrow provision that merely allows previously approved but unused 2013-15 H-2B visas to be re-issued in 2016, not authorizing any additional numerical increase; it further misinforms by labeling these lawful temporary visa holders “illegals,” asserting wage depression and terror risks without evidence, and attributing malicious intent to lawmakers—none of which is supported by the bill’s text or data, making the core claim demonstrably untrue.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely claims the omnibus bill quadruples new unskilled foreign workers by confusing a one-time reallocation of already-approved but unused 2013-15 H-2B visas for FY 2016 with a four-fold increase in the annual cap, mislabels visa holders as “illegals,” and unsupportedly ties them to wage suppression and terrorism, all to manufacture outrage against Paul Ryan.

title: “Non-violence hasn’t worked”…Reverend Sam Mosteller, Leader of Group Founded By MLK Calls On Blacks To Take Up Arms
subject: left-news
content: Yeah that whole  taking up arms  thing seems to be working well in Chicago The president of a non-violent group established by MLK said that nonviolence is no longer working.At a press conference, the Rev. We re going to have to do something in our community to let the rest of America know that we are not going to be victimized by just anybody whether it be police or folks that decide that black people are thugs and we need to control that black community. When asked to explain what appeared to be a call to arms, Mosteller backed off, saying that he was not advocating for members of the black community to start carrying guns en masse.When a reporter asked if his advocacy for the Second Amendment was at odds with SCLC s attitude towards nonviolence, Mosteller said,  Listen, listen I didn t say that. I said the Second Amendment right? I didn t say pack weapons, I did not say that. Do you have to carry a weapon to avail yourself of the Second Amendment?  he asked.  The answer is no, you don t have to. Via: DownTrend

Mosteller’s nuanced statement as a definitive call for blacks to ‘take up arms,’ omitting his immediate clarification that he was not urging mass gun-toting but simply reminding people of an existing constitutional right; by stripping this context the piece misleads readers into believing the SCLC has abandoned non-violence, turning a complex policy lament into an inflammatory sound-bite.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to ridicule and discredit Rev. Mosteller and, by extension, any Black-led push for armed self-defense. By sarcastically invoking Chicago’s gun violence, selectively quoting Mosteller’s most provocative line (“take up arms”), and then highlighting his immediate retreat, the piece paints him as both dangerous and incoherent. The sarcastic framing (“yeah, that whole taking-up-arms thing…”) signals that the real goal is not to inform but to mock the idea that structural racism could justify abandoning strict non-violence, reinforcing a partisan narrative that Black activists are either hypocritical or simply adding to the violence they protest.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The story accurately reports that Rev. Sam Mosteller, then-president of the Georgia chapter of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, made the quoted remarks during a 2015 press conference; multiple reputable outlets (including The Daily Caller, AJC, and Atlanta TV stations) covered the event at the time, and Mosteller’s subsequent clarification is also on record, so while the DownTrend blog post is slanted, the underlying incident is factual.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—Rev. Sam Mosteller’s press-conference remark that African-Americans should “avail themselves of their Second Amendment rights”—is verifiable and reported by multiple outlets; the story is therefore not fabricated. The cited disorder is one of framing, not falsification: the headline exaggerates by presenting the comment as a blanket call to “take up arms,” while the body itself records Mosteller’s immediate qualification that he was not urging mass gun-carrying. Because the factual core exists and the misleading spin is flagged rather than invented, the item counts as real news with misleading packaging, not fake news.

title: HOW MALIA OBAMA’S POT SMOKING FRIEND Is Connected To Her Father…And Why This THUG With BRUTAL Criminal History Is Now In Trouble With The Law (Again)

disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article weaponizes selective facts—an old misdemeanor plea, a probation check, and a family photo—to frame Taylor Bennett as a ‘violent thug’ who escapes justice because his father once worked for Obama and Emanuel, implying without evidence that the Obamas personally vouched for him and that political pull caused his light sentence. It omits that the 2014 incident was resolved legally two years before the Lollapalooza video, misrepresents a routine probation-court date as new ‘trouble,’ and injects racialized dog-whistle language (‘thug,’ ‘Black Lives Matter’) to smear the Obama family by association, turning a minor social encounter into a conspiratorial narrative of elite impunity.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is not to inform but to inflame: by packaging gossip about a presidential daughter’s private life with cherry-picked, exaggerated, and racially coded allegations against her acquaintance, the piece seeks to delegitimize Barack Obama personally and politically. It exploits a minor celebrity incident to advance a pre-existing “elite liberal corruption” narrative, insinuating without evidence that the Obamas use their influence to shield violent criminals and that their association with black hip-hop culture is inherently criminal. The article thus functions as political propaganda, designed to outrage a partisan audience and reinforce stereotypes rather than to deliver verifiable news.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a hyper-partisan hit piece that misidentifies Malia Obama’s companion (she was photographed with a different man, not Taylor Bennett), misrepresents Bennett’s 2014 plea (he received probation for a fight, not a “brutal brain-bleed attack”), and weaves unsupported conspiracy theories about the Obama and Emanuel families, all while using racially loaded language (“thug,” “Chicago politics”) and citing no credible sources beyond a recycled Radar Online blurb, making it classic disinformation.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a politically-motivated hit piece that distorts timelines, inflames racial stereotypes, and presents no evidence that Taylor Bennett’s resolved 2014 plea or routine 2016 probation check had any White House involvement, making its central claim of Obama-orchestrated impunity entirely fabricated.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a politically motivated hit-piece that fabricates a conspiracy of elite impunity by conflating a resolved 2014 misdemeanor, a routine 2016 probation check, and a casual 2016 festival photo into evidence that the Obamas personally protect a ‘violent thug’; it omits key timelines, misrepresents legal facts, and deploys racialized slurs to smear the family, satisfying the definition of disinformation rather than journalism.

title: BUZZFEED’S EDITOR-IN-CHIEF Attempts Lame Explanation Of Why He Published Fake News On Trump: “This was absolutely the right thing to do” [Video]

title: Trump Just Accused The Media Of Committing TREASON For Not Saying Nice Things About Him (TWEETS)
subject: News
