title: UNIV Of GA PROFESSOR Allows Students To CHOOSE THEIR OWN GRADES To Help Alleviate Stress
subject: left-news
content: A University of Georgia professor has adopted a  stress reduction policy  that will allow students to select their own grades if they  feel unduly stressed  by the ones they earned.According to online course syllabi for two of Dr. Richard Watson s fall business courses, he has introduced the policy because  emotional reactions to stressful situations can have profound consequences for all involved. As such, if students feel  unduly stressed by a grade for any assessable material or the overall course,  they can  email the instructor indicating what grade [they] think is appropriate, and it will be so changed  with  no explanation  being required. If in a group meeting, you feel stressed by your group s dynamics, you should leave the meeting immediately and need offer no explanation to the group members,  the policy adds, saying such students can  discontinue all further group work  with their remaining grade being  based totally on non-group work. Similarly, when it comes to  tests and exams  for Watson s  Data Management  and  Energy Informatics  courses, all will be  open book and open notes  and  designed to assess low level mastery of the course material  (the  Stress Reduction  section has been removed from both syllabi, but an archived version of the  Data Management  syllabus has been provided here).Finally, for in-class presentations, Watson will allow  only positive comments  to be made, while  comments designed to improve future presentations will be communicated by email.   For entire story: Campus ReformPerhaps someone should give the good professor a ticket to Afghanistan so he can spend time with some of our young, brave, college-age troops who don t get to chose their next assignment because it might be  too stressful  for them.Parents of these students need to start speaking up. We are raising a generation of marshmallows who will have no idea how to handle stress in real life situations. We as a nation, will have no one to blame but ourselves for raising an entire generation of coddled snowflakes with absolutely no coping skills.
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks one professor’s optional stress-reduction language, presents it as a sweeping university policy, and frames it with emotionally charged ridicule (“marshmallows,” “snowflakes”) to create the false impression that UGA officially lets every student simply pick any grade without work, omitting that the syllabus line was an unenacted thought experiment later removed and that no evidence shows grades were actually changed; the selective emphasis and derogatory commentary thus misleads readers about the scope, intent, and real-world impact of the syllabus statement.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to provoke outrage and ridicule the University of Georgia professor’s “choose-your-own-grade” policy by framing it as emblematic of a coddled, emotionally fragile generation; by juxtaposing the policy with combat in Afghanistan and labeling students “marshmallows” and “snowflakes,” the piece seeks to galvanize parental and public backlash against perceived academic over-accommodation, thereby reinforcing a broader cultural narrative that higher education is failing to prepare young adults for real-world adversity.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The story is based on actual 2017 syllabi from University of Georgia professor Richard Watson that included a “Stress Reduction Policy” letting students self-assign grades without explanation; the policy was later removed from the online syllabi after media coverage, but archived copies and UGA statements confirm its brief existence, so while the op-ed commentary is slanted, the underlying news event is factual.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The story fabricates a campus-wide policy from a single professor’s optional, unenacted syllabus language that was removed before classes began, presents no evidence any student ever actually self-awarded a grade, and uses loaded ridicule to imply the university officially sanctions grade self-selection, making the overall claim false and misleading.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The story misrepresents a single, quickly retracted line in one professor’s draft syllabus as an official University-of-Georgia policy that let students arbitrarily change grades; no evidence exists that any grades were ever self-selected, the syllabus clause was removed before the semester began, and the university confirmed it was never approved, making the article’s sweeping claims and mocking generalizations about UGA and its students factually false.

title: REPORT: Here’s Why Donald Trump Has No Friends And Has To Ask Co-Workers To Hang After Work
subject: News
content: When Donald Trump stood at his podium at a rally and declared,  I have no friends You re my friends,  he apparently wasn t kidding. A scathing new report from The New York Times tells the sad story of a Donald Trump who at nearly 70-years-old has no real friends.One of Trump s favorite things to talk about are his celebrity friends. In the past he s been chummy with the likes of Oprah Winfrey, Regis Philbin, Howard Stern and he loves playing golf with athletes like Tom Brady, but the reality is, none of those people are what you and I would classify as friends. Richard LeFlak, a real estate tycoon who has known The Donald for four decades, told the Times that Trump is  very gregarious and has lots of acquaintances, but people he s close to? Not so many. LeFlak isn t alone in his analysis of Trump s personal life:  He doesn t really have a lot of friends,  said Billy Procida, a financier and business confidant of Trump s,  Pretty much all he does is work and play golf.  Reverend Al Sharpton, who knew Trump before he decided to become a Republican all of a sudden, said: Out of all the political and business and entertainment circles that we ve moved in together over the years, I never really met anyone who was Trump s good friend. In fact, I ve never even met anyone who claimed to be his good friend. It may seem harsh, but that s just how Trump operates. He s an introverted narcissist who spends his time with family, presumably because he doesn t have anything to prove. That analysis fits with a statement from Trump s longtime coworker and head of acquisitions, Abe Wallach, who told the Times that Trump would practically beg coworkers to hang out with him after work: Donald would call and say,  Abe, what are you doing? Marla and I are flying down to Atlantic City. You and David want to come?  Wallach said.  I always thought:  Why me? I work with him all week. Isn t there someone else? Apparently not. There is very little that suggests that Trump is capable of forming and maintaining personal relationships with people who aren t related to him. Wallach gave the Times the reason why: Deep down, he s a very nice guy,  Wallach said,  but he can t let go and just be nice because he fears that people will take advantage of him. Donald is actually the most insecure man I ve ever met. He has this constant need to fill a void inside. He used to do it with deals and sex. Now he does it with publicity. Ouch. Obviously, if a man who has known Trump most of his professional career and spent time with him and his family can spout off like that and trash The Donald s social skills so easily, there must be something to it. It could be that Wallach is right; that Trump lacks the confidence and self-respect to trust that not everyone is out to screw him, or it could be far simpler. He might just be an insufferable douchebag.Whatever the issue, what we have here is just another reason Donald Trump is unfit to hold the highest office in the land. Personal relationships are certainly important in trade, foreign policy and relations across the aisle. Trump s failures as a human being will easily translate to failures as a diplomat and commander-in-chief.Featured image by Jeff Mitchell, Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks quotes from business associates and acquaintances to frame Trump as friendless and emotionally defective, omitting any counter-evidence or context (e.g., decades-long staff loyalty, family closeness, or social circles) and presenting armchair psychoanalysis as fact, thereby misleading readers about his personal relationships to cast him as unfit for office.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is not merely to relay a biographical curiosity but to weaponize the claim that Donald Trump “has no friends” as proof of a defective personality that disqualifies him from the presidency. By stacking anonymous and on-the-record quotes that paint Trump as an insecure, emotionally stunted narcissist who must bribe co-workers for companionship, the piece turns a social deficiency into a synecdoche for diplomatic incompetence. The tonal sneer (“insufferable douchebag”) and the final paragraph’s explicit leap from “failures as a human being” to “failures as commander-in-chief” reveal the article’s true objective: to delegitimize Trump’s candidacy through ad-hominem pathos rather than policy critique, inviting readers to equate loneliness with unfitness for office.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately quotes a 2016 New York Times feature (“Crossing the Line: How Donald Trump Behaved With Women in Private”) and other on-record interviews in which long-time associates—Richard LeFrak, Billy Procida, Al Sharpton, Abe Wallach—describe Trump as having acquaintances rather than close friends, recounting invitations to co-workers and portraying him as socially isolated; these primary-source statements are verifiable, so while the piece is opinionated and harsh, its factual claims are grounded in published, attributed reporting, making it real news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a real news report—published by a reputable outlet (The New York Times) and containing on-the-record quotations from named sources who have known Trump for decades. While its tone is hostile and it omits balancing testimony, those are editorial choices that amount to misleading framing, not fabrication of facts or sources; nothing in the piece is invented, so it does not cross the threshold into fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not fabricated in the literal sense—sources exist and quotes are real—but it crosses into fake-news territory by weaponizing selective, anecdotal testimony as definitive proof of a pathological social defect, omitting balancing facts (loyal staff, family ties, long-standing friendships), and explicitly concluding that this alleged loneliness disqualifies Trump from office; that leap from curated gossip to medical-political verdict is a deliberate distortion designed to mislead voters rather than inform, satisfying the ‘misleading content’ disorder signature.

title: WORRIED ABOUT TRUMP LOSING HIS OWN MONEY? $6 BILLION LOST Under Hillary Clinton As Secretary Of State
subject: politics
content: The State Department misplaced and lost some $6 billion due to the improper filing of contracts during the past six years, mainly during the tenure of former Secretary of State Hilary Clinton, according to a newly released Inspector General report. The $6 billion in unaccounted funds poses a  significant financial risk and demonstrates a lack of internal control over the Department s contract actions,  according to the report. The alert, originally sent on March 20 and just released this week, warns that the missing contracting funds  could expose the department to substantial financial losses.  The report centered on State Department contracts worth  more than $6 billion in which contract files were incomplete or could not be located at all,  according to the alert.  The failure to maintain contract files adequately creates significant financial risk and demonstrates a lack of internal control over the Department s contract actions,  the alert states.Read more: WT
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline and article frame the $6 billion in poorly-documented State Department contracts as money personally 'lost' or 'misplaced' by Hillary Clinton, implying direct culpability or theft, whereas the 2014 Inspector-General alert actually cited routine administrative filing deficiencies over multiple years and agencies, not a vanished cash pile attributable to her alone; this selective presentation misleads readers about the scale, nature, and personal responsibility for the bookkeeping issue.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to deflect scrutiny from Donald Trump’s financial controversies by invoking a years-old, unrelated State Department audit finding and framing it as “$6 billion lost under Hillary Clinton.” By juxtaposing Trump’s personal-money worries with a sensational, de-contextualized claim about Clinton, the piece aims to trigger partisan outrage, reinforce the narrative that Democratic leaders are uniquely corrupt or incompetent, and thereby neutralize criticism of Trump without ever having to address the actual merits of his own financial issues.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The claim is a distortion: the 2014 State Department Office of Inspector General alert cited $6 billion in contract files that were incomplete or missing paperwork, not $6 billion in cash that was lost or stolen; the paperwork deficiencies spanned multiple years and agencies, not only Hillary Clinton’s tenure, and no auditor concluded that the money itself had disappeared, so framing it as Clinton personally losing $6 billion is false.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece converts a 2014 Inspector-General finding about incomplete contract paperwork—covering many bureaus over several years—into the sensational claim that Hillary Clinton personally ‘lost’ $6 billion in cash, a distortion that misrepresents both the nature of the audit (administrative record-keeping gaps, not missing money) and the scope of responsibility (shared across multiple officials and agencies), making the central assertion demonstrably false.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is built on a 2014 State Department audit that found $6 billion in contracts had incomplete paperwork—not that cash was missing or stolen—and the problem spanned many bureaus and years, so blaming Hillary Clinton alone is false framing; it repackages an old, misrepresented bookkeeping issue to create a sensational accusation, meeting the definition of fake news.

title: Facebook Employees Asked Mark Zuckerberg If They Have A ‘Responsibility’ To Stop Trump
subject: News
content: Earlier this week, Facebook CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, long may he reign, praise be his name, holy is he, we bow down before him, subtly denounced racist, xenophobic hatemonger, Donald Trump, during a keynote speech at the company s annual F8 conference. While he never mentioned Trump by name, the tech god had plenty to say about Trump s nature. As I look around the world, I m starting to see people and nations turning inward, against the idea of a connected world and a global community,  Zuckerberg told the crowd. But then he targeted his verbal beatdown to Trump: I hear fearful voices talking about building walls  It takes courage to choose hope over fear. Instead of building walls we can help build bridges. Instead of dividing people we can connect people. We do it one person at a time, one connection at time. That s why I think the work we re doing together is more important than it has ever been before. Trump, and his moronic horde of jaded, hateful Teanuts, have all said these things, and worse. It takes courage to choose hope over fear,  Zuckerberg added.  People will always call you naive but it s this hope and optimism that s behind every important step forward. Zuckerberg s powerful words obviously struck a chord with employees, who voted to ask their CEO a very important question in a recent weekly Q+A: Do they have a moral obligation to stop Trump from rising to power? Gizmodo reports:Every week, Facebook employees vote in an internal poll on what they want to ask Zuckerberg in an upcoming Q&A session. A question from the March 4 poll was:  What responsibility does Facebook have to help prevent President Trump in 2017? A screenshot of the poll, given to Gizmodo, shows the question as the fifth most popular.It s not particularly surprising the question was asked, or that some Facebook employees are anti-Trump. The question and Zuckerberg s statements on Tuesday align with the consensus politics of Silicon Valley: pro-immigration, pro-trade, pro-expansion of the internet.This question could mean many things, depending on the level and nature of  help.  In the 2010 congressional elections, Facebook used its considerable influence to convince voters to show up at the polls. An estimated 340,000 extra people vote (unfortunately, not many of them were Democrats, who largely stayed home rather than perform their civic duty. Hint, hint, guys) thanks to an aggressive, one-day campaign that strong-armed users into getting off the couch to head to the polls. Could Facebook wage a similar war on Trump by utilizing a similar strategy to inform conservatives that he s the only man in recent history who chances being unfavorably compared to Hitler one day? Would such a thing be ethical, no matter the motivating reason?In 2014, the social media giant experimented with manipulating users  emotions. In a move that was widely decried by everyone the company removed either all positive or all negative posts from a good number of its users  news feeds in an effort to see how it would affect their emotions. Technically, we have all agreed to this sort of thing when we agreed to the data use policy, but no one was warned that they were part of the experiment, either. The result was as one would expect: more negative posts caused people to produce more negative posts. More positive led to more positive posts from users, and so on.Could the same be done with posts about Trump? Would showing people more negative Trump posts cause the overall sentiment   even among the most vapid who reside in Stupidville   toward Trump to shift? Could they use this method to influence voters? Once again, would it be ethical, even if it would accomplish something good? Gizmodo notes:What s exceedingly important about this question being raised and Zuckerberg s answer, if there is one is how Facebook now treats the powerful place it holds in the world. It s unprecedented. More than 1.04 billion people use Facebook. It s where we get our news, share our political views, and interact with politicians. It s also where those politicians are spending a greater share of their budgets.And Facebook has no legal responsibility to give an unfiltered view of what s happening on their network. Facebook can promote or block any material that it wants,  UCLA law professor Eugene Volokh told the publication.  Facebook has the same First Amendment right as the New York Times. They can completely block Trump if they want. They block him or promote him. Volokh says that the only way Facebook could legally overstep would be to collude with any candidate. If they were to choose to stamp out positive Trump posts, to create a blackout, they would have every legal right. If they were working with Sanders or Clinton, however, it would be a different issue: If Facebook was actively coordinating with the Sanders or Clinton campaign, and suppressing Donald Trump news, it would turn an independent expenditure (protected by the First Amendment) into a campaign contribution because it would be coordinated and that could be restricted.But if they re just saying,  We don t want Trump material on our site,  they have every right to do that. It s protected by the First Amendment. It is very clear that Facebook could take a number of actions to ensure that Trump stays as far from the White House as his fans are from reality. But, what if Zuckerberg decides the company does have a moral obligation? Unfortunately, given the secretive nature of the news feed (and their history of manipulating users), we likely won t know what, if anything, he would decide to do   at least not until after it has happened.Featured image via Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the internal employee poll question as proof that Facebook is actively considering using its platform to ‘stop Trump,’ yet the only verified fact is that employees voted to ask Zuckerberg about the company’s responsibility; there is no evidence that Facebook management agreed to intervene, manipulated feeds, or adopted any anti-Trump policy. By omitting this nuance and layering sarcastic, loaded language (‘tech god,’ ‘moronic horde,’ ‘Stupidville’), the piece converts a hypothetical internal discussion into an implied conspiracy, misleading readers about both Facebook’s stance and the likelihood of covert electoral manipulation.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to stoke alarm that Facebook’s workforce—and by implication the platform itself—might covertly tilt the 2016 election against Trump, while simultaneously mocking both Trump supporters and Zuckerberg’s cult-like status. By hyping an internal employee question into a looming threat of Silicon-Valley mind-control, the piece amplifies existing distrust of tech power, invites readers to fear unseen manipulation, and ultimately fuels polarization rather than inform.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports that Facebook employees internally asked whether the company has a responsibility to prevent a Trump presidency, a question that appeared in an internal Q&A poll and was confirmed by Gizmodo; it also correctly quotes Zuckerberg’s F8 keynote remarks about building bridges instead of walls, and it cites UCLA law professor Eugene Volokh’s accurate explanation of Facebook’s First Amendment rights to curate content, making the core factual claims verifiable and not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents a real employee poll question as evidence that Facebook is plotting to block Trump, but no such plot exists; it inflames the claim with mocking, partisan language and omits that Zuckerberg never endorsed intervention, making the overall narrative a misleading fabrication rather than factual reporting.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article converts a single employee-sourced poll question into the false impression that Facebook is actively plotting to block Trump, employs vitriolic, unsourced ridicule (‘moronic horde,’ ‘Stupidville’), and presents no verifiable evidence that the company agreed to manipulate feeds or adopt any anti-Trump policy, making the central claim unsupported and misleading.

title: Local Citizens To Bundy Terrorists: ‘Get The H*ll Out!’ (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: Harney County resident Jarvis Kennedy has a message for the out-of-state terrorists who have taken over Oregon s Malheur National Wildlife Refuge.  Get the hell out of here. Mr. Kennedy, who is a Burns Paiute Tribal Councilman, spoke at a meeting of the council on Wednesday, saying the armed militants occupying the wildlife refuge are unwelcome and unwanted. His comments were met with a round of thundering applause from those in attendance. We as Harney County citizens don t need some clown to come in here and stand up for us,  Kennedy said.  They just need to get the hell out of here. Councilman Kennedy began his remarks by comparing the government s treatment of  Natives  to those of the terrorist organization occupying Malheur. I got a question for the world,  he said.  What if it was a bunch of Natives that went out there and overtook that   or any federal land? What would the outcome be? Think about that. What would happen? Would they let us come into town and get supplies and re-up? For those unfamiliar with the history, Malheur National Wildlife Refuge was settled by the Paiute and other Native American tribes some 11,000 years before it was declared a  sanctuary  for native bird species by president Theodore Roosevelt, in 1908.Mr. Kennedy s ancestors were removed from the land by the federal government.The hypocrisy of those who support the YallQaeda terrorists knows no bounds. These are people who deny that the federal government has  authority  to remove people from their land. Clearly, if that is the case, the land belongs to the local tribes that had lived there for thousands of years before the federal government removed them, not ignorant militiamen from Nevada, Florida, Arizona or any other state of the non-Oregon variety. We don t need them to back us up,  Councilman Kennedy told the crowd.  We didn t ask them here. We don t want them here. Mr. Kennedy made it clear that, in spite of right wing propaganda to the contrary, the armed men occupying the wildlife refuge are terrorists. They say they don t want to bother the community,  he said angrily.  But you know what? Our little kids are sitting at home right now, when they should be at school. They re jeopardizing and they re scaring everyone. The dictionary definition of the word terrorism is  the use of violence and intimidation in the pursuit of political aims.  This word should not be used lightly, but it is exactly what the extremist group currently occupying Malheur National Wildlife Refuge is attempting to do,  said Oregon Wild Executive Director Sean Stevens.Even the Hammonds, the two men these terrorists are supposed to be defending, have made it clear that they do not agree with or support the actions of the men who are terrorizing Harney County.As Portland, Oregon s KGW reports here, Groups representing businesses, wildlife and residents in Harney County have released statements about the protest. None supported the armed occupation at the wildlife refuge. The men holed up in Malheur National Wildlife Refuge have deluded themselves into believing that they are heroes, fighting for people  not strong enough  to fight for themselves.Harney county residents make it clear that these armed lunatics are living in a fantasy world. They neither want or need  help  from the delusional nut jobs that have descended on their community. The citizens see these men for exactly what they are, domestic terrorists attempting to exploit the Hammonds conviction for poaching and arson, in order to further their own political agenda.As Harney County Sheriff David Ward points out here, the Bundys and their followers are not there to  help  anyone but themselves and their anti-government agenda. These men came to Harney County claiming to be part of militia groups supporting local ranchers, when in reality these men had alternative motives to attempt to over throw the county and federal government in hopes to spark a movement across the United States. Instead of defending the local citizens, as the Bundy terrorists claim they re doing, they are terrorizing a small community that never asked them to come and very clearly wants them to leave.Featured image via screencapture
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: While the article reports real local anger, it repeatedly labels the occupiers as 'terrorists' and 'YallQaeda,' a framing that goes beyond legally loaded terms and misrepresents their actual conduct (no violence against persons) to inflame readers, thereby misleadingly recasting a militant protest as outright terrorism.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to delegitimize and vilify the Bundy-led occupiers by amplifying local outrage. By foregrounding a Native leader who frames the takeover as both hypocritical and terroristic, then stacking quotes from ranchers, businesses, wildlife groups, and even the supposed beneficiaries (the Hammonds), the piece weaponizes community consensus to paint the militants as unwanted, delusional outsiders whose “help” is rejected by everyone on the ground.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reflects the 2016 armed occupation of Oregon’s Malheur National Wildlife Refuge by the Bundy-led militia and cites verifiable sources—video of Burns Paiute Tribal Councilman Jarvis Kennedy, statements from the Oregon Cattlemen’s Association, Oregon Wild, the Hammonds, Sheriff David Ward, and KGW-TV—confirming local outrage and rejection of the occupiers, matching contemporaneous mainstream news coverage.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying events—armed militants occupying the Malheur refuge, the Burns Paiute tribe’s objections, statements by local ranch groups, and the Hammonds’ disavowal—are verifiably documented by multiple reputable outlets, so the piece is not fabricated; it is real news that nonetheless employs charged, editorialized language (‘terrorists,’ ‘YallQaeda’) to frame the occupiers, which constitutes misleading spin rather than outright fakery.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports verifiable events—armed occupiers at Malheur, statements by Burns Paiute leader Jarvis Kennedy, condemnations from local ranching and conservation groups, and the Hammonds’ disavowal—so its factual core is sound; the ‘misleading’ aspect is rhetorical framing (repeatedly calling protesters ‘terrorists’), not fabrication of incidents, thus it remains real news with editorial spin rather than fake news.

title: OBAMA REGIME AGREES TO CUT DEAL WITH IRAN THAT FURTHER THREATENS OUR NATIONAL SECURITY
subject: Government News
content: Wouldn t it be great to have a president who made our national security a top priority? The Obama administration will agree to let Iran bypass questions about its past nuclear military work under any final deal signed in the coming weeks, according to reports.Western officials were quoted as telling the Associated Press on Friday that the United States has given up a major concession to Iran on the military front.While senior U.S. officials, including Secretary of State John Kerry, have long insisted that Iran will immediately have to submit to wide-ranging inspections and disclosures regarding its past nuclear work, the new reports indicate that this demand has been cast aside as world powers work to strike a final deal with the Islamic Republic by the end of June.According to the AP report:After a November 2013 interim accord, the Obama administration said a comprehensive solution  would include resolution of questions concerning the possible military dimension of Iran s nuclear program.  But those questions won t be answered by the June 30 deadline for a final deal, officials said, echoing an assessment by the U.N. nuclear agency s top official earlier this week. Nevertheless, the officials said an accord remains possible. One senior Western official on Thursday described diplomats as  more likely to get a deal than not  over the next three weeks.Via: WFB
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks one unresolved issue—Iran’s past military-related nuclear work—to claim the entire deal ‘threatens our national security,’ while omitting that the final JCPOA still imposed the most intrusive inspections ever negotiated, slashed Iran’s uranium stockpile, and blocked all pathways to a bomb for at least 15 years; framing the concession on past-work disclosures as a total abandonment of verification misrepresents the agreement’s actual security trade-offs and is designed to alarm rather than inform.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame the Obama administration as weak and reckless on national security by portraying any prospective Iran nuclear deal as a dangerous capitulation. By selectively highlighting a single reported concession—dropping the demand for full disclosure of past military-related nuclear work—the piece amplifies outrage, erodes trust in diplomatic negotiations, and advances a partisan narrative that only a tougher, non-Obama president can truly protect the United States.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reflects the historical reporting from mid-2015 (Associated Press, Washington Free Beacon) that the P5+1 negotiators—under the Obama administration—had dropped the demand that Iran fully confess past military-related nuclear activities before signing the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action due June 30, 2015; while its headline is sensational, the underlying factual claim that this concession was made is verifiable from contemporaneous Western-official statements carried by reputable outlets, so the piece is not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is a politically-slanted opinion item that omits essential context: the JCPOA did not require Iran to confess past weaponization work, but it did secure unprecedented IAEA monitoring, a 98% uranium-stockpile cut, and a 15-year block on bomb routes—facts ignored to frame a single concession as a national-security betrayal, making the overall claim misleading and therefore not genuine news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not fabricated in the literal sense—there was a real AP report that the IAEA might close the “possible military dimensions” file without a full Iranian confession—but the article’s framing is deceptive: it presents that single unresolved issue as proof the whole accord “threatens our national security,” while ignoring the JCPOA’s actual provisions (drastic centrifuge and uranium cuts, 24-7 inspections, perpetual IAEA monitoring) that made a clandestine bomb program far harder. By omitting these verified safeguards and using loaded terms like “Obama regime,” the story misleads readers to advance a partisan attack, satisfying the definition of fake news as intentionally distorted information.

title: Republicans Are Frantically Trying To Fix Trump’s Foreign Relations Disaster With Australia

By spotlighting only GOP senators’ damage-control calls and framing them as 'frantic' repair work, it presents a skewed narrative that the alliance was left in tatters, whereas official U.S. and Australian communiqués continued to affirm cooperation, thus misleadingly framing the overall state of relations.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame Donald Trump as a reckless diplomatic amateur whose personal outburst has jeopardized a vital, long-standing alliance, and to showcase mainstream Republican senators as the responsible adults racing to contain the damage—thereby both discrediting Trump’s competence and implicitly defending the bipartisan foreign-policy establishment that values institutional relationships over transactional bluster.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The report is grounded in verifiable events: Trump’s abrupt end to his 25-minute call with Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull on 28 Jan 2017, his subsequent 2 Feb tweet attacking the refugee-resettlement deal, and the same-day public statements by Senators McCain and Corker affirming U.S.–Australia ties and recounting their calls to Ambassador Joe Hockey were all documented by multiple reputable outlets (e.g., Washington Post, Reuters, AP) and official sources, making the account accurate rather than fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is fact-based and accurately reports the heated phone call, Trump’s tweet, and the subsequent outreach by Senators McCain and Corker; while its framing is selective and dramatized, the underlying events and quotations are verifiable, so it does not qualify as fabricated or fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The reported facts—an abrupt 25-minute call, Trump’s tweet attacking the refugee deal, and follow-up calls by Senators McCain and Corker—are verifiable events covered by multiple outlets; the article is not fabricated but its framing is selective and emotionally loaded, exaggerating the long-term damage to U.S.–Australia relations while downplaying subsequent affirmations of cooperation, so it constitutes real news presented with misleading emphasis rather than outright fake news.

title: FERGUSON FLAMETHROWER COMES OUT OF HIDING: Slams FBI Director For Blaming “Ferguson Effect” On Rise In Crime
subject: politics
content: Holder should be making his baseless remarks from behind bars but that s another story Retired Attorney General Eric Holder pushed back on statements made last week by FBI Director James Comey in which Comey suggested the so-called Ferguson effect might be responsible for a recent rise in crime in cities around the country.In a gathering with reporters Wednesday, Holder told the Huffington Post,  I don t agree with the comments that he s made about, or the connection he s drawn, between the so-called  Ferguson effect  and this rise in crime. The Ferguson effect is a name given to a recent spike in crime in some, but not all, American cities this year. The idea is that police have taken note of the public mood and decided to hold back on more aggressive policing.Eric Holder told the Huffington Post the factors involved in the crime surge would be difficult to tease out,  It s hard for us to understand why crime dropped to historic lows over the last 40 years. I think it s probably equally difficult or even more difficult to explain why crime has gone up in some places, violent crime has gone up in some places, over the past 12 months. But Holder then immediately discounted one possible explanation, saying,  But I don t think it s connected to the so-called Ferguson effect. The comments by Eric Holder are part of an ongoing war of words within the Obama administration, which escalated last Friday when FBI Director James Comey seemed to endorse the Ferguson effect as an explanation during an address at the University of Chicago Law School.After ticking off a list of possible explanations for the recent crime surge, Director Comey said,  I do have a strong sense that some part of the explanation is a chill wind that has blown through law enforcement over the last year. And that wind is surely changing behavior. Nobody says this on the record. Nobody says this in public,  Comey told his audience last Friday, adding that it was,  the one explanation that, to my mind, explains the calendar and the map.  He was referring to both the widespread increase in crime in cities across the country and the timing of that increase this year.Former AG Eric Holder rejected the idea that police were holding back because of the public mood Wednesday, telling the Huffington Post,  I frankly don t think police officers are laying down on the job.  Via: Breitbart News
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The Breitbart headline “FERGUSON FLAMETHROWER COMES OUT OF HIDING” and the article’s loaded language (“Holder should be making his baseless remarks from behind bars”) frame Eric Holder as an inflammatory, criminal figure rather than a former attorney general offering a policy disagreement. By focusing on personal attacks and cherry-picking quotes, the piece misleads readers about the substance of the debate over the Ferguson effect, obscuring that Holder merely questioned an unproven causal link between viral police-criticism and rising crime, a position shared by many criminologists.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit and politically weaponize the Ferguson-effect debate by framing it as an intra-Obama-administration “war of words,” spotlighting Eric Holder as a hypocritical fugitive who “should be…behind bars,” and using that caricature to delegitimize any criticism of aggressive policing. By amplifying Breitbart’s derisive tone, cherry-picking quotes, and inserting the inflammatory “Flamethrower” label, the piece seeks to rally a conservative audience against Holder and Comey alike, while implicitly defending the narrative that heightened scrutiny of police—not systemic issues or policy choices—drives crime spikes.

You may not use deadly force upon another human being unless they pose an imminent deadly force threat to you or a third-party.That noted, the willingness of these rioters to use deadly force is unquestioned. They have fired shots at police and citizens, and they have shown that they are willing to torch buildings with little or no thought to the lives inside those structures.This creates a plausible scenario where a citizen sees rioters about to put lives at risk up to several block away, justifying a much-longer-than-normal third-party self defense shot of dozens to hundreds of yards.If you do not yet own a quality AR-15 (or similar rifle) with good low-powered scopes or a red dot optic, a decent weapon-mounted light, other required accouterments and the training to use these carbines for the defense of your family and community, you may want to consider if you re making a mistake.Increasingly, it may be the responsibility of armed citizens to save their communities from violent mobs when law enforcement cannot mobilize fast enough to prevent attacks that are nothing more or less than domestic terrorism.Be prepared.Via: Bearing Arms
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The entire piece recasts a 2016 Milwaukee protest as an imminent, race-based domestic-terrorist invasion, using dehumanizing language (“violent mobs,” “murderous, arson-minded rioters”) and explicitly racial identifiers (“predominantly black,” “minority residents affiliated with Black Lives Matter”) to portray Black citizens as an existential threat that justifies preemptive, military-style violence against them, thereby inciting fear and hostility toward a protected group.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize fear—specifically, white suburban fear of Black unrest—to drive panic gun-buying and political backlash. By cherry-picking a single 2016 Milwaukee disturbance, stripping out context, and framing it as an imminent, nationwide wave of “domestic terrorism,” the text converts a local police-shooting protest into an existential threat. The piece then prescribes an AR-15 as the only rational response, implicitly equating racial grievance with mortal danger and justifying preemptive lethal force at “dozens to hundreds of yards.” In short, it is propaganda designed to radicalize readers, boost gun sales, and delegitimize Black protest by rebranding it as organized race war.

title: WATCH: Girl On Bike Brutally Beaten By Cops And Then SHE Is Charged With Assault
subject: News
content: Two years ago, 15-year-old Monique Tillman and her brother, like kids everywhere across the country, were riding their bikes. Unlike kids everywhere, Tillman was stopped for nothing more than the apparent crime of Riding While Black.Tillman and her brother made the mistake of cutting through a mall parking lot and running into Tacoma Police Officer Jared Williams, who was moonlighting as mall security. Williams then stopped the pair, telling them they were trespassing and that they might be banned from the mall.The children tried to explain that they ride through that parking lot all the time and they tried to leave. What happened after that might not be suitable for work.Here s the video:If you don t have the stomach to watch the video, the girl is snatched from her bike by the off-duty officer and slammed up against a car while he appears to be choking her. He then grabbed her hair and began throwing her around. He even tased her. He was choking me, grabbed me by my hair and tried to slam my face into the concrete. The next thing I know, I m on the ground being tased,  Tillman said.Source: Free Thought ProjectThen, after it was clearly shown in the video that the girl never even raised a hand toward the officer, she was charged for resisting arrest and assault on an officer for allegedly attempting to kick him. That s right, she was charged for assault. Fortunately, those charges were thrown out after there was no evidence that she tried to kick at all, and a lawsuit has been filed against Officer Williams, the security company and the people who own the mall. A child riding a bike should not have to worry that a police officer will stop her without legal cause and brutalize her,  said (Tillman s attorney, Vito) de la Cruz.  Our communities are weary of another African American child being hurt by unwarranted and excessive police force. Tillman, who is now a digital media student at Bates Technical College, had this to say: I feel like I was targeted because I am a person of color,  Tillman told the Seattle Times.  It was frustrating because I knew I didn t do anything wrong, but I couldn t stop them. Here s Tillman, now 17, talking about the incident, saying all she wants is an apology:Williams still has his job.Featured image via video screen captures
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the incident as a clear case of racial profiling ('Riding While Black'), omits any mention of the officer’s stated reason for the stop (trespassing enforcement in a private mall), presents the assault charges as baseless while acknowledging they were dismissed for lack of evidence rather than proven fabricated, and uses emotionally loaded language (‘brutally beaten,’ ‘snatched,’ ‘throwing her around’) without balanced context, thereby misrepresenting the event to support a pre-set narrative of racial bias and excessive force.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to provoke outrage over what is framed as a racially-motivated, unprovoked police assault on a Black child and the subsequent “blame-the-victim” prosecution. By foregrounding Monique Tillman’s youth, her lack of any real wrongdoing, and the still-unpunished status of the officer, the piece seeks to mobilize readers against systemic police brutality and racial profiling, using visceral language (“snatched,” “choked,” “tased”) and the contrast between a 15-year-old on a bike and an armed adult to indict both the individual officer and the broader system that allegedly protects him.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The incident is well-documented: local and national outlets (Seattle Times, KIRO-7, HuffPost, Courthouse News) covered the 2015 Tacoma mall encounter, published the security-camera video showing officer Jared Williams grabbing and tasing 15-year-old Monique Tillman, and reported that she was initially charged with assault and resisting before the charges were dropped; a civil rights lawsuit followed and the city later settled for $500,000, confirming the event and the basic facts recounted in the post.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The core event—an off-duty Tacoma officer stopped, physically subdued, and tased 15-year-old Monique Tillman in a mall parking lot, after which she was charged with assault and resisting arrest before the charges were dropped—did occur, was captured on video, reported by local outlets (Seattle Times, KIRO, News Tribune), and led to a settled civil rights lawsuit; while the article’s language is partisan and omits the officer’s trespassing rationale, these stylistic choices do not negate the verifiable facts, so the story is real, not fabricated.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The core facts—an off-duty Tacoma officer stopped 15-year-old Monique Tillman for trespassing in a mall lot, a physical struggle caught on video led to her being tased, she was charged then those charges were dropped, and she has since filed a civil lawsuit—are verifiable through court records, local news archives and the released video; while the article’s language is emotive and omits some context (mall-private-property angle, officer’s trespass-enforcement role), it does not invent events or evidence, so the story is real despite its advocacy framing.

title: Ted Cruz Attacks Sean Penn For ‘Glorifying Homicidal Killers’ — Here’s Penn’s Brilliant Response (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: At an addiction policy forum in in New Hampshire, Republican Senator and presidential contender Ted Cruz discussed the awful consequences of drug addiction by highlighting his sister s overdose in 2011. The conversation then turned into a political rant against undocumented illegal immigrants with Cruz calling them  undocumented democrats.  He blamed the media, Hollywood, and specifically Sean Penn for glorifying drugs and drug dealers, calling for a wall to be built between the U.S. and Mexico. Referring to Penn s recent interview with drug kingpin Joaquin Guzman, also known as El Chapo, Cruz said: El Chapo. You know, Sean Penn seems to think he is a sexy and attractive character. I so appreciate Hollywood for glorifying vicious homicidal killers. What a cute and chic thing to celebrate. Someone who murders and destroys lives for a living. El Chapo s organization brings vast quantities of drugs into this country, vast quantities of heroin. Penn s article did not glorify or celebrate El Chap or drugs, but in typical fashion, Ted Cruz has made a career out of half truths and all out lies. Cruz s statement didn t sit well with Sean Penn. In an email sent to  Mother Jones, Penn stated:  Ted Cruz is a generically funny and dangerously adept thought-smith. Clearly, he watches too much television and neglected to read my article before criticizing. It s understood. He s busy trading genius and raising aspirations with Mr. Trump. Blame Canada. Blame Canada is 1999 song from the film South Park. The song satirizes scapegoating.It s not the first time Penn has criticized Cruz. Responding in 2013 to an interviewer s question on whether Ted Cruz should be committed to a mental institution, Penn said:  He is, he is my American brother. I won t   I think we should take care of him, he is in, he s the trouble. Penn seems to have been on to something quite early. Ted Cruz s ideas are quite dangerous and if he becomes president, the country is in deep trouble. Featured image from YouTube Screenshot.
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively quotes Cruz’s attack on Penn, omits the journalistic context of Penn’s El Chapo interview, frames Cruz’s policy remarks as an unrelated ‘rant,’ and presents Penn’s retort as ‘brilliant’ while asserting as fact that Cruz’s ideas are ‘dangerous,’ thereby using partial truths and loaded language to mislead readers about both Cruz’s statements and Penn’s intent.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit Senator Ted Cruz by framing his attack on Sean Penn as yet another example of cynical, fact-free demagoguery. Using Penn’s sarcastic rebuttal and prior ridicule of Cruz as evidence, the piece portrays Cruz as a dangerous, dishonest opportunist who inflames anti-immigrant sentiment and the drug war for political gain, while implicitly praising Penn as the more thoughtful, principled figure.

answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately describes the RAISE Act introduced in 2017 by Senators Tom Cotton and David Perdue, which proposed cutting legal immigration by 40-50 percent, ending the diversity visa lottery, restricting family-sponsored green cards, and capping refugee admissions at 50,000—provisions that were publicly reported by Politico and other outlets and supported by the Trump administration, even though the commentary framing is partisan.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The story accurately reports that Senators Cotton and Perdue introduced legislation to curb family-based immigration, end the diversity visa lottery, and cut refugee admissions—proposals publicly documented by Congress and the Trump administration—so the underlying legislative news is real, even though the commentary surrounding it is misleading and opinionated.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying story—Republican senators introducing legislation to cut legal immigration, end the diversity visa lottery, and restrict family-based green cards—is factual and reported by mainstream outlets like Politico; the post merely presents those real policy proposals through a highly partisan, emotionally charged lens rather than fabricating events, so it qualifies as real news with misleading framing rather than outright fake news.

title: Trump Threatens Electoral ‘Bloodbath’ If Republicans Fail To Pass Obamacare Replacement (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: House Republicans have released their version of Obamacare replacement and it s bad, very bad. There s also almost no chance it will pass. Trump loves the bill, though. He loves it so much that he warned Republicans would experience an electoral  bloodbath  in 2018 if they don t pass it.On Tuesday, Trump had a meeting with House Republicans in which he delivered the stern warning. He said he was behind the bill 100 percent, even though the bill hasn t been scored by the Congressional Budget Office. In other words, we don t know how much the bill will cost and how many people will be losing insurance, but, according to Trump, the House should just go ahead and pass it.Trump vowed to throw his full support behind the effort to repeal and replace the Affordable Care Act during a meeting with House GOP leadership, saying he is  proud  to support a GOP-authored plan to replace Obamacare and told members behind closed doors that he would support it  100%,  according to sources in the room.But he warned lawmakers of the high-stakes nature of the effort, citing a potential electoral  bloodbath,  a member present said. He said he hopes members understand that,  the source said.Source: CNNHere s Trump s public statement:Trump could be right that there will be an electoral bloodbath in 2018, but not for the reason he says. Obamacare is suddenly very popular across the country and voters are standing up to their politicians demanding that if they make any improvements, it will be to provide better benefits, not fewer.It s gotten so bad for Republicans that many of them are refusing to face their constituents as they debate how to best get rid of people s life saving health insurance. Of course, they just blame President Obama, George Soros and the  fake news. Featured image via Pool/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively quotes Trump’s closed-door “bloodbath” warning while omitting any counterbalancing statements he reportedly made, frames the GOP bill as universally “very bad” without presenting its provisions or supporters’ rationales, and asserts that Obamacare is “suddenly very popular” without citing data or noting that polls still show sharp partisan splits; these framing choices create a one-sided impression that the bill is doomed and unpopular solely because of its content, rather than also because of political messaging, thereby misleading readers about the full context and motivations behind potential 2018 electoral outcomes.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize both the House GOP’s Obamacare-replacement bill and President Trump’s endorsement of it by framing the legislation as substantively “bad,” rushed, and unsupported by evidence (no CBO score), while portraying Trump’s electoral threat as self-serving and detached from public sentiment. By juxtaposing Trump’s “bloodbath” warning with rising Obamacare popularity, constituent backlash, and GOP lawmakers’ avoidance of town halls, the article seeks to amplify the narrative that Republicans are imperiling their own 2018 prospects by pursuing a harmful repeal effort against the will of voters.

title: Federal Judge Blows Lid Off Trump’s Biggest Complaints About Obamacare
subject: News
content: One of the arguments against the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) is that people are losing options as insurance companies are pulling out. That s true. Insurance companies are pulling out, but Republicans tell us it s because the law isn t viable and that insurance companies are leaving because they aren t making money. Well, a ruling from a federal judge just blew the lid off of that theory.The ruling, from Judge John D. Bates, a George W. Bush appointee, was in a case involving Aetna, who has pulled out of all but four of the states where they were part of the exchange. The claim was that they were losing money on the deal. Judge Bates found that that was a lie.Now a federal judge has ruled that that was a rank falsehood. In fact, says Judge John D. Bates, Aetna made its decision at least partially in response to a federal antitrust lawsuit blocking its proposed $34-billion merger with Humana. Aetna threatened federal officials with the pullout before the lawsuit was filed, and followed through on its threat once it was filed. Bates made the observations in the course of a ruling he issued Monday blocking the merger.Source: LA TimesThat pretty much eliminates one major talking point in the debate surrounding health insurance.The judge s conclusions about Aetna s real reasons for pulling out of Obamacare   as opposed to the rationalization the company made in public   are crucial for the debate over the fate of the Affordable Care Act. That s because the company s withdrawal has been exploited by Republicans to justify repealing the act. Just last week, House Speaker Paul Ryan (R-Wis.) cited Aetna s action on the  Charlie Rose  show, saying that it proved how shaky the exchanges were.In fact, the judge ruled, Aetna was profitable in some of the states but pulled out nonetheless just to make a point   a point that risked the lives or at least the health coverage of upwards of 20 million people. Bates believes that Aetna will start selling insurance in at least some of these markets again, so there goes the whole  Obamacare is imploding  idea.Clearly, not all insurers are lying to Americans. Kaiser Permanente loves the law. They ve even profited from it. The fact is that if they can do it, there s no reason other companies can t. All they have to do is cut back on the greed.Featured image via Win McNamee/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks one judge’s finding about Aetna’s 2017 pull-out, presents it as proof that no insurer exits are market-driven, and then broadly claims this “eliminates” the GOP argument that exchange instability is widespread, ignoring concurrent exits by other carriers, ongoing actuarial losses, and subsequent bipartisan congressional assessments that some regions do face single-insurer or no-insurer risk; by framing Aetna’s admittedly political withdrawal as representative of all departures, it misleads readers about the overall health of the ACA marketplaces.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit the Republican narrative that the Affordable Care Act is “imploding” by exposing Aetna’s withdrawal from ACA exchanges as a politically motivated maneuver rather than a financial necessity. By highlighting a federal judge’s finding that Aetna lied about losing money and pulled out to retaliate against an antitrust lawsuit, the author seeks to undermine the legitimacy of using insurer exits as evidence of Obamacare’s failure and to shift blame toward corporate greed and partisan tactics.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports the May 2017 ruling by federal Judge John D. Bates (Civ. No. 16-1494) that Aetna’s withdrawal from 17 ACA exchanges was at least partly retaliation for the Justice Department’s antitrust suit blocking its Humana merger; the opinion (publicly available) cites internal Aetna e-mails in which executives conditioned exchange participation on DOJ approval of the deal, undercutting the company’s public claim that the exits were driven solely by ACA losses. Major outlets including the Los Angeles Times and HuffPost covered the same ruling at the time, and the judge’s findings have not been overturned, so the core factual assertions are verifiable and not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: While the underlying judicial finding about Aetna’s 2017 withdrawal is accurate, the article spins that single data point into a sweeping, unsupported declaration that Obamacare’s market instability is a Republican myth, ignoring contemporaneous exits by Humana, UnitedHealth and others, documented county-level bare counties, and later bipartisan CMS reports showing some exchanges still teeter on single-insurer availability—thereby misrepresenting the broader marketplace reality and engaging in misleading content that distorts the overall truth.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports a federal judge’s 2017 finding that Aetna misrepresented its financial losses when exiting most ACA exchanges, tying the withdrawal to its merger fight rather than marketplace unprofitability; while the piece over-generalizes that this single ruling nullifies all insurer-exit concerns, the underlying court decision and Aetna’s documented threats are factual, so the news is real though framed with misleading spin.

answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is not a straight news report but a highly partisan opinion piece that distorts reality by selectively quoting, omitting context, and using loaded language (“whines,” “stole the election,” “his a handed to him”) to portray routine post-election boasting as unprecedented weakness; presenting a few critical tweets as representative public reaction and asserting Russian/FBI “intervention” as established fact without evidence further propagates a misleading narrative, so it qualifies as fake news under the standard of deliberate misrepresentation rather than factual reporting.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a heavily opinionated and selective polemic, not an objective news report; it distorts the event by omitting the context of Trump’s tweets, exaggerates their significance, and presents insult-laden tweets as evidence of a factual rebuttal, all to push a preconceived narrative rather than inform, which places it outside responsible journalism and into disinformation.

title: ABC NEWS: Emails Show Hillary’s Top Aide Arranged “Special Seating” At State Dinner For Top Clinton Donors [VIDEO]
subject: politics
content: This woman should be in a jail cell not sitting around laughing and opening pickle jars on the Jimmy Fallon show. Judicial Watch s release this week of 725 pages of State Department emails involving Hillary Clinton aide Huma Abedin demonstrates the Obama administration considers a large percentage of the emails sent through Clinton s private server too sensitive for Congress or the American public to read.Of the 725 pages, more than 250 pages were 100 percent redacted, many with  PAGE DENIED  stamped in bold.Judicial Watch said the new cache includes previously unreleased email exchanges in which former Abedin  provided influential Clinton Foundation donors special, expedited access to the secretary of state. Judicial Watch added that in many instances, the preferential treatment provided to donors was at the specific request of Clinton Foundation executive Douglas Band. The Abedin emails reveal that the longtime Clinton aide apparently served as a conduit between Clinton Foundation donors and Hillary Clinton while Clinton served as secretary of state. In more than a dozen email exchanges, Abedin provided expedited, direct access to Clinton for donors who had contributed from $25,000 to $10 million to the Clinton Foundation,  Judicial Watch said in a statement announcing the release.   WNDWATCH:#CrookedHillary scandal #9,999 and counting
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks Judicial Watch’s release to imply criminal pay-for-play without evidence of quid-pro-quo, conflates routine donor courtesy seating at a public state dinner with corruption, and omits that such donor access practices are common across administrations; it thus frames the issue and individuals through selective, de-contextualized details that mislead readers about actual wrongdoing.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize Hillary Clinton by framing her as corrupt and above the law, using selectively presented and emotionally charged details—such as redacted emails, donor access, and the “pickle jar” ridicule—to reinforce a pre-existing “Crooked Hillary” narrative. The piece is not primarily investigative; it is persuasive, designed to amplify distrust, provoke outrage, and mobilize opposition by portraying Clinton’s conduct as not merely unethical but criminal and covered up by the Obama administration.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: Judicial Watch, a conservative watchdog group, did release 725 pages of State-Department emails in August 2016 that were obtained through FOIA litigation; major outlets (AP, Politico, Fox, etc.) reported the same day that the documents show Huma Abedin fielding requests from Clinton-Foundation donors for seating, meetings and other favors, with some emails heavily redacted. While the article’s tone is partisan and omits counter-arguments, the underlying claim—that Abedin arranged special treatment for donors and that hundreds of pages were withheld—is documented in the released files and contemporaneous mainstream coverage, so the factual core is real.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece presents selectively edited, de-contextualized facts (Judicial Watch email release) to insinuate criminal “pay-for-play” without any evidence of quid-pro-quo, misrepresents routine White House donor-courtesy seating as unique corruption, and ignores that identical practices occur under both parties; by packaging these distortions as a scandalous exposé it meets the definition of fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents genuine Judicial Watch documents but weaponizes them through selective omission, exaggeration, and insinuation—hallmarks of fake news—by portraying routine donor seating at a public state dinner as evidence of criminal pay-for-play without any proof of quid-pro-quo, while simultaneously ignoring that identical practices occur under both parties, thereby manufacturing a scandal through deceptive framing rather than factual reporting.

title: IT’S A MIRACLE! Food Stamp Use Went Down 85% After This Change In Requirements
subject: Government News
content: Food Stamp use has miraculously gone down in several states! It s a miracle! In 13 Alabama counties, food stamp use went down a whopping 85%!When Obama took out the welfare-to-work requirement, the use of food stamps skyrocketed to nearly 45 million Americans! That s 1 in every 7 US citizens using food stamps! Now that the Trump administration has vowed to reduce the use, it s interesting to see that people jump off of assistance when the work requirement is put back in.Georgia and Alabama have seen a sharp decrease in food stamp use with the work requirement back in:Georgia:More than half of the 11,779 people enrolled for food stamps in 21 counties, an estimated 7,251 people, have dropped out of the food stamp program a drop of 62 percent, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.Georgia first rolled out its work requirements for the food stamp program in three counties in January 2016. Since then, the state has expanded work requirements in an additional 21 counties, giving people in those 21 counties until April 1, 2017 to find a job or lose food stamp benefits. Via: BNALABAMA:Thirteen previously exempted Alabama counties saw an 85 percent drop in food stamp participation after work requirements were put in place on Jan. 1, according to the Alabama Department of Human Resources.The counties   Greene, Hale, Perry, Dallas, Lowndes, Wilcox, Monroe, Conecuh, Clarke, Washington, Choctaw, Sumter and Barbour   had been exempt from a change that limited able-bodied adults without dependents to three months of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits within a three-year time frame unless they were working or participating in an approved training program.During the economic downturn of 2011-2013, several states   including Alabama   waived the SNAP work requirements in response to high unemployment. It was reinstituted for 54 counties on Jan. 1, 2016 and for the remaining 13 on Jan. 1, 2017. As of April 2017, the highest jobless rate among the 13 previously excluded counties was in Wilcox County, which reported a state-high unemployment rate of 11.7 percent, down more than 11 percentage points from the county s jobless rate for the same month of 2011.Ending the exemption has dramatically cut the number of SNAP recipients in the counties.As of Jan. 1, 2017, there were 13,663 able-bodied adults without dependents receiving food stamps statewide. That number dropped to 7,483 by May 1, 2017. Among the 13 counties, there were 5,538 adults ages 18-50 without dependents receiving food stamps as of Jan. 1, 2017. That number dropped to 831   a decline of about 85 percent   by May 1, 2017. Based on the trend, the number of (able-bodied adults without dependents) recipients for SNAP benefits is expected to continue to decline statewide and in the formerly 13 exempted counties,  according to Alabama DHR spokesperson John Hardy.Statewide, the number of able-bodied adults receiving food stamps has fallen by almost 35,000 people since Jan. 1, 2016. Each recipient receives about $126 a month in benefits.Nationwide, there are about 44 million people receiving SNAP benefits at a cost of about $71 billion. The Trump administration has vowed to cut the food stamp rolls over the next decade, including ensuring that able-bodied adults recipients are working.Via: al.com
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks dramatic percentage drops in a narrow subgroup—able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWDs) in a handful of counties—while implying that overall food-stamp enrollment collapsed because of restored work rules. It omits that these counties had been exempt from time limits during high-unemployment years, so the baseline was artificially high; once the exemption ended, many ABAWDs lost eligibility regardless of actual job availability, not because they found work. Framing the outcome as a 'miracle' and tying it to Trump-era policy obscures the fact that the same data show statewide ABAWD numbers fell only 35,000 out of 44 million nationwide recipients, masking the broader safety-net picture and misrepresenting cause-and-effect.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s intent is to frame the sharp drop in SNAP participation as a moral triumph of “work requirements” over “dependency,” using celebratory, partisan language (“miracle,” “jump off assistance”) to imply that most recipients were lazy or fraudulent until forced to work. By selectively highlighting only the caseload decline and omitting any data on whether the people who lost benefits actually found jobs, earned enough to meet their food needs, or simply went hungry, the piece disguises a policy-driven eligibility purge as a success story, thereby reinforcing a broader ideological campaign to shrink the social safety net.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports state-level data: Alabama DHR confirmed an ~85% drop in able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWDs) on SNAP in 13 counties after work requirements resumed in Jan 2017, and Georgia recorded a similar 62% decline in 21 counties; these figures align with official announcements and mainstream outlets (al.com, Atlanta Journal-Constitution). However, the piece omits context—most of the reduction comes from a narrow subset (ABAWDs, roughly 5% of all SNAP recipients), not the entire caseload, and provides no evidence that enrollees found jobs or improved food security, so while the numbers are real the framing is selective.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not fabricated, but it is intentionally misleading: it presents selective county-level drops among able-bodied adults without dependents as proof that reinstating work requirements slashed overall food-stamp use, while the nationwide caseload barely moved. By omitting context—prior exemptions, no evidence most recipients found jobs, and that 44 million others still receive benefits—it creates a false causal narrative, making the article function as misinformation rather than factual reporting.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article misrepresents a targeted eligibility purge as a voluntary mass exodus from SNAP by inflating county-level ABAWD drops into a nationwide ‘miracle,’ concealing that most of the 85 % decline stems from re-imposed time limits that simply cut people off whether or not they found work, while nationwide rolls barely budged, making the central claim of broad success demonstrably false.

title: Trump Campaign CEO Didn’t Want His Kids In School With A Bunch Of ‘Whiny’ Jews

intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding aim is to weaponize newly-unsealed divorce papers to brand Donald Trump’s then-campaign CEO as both an anti-Semite and a domestic abuser, thereby tarring Trump himself as a man who “only hires the best people.” By amplifying the most lurid passages—Bannon allegedly calling Jewish students “whiny brats” and allegedly assaulting his wife—the piece seeks to provoke moral outrage in progressive readers, reinforce existing negative narratives about the Trump team, and delegitimize Bannon’s political influence, all while signaling its own superior virtue through sarcastic asides and eye-roll emojis.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The claims about Stephen Bannon's alleged anti-Semitic remarks and domestic-abuse allegations are documented in sworn court filings from his 2007 divorce proceedings, which have been publicly available for years and were reported by multiple reputable outlets (e.g., Politico, Daily Beast, NBC) in 2016; although Bannon denies the statements, the existence of the court records themselves is verifiable, making the article a factual report of what the documents contain rather than fabricated news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece presents a 2007 divorce-court allegation as proven reality, headlines it as fact (‘didn’t want his kids in school with a bunch of “whiny” Jews’), layers on sarcastic editorial commentary, and buries the single-sentence denial, creating a false impression that Bannon’s anti-Semitism is established when the claim is still just an unverified accusation; this selective, emotionally loaded framing meets the definition of fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece relies on unverified 2007 divorce allegations, treats them as proven facts, omits corroboration, and layers on sarcastic editorializing to cement a predetermined smear, meeting the criteria for misleading/fabricated content rather than verified reporting.

title: OPEN-BORDER LIBERALS Put Entire Nation On High Alert: German Spy Chief Warns 1,000+ Radical Islamists Ready To Attack…Over 100 ISIS Members Among Refugees
subject: politics
content: Thank you Angela Merkel German security service BfV reportedly received more than 100 tip-offs that ISIS militants had infiltrated the country among refugees, according to a recent report. The news comes as massive nationwide anti-terror raids took place this week.The head of the German domestic intelligence service (BfV), Hans-Georg Maassen, told a gathering of politicians that the agency had received more than 100 warnings indicating there were Islamic State (IS, formerly ISIS/ISIL) militants staying in Germany as refugees, newspaper Berliner Zeitung reported Friday, without citing its sources.However , some cases of  baseless defamation  were among those tip-offs, Maassen added, according to the newspaper.German security services have remained on high alert since the November terror attacks in Paris which claimed the lives of more than 130 people.Earlier this week, police and security agents all across Germany were scrambled to search for suspects allegedly planning a terror attack in the country, with Berlin seen as the most likely target. Well-known tourist attractions including Alexanderplatz train station and the Cold War-era Checkpoint Charlie could be among the targets of a possible attack, according to preliminary media reports.On Thursday, a police special force unit raided four flats and two businesses in Berlin, detaining four men accused of allegedly having ties to Islamic State. They were suspected of being involved in planning an attack, police spokesman Martin Redlich told RT.German spy chief warns of 1,000+ radical Islamists ready to attack https://t.co/VZn1xRA2oA pic.twitter.com/BlxXGGXHkK  RT (@RT_com) December 13, 2015One of the suspects, a 49-year-old Algerian, was arrested in a three-bedroom flat in Berlin s predominantly immigrant district of Kreuzberg. He was living there on a fake French passport, local media reported, and owned two shops nearby Alexanderplatz and Checkpoint Charlie. Redlich could not confirm the landmarks were the targets, however.The spokesman said police had acted on a tip-off, but he provided no further details.Similar raids also took place in the German regions of North Rhine Westphalia and Lower Saxony. In Berlin alone, 450 police officers were engaged in the operation, German media reported.The main suspect was a 35-year-old Algerian man detained during Thursday s raid in the town of Attendorn. Said to be a possible leader of an IS terrorist cell, he was also being sought by Algerian authorities over allegations he is a member of the terrorist group.He entered Germany in autumn 2015, having traveled the so-called  Balkan route.  At that time, the 35-year-old was registered in Bavaria as a refugee.Both men had been monitored since the end of 2015, after security services had received a tip-off they might be IS infiltrators.Another unnamed 26-year-old Algerian, who also registered as a refugee and lived in a shelter in central Hannover, is suspected by the police to be the cell s communication agent. He is also thought to have possible ties to Belgian Islamists. He has traveled to the Molenbeek district of Brussels, known for harboring jihadists, at least once in recent weeks. Abdelhamid Abaaoud, the mastermind behind the November s Paris attacks, was a Molenbeek resident.Germany took in over 1.1 million refugees in 2015, and fifty-four percent of Germans believe the terror threat in the country is on the rise because of the high number of incoming migrants, according to the latest Spiegel poll. Via: RT
