title: Ben Cohen’s Response To Fox News’ Bernie Sanders Conspiracy Theory Is Perfect (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: Fox News and other conservative outlets are doing everything they can to spread the conspiracy theory that Bernie Sanders is behind Chicago s protest that shut down Donald Trump s rally on Friday. During a segment on Fox Business Network, Ben & Jerry s co-founder, Ben Cohen, was questioned about the matter. Cohen responded appropriately by laughing at the show s host Neil Cavuto.Mentioning that Trump has accused Sanders of being behind the protest, he Cavuto asks Cohen  What do you make of it that there were many Sanders protesters there? Cohen responds, saying: I got no idea who was there. But I can tell you that Donald Trump brings out a lot of strong feelings. And I believe a fairly significant majority of Americans do not agree with Donald Trump and are embarrassed by the way he is conducting himself and . Cohen is then interrupted by Cavuto, who says: Well that s your opinion and you re entitled to it. Cavuto, bizarrely, then brings up the time that Sanders  rally was interrupted by Black Lives Matter activists. Cavuto s attempt to equivocate the two protests is rather weak. When Sanders was interrupted, he let the two courageous young women who interrupted him, take the podium. That showed Sanders has the one of the most important qualities of a great leader   the wisdom to know when to listen.Trump and his supporters, on the other hand, have an entirely different attitude towards those who disagree with them. Cohen responds to the Cavuto, saying: Well, there are two different ways of handling protesters. I mean there has always been protesters, there has always been people who are trying to disrupt political speeches, but going and telling people to rough them up, beat them up   it s not American, it s not what I want to see in my country. Conservatives are so desperate to put this conspiracy out there, they are willing to completely destroy a woman s reputation by spreading a rumor so ridiculous it shouldn t even need a Snopes article to bust it.Yes, there were Sanders  supporters at the rally that night. They were involved in one of the greatest protests in history. They did not, however, shut the rally down. Trump choose to end the event. Those Sanders supporters were also a very small group of people among thousands of activists who came to together to show Trump that he cannot just roll into any community and subject them to his vitriol without dissent.Chicago is a bastion of radical leftist resistance organizing. I would personally have been surprised if the campaign hadn t seen the type of protest that took place on Friday. This was going to happen no matter what other candidates are running.It should be noted that while Cohen s commentary on the protest is sound, he does seem to imply in the interview that Trump and Sanders might have a lot of common ground on issues. This shouldn t in any way be interpreted to think that a Trump presidency wouldn t be disastrous. Trump and Sanders may have some overlap in their observations of problems facing this nation though their policy prescriptions are as different as night and day. Come election day in November,  people need to accept that any candidate would be better than Trump.You can watch the Fox News segment below.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0KOIkPoOZWwFeatured image from video screenshot via YouTube
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: Fox anchors repeatedly imply that Sanders masterminded the Chicago protest, yet offer no evidence—only the presence of some Sanders supporters—to frame him as responsible, while ignoring that Trump himself cancelled the rally and that the protest was a broad, multi-group action; this selective framing misleads viewers about causation and culpability.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to defend Bernie Sanders and the Chicago protesters against right-wing conspiracy claims, using Ben Cohen’s televised push-back as a rhetorical weapon. By ridiculing Fox’s “ridiculous” rumor, contrasting Sanders’ respectful handling of dissent with Trump’s incitement of violence, and insisting that the shutdown was a spontaneous, multi-group act of legitimate resistance rather than a Sanders plot, the piece seeks to delegitimize conservative media narratives, valorize left-wing activism, and underscore the moral urgency of defeating Trump in November.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The piece accurately describes a real televised exchange (readily verifiable on YouTube) in which Ben Cohen, on Fox Business Network, laughed off Neil Cavuto’s suggestion that Bernie Sanders orchestrated the Chicago Trump-rally protest, instead condemning Trump’s encouragement of violence; although the article’s tone is partisan and editorial, its factual claims about the interview, the protest’s composition, and Trump’s cancellation of the event are all supported by contemporaneous video and mainstream reporting, so it is not fabricated or fake news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports the Fox Business exchange, Cohen’s push-back, and the broader context that Trump—not Sanders—cancelled the rally, while explicitly noting that only some protesters were Sanders supporters and that no evidence ties the campaign to the event, so the piece itself is factual reportage rather than disinformation.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports a televised exchange in which Ben Cohen rebuts unsupported Fox claims that Bernie Sanders orchestrated the Chicago protest; it correctly notes that Trump—not protesters—cancelled the rally, that participants came from multiple groups, and that conservative media advanced a baseless conspiracy, all verifiable through the embedded video and contemporaneous news coverage.

title: FLORIDA CAR DEALER THREATENED WITH FINES FOR DISPLAYING AMERICAN FLAGS [Video]
subject: left-news
content: It doesn t get much more anti-American than forcing the removal of American flags from an American owned business A Florida car dealership is facing fines for displaying its patriotism.The Kia dealership in West Palm Beach faces penalties of up to $1,000 per day for a code-enforcement violation it received from Palm Beach County for displaying six American flags on its property, WPTV reported.The county said the dealership is violating a that prohibits the display of pennants, balloons, banners and other signs made of lightweight fabric, plastic or similar substances. We re just trying to show our patriotism,  dealership general manager Mike Wangle told WPTV.The notice said the dealership must remove the flags by the Fourth of July or the fine will be imposed. You would think they they would let us leave it up during the Fourth and then say,  take them down after the holiday,  Wangle said.He told WPTV he understands the code, but doesn t understand why the flags don t fall under the flags category.// <![CDATA[ var p = new anv_pl_def(); p.config = {}; p.config.width = 640; p.config.height = 360; p.loadVideoExpressV3('|1000011|SPS'); // ]]> I don t have a problem taking the banners down if we had banners saying  we re open , or a  big sale.  Those are banners,  he said.  But when you re displaying the American flag, that s a little different. That s why we re kind of upset about it. He added that he will keep the banners flying until July 5 to display patriotism on Independence Day, even if he has to pay the fine himself.Via: Biz Pac Review // ]]>
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The story itself is real—the dealership did receive a county notice objecting to six fabric flags on poles because the local sign code bans lightweight fabric banners/pennants used for advertising; however, the article frames it as an anti-American crackdown on the U.S. flag, implying the county is punishing patriotism. In fact, the code treats the fabric flags as promotional signage, not as official U.S. flags (which are exempt), so presenting the citation as targeting the American flag per se supplies false contextual information that inflames readers.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to provoke outrage and frame the county’s neutral, content-blind zoning rule as an anti-American attack on patriotism. By spotlighting the emotional quote “It doesn’t get much more anti-American…,” juxtaposing the July 4 deadline with the word “violation,” and omitting any explanation that the ordinance treats all lightweight fabric signs the same regardless of their message, the piece is designed to generate clicks, shares, and indignation rather than to inform readers about mundane land-use enforcement.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The story is based on a 2015 report from West Palm Beach’s WPTV (an NBC affiliate) and was subsequently covered by other local outlets; the Palm Beach County code-enforcement citation cited in the piece is verifiable public record, and the dealership manager’s quotes were given on-camera, so while the headline is sensationalized the underlying event actually occurred.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—a Kia dealership in West Palm Beach receiving a county notice that it must remove six lightweight fabric flags or face daily fines—is factual; the county cited a sign ordinance that bans lightweight fabric banners/pennants when used for promotional display, not the official U.S. flag itself. The story becomes misleading because it frames the enforcement as an anti-American attack on patriotism, when in reality the code treats the items as advertising signage and exempts formal U.S. flags, so the dispute is over code interpretation, not suppression of national symbols.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—a county code-enforcement notice to a Florida car dealership over six lightweight fabric flags—did occur, so the story is not fabricated; however, the article supplies false context by presenting the routine, content-neutral sign-code citation as an anti-American attack on displaying the U.S. flag, thereby misleading readers while still rooted in a real incident.

title: WATCH: MEGYN KELLY HUMILIATES HERSELF (AGAIN)…Tries To Cozy Up To Traitor Jane Fonda…Gets Major SMACKDOWN On Live TV
subject: left-news
content: One day after actress Debra Messing revealed that she regretted going on Megyn Kelly s new NBC morning show, the embattled host managed to draw the ire of an even bigger Hollywood star.Megyn sat down with Oscar-winning screen icon Jane Fonda on Wednesday, and in an ill-advised and poorly conceived move, decided to ask the 79-year-old actress to detail the plastic surgery she has had done over the years.The nasty exchange on day 2  of Megyn Kelly s new job at NBC couldn t have taken place between two more self-serving and arrogant women.Watch: You, you ve been an example to everyone, on how to age beautifully and with strength. And unapologetically,  began Megyn, nervously drawing out her question. You admit you had work done. I think it s to your credit. You look amazing. Have you   why did you say .. I read you felt you re not proud to admit you had work done, why not? At that moment a steely Fonda stared Megyn straight in the eyes and very firmly asked:  We really want to talk about that now? Via: Daily Mail
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline and framing use emotionally loaded language (‘HUMILIATES HERSELF’, ‘TRAITOR’, ‘MAJOR SMACKDOWN’) to present a routine, slightly awkward interview question as a catastrophic self-own and to vilify both Kelly and Fonda. By cherry-picking one exchange and exaggerating its significance, the piece misleads readers about the actual tone and stakes of the segment, turning standard celebrity-interview friction into evidence of moral failure and professional collapse.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize a brief, awkward exchange into click-bait “proof” that Megyn Kelly is a perennial embarrassment and that any interaction with a liberal icon like Jane Fonda must end in public humiliation. By framing the segment as a “nasty” showdown between “self-serving and arrogant women,” the piece stokes partisan outrage, drives traffic through sensational headlines, and reinforces pre-existing narratives that both Kelly and Hollywood elites are contemptible—thereby monetizing anger rather than informing.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The incident described—Megyn Kelly asking Jane Fonda about plastic surgery and Fonda’s curt reply, “We really want to talk about that now?”—is widely documented by multiple reputable outlets (e.g., the Daily Mail, Variety, USA Today) who reported the same exchange during Kelly’s 2017 NBC show, so the core event is factual even though the article’s tone is hyperbolic and partisan.

title: Energy Department To Close Office Of International Climate And Technology
subject: News
content: In response to the U.S. withdrawing from the Paris climate agreement earlier this month, the Energy Department is shutting down the Office of International Climate and Technology, a department that works with other countries to develop clean energy technology.An agency spokesman tried to justify the Energy Department shutting down the office by stating that the DOE is  looking for ways to consolidate the many duplicative programs that currently exist within DOE,  thus the Office of International Climate and Technology is getting the chop.The 11-person office has been in operation since 2010, operating as a means for the U.S. to work with international partners on energy sector technology in an effort to reduce greenhouse gases. The employees of the Office of International Climate and Technology also play a large part in the Clean Energy Ministerial, a conference for high-polluting nations to focus on making the energy sector greener.DOE spokeswoman Shaylyn Hynes said there are numerous international offices within the Energy Department that could take on the work of the Office of International Climate and Technology, however, she failed to acknowledge whether one actually would. The Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy (EERE) has an International Affairs team, while the International Affairs Office has a renewables team,  Hynes said.  The Department is looking for ways to eliminate this kind of unnecessary duplication   just like any responsible American business would. The closing of this particular office is most likely a direct result of Trump s 2018 budget proposal, which slashes funding for both the DOE and the Environmental Protection Agency, particularly cuts for climate change initiatives and research efforts. Naturally, environmentalists are horrified by the news of the international office s closure. Willfully ignoring the climate crisis is recklessly and unnecessarily dangerous for families and communities across the country, and it s clear that Trump will stop at nothing to completely isolate the United States and irreparably damage our reputation with the rest of the world,  said John Coequyt, the global climate policy director at the Sierra Club. Ignorance is not diplomacy, and if Trump were acting like a leader, he would know that. Hynes responded by saying that the Trump administration is not bringing an end to its clean energy efforts, drawing particular attention to Energy Secretary Rick Perry s support for carbon capture storage and nuclear energy efforts at a recent Clean Energy Ministerial.Featured image via Kevin Frayer/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively frames the office closure as a purely political retaliation for exiting the Paris Agreement, while downplaying the DOE’s stated rationale of consolidating overlapping programs; by quoting only environmentalist outrage and omitting any detail on whether the 11-person team’s functions will actually be lost or simply shifted to existing EERE or International Affairs units, it misleads readers into assuming a total abandonment of U.S. international clean-energy cooperation.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame the closure of the Office of International Climate and Technology as a politically-motivated, ideologically-driven retreat from global climate leadership that endangers both the planet and America’s diplomatic standing. By foregrounding the Trump administration’s budget-slashing logic, quoting only environmentalist outrage, and presenting the DOE’s “duplication” rationale as a thin pretext, the piece seeks to delegitimize the shutdown and cast it as part of a broader pattern of climate denial and international isolation.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports the closure of the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of International Climate and Technology, citing official DOE statements and a spokeswoman, and aligns with documented 2018 Trump budget proposals that targeted climate and energy programs; no factual inaccuracies or unattributed claims are evident, and the inclusion of named sources and context (Paris withdrawal, Clean Energy Ministerial) supports its authenticity.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports an actual DOE decision that can be verified through official sources; the closure of the Office of International Climate and Technology is factual, even though the piece injects interpretive bias by emphasizing political motives and environmentalist reactions while offering limited evidence that the office’s functions will be fully transferred rather than eliminated.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports an actual DOE decision to close a small office, cites named officials and budget documents, and includes both the department’s consolidation rationale and environmentalist criticism; while its framing is partisan and omits detail on whether the office’s functions will be fully transferred, no facts are fabricated, so it remains real news with a slant rather than fake news.

title: HOW TO PUT THE SCREWS TO LEFTIST ESPN AND SAVE TONS OF MONEY ON YOUR CABLE BILL IN 3 EASY STEPS
subject: politics
content: Brilliant just brilliant Remember when Disney s ESPN punished Trump for his remarks about illegal aliens and moved their annual golf outing from Trump s golf course as a  punishment  for his views?Do you remember when ESPN cut Hank Williams  theme song from Monday Night Football after making an analogy to Adolf Hitler when talking about Barack Obama?Remember when their own little ESPN barbie made international news after berating a woman in a parking garage for simply doing her job?https://youtu.be/Pz1XY18_D3gRemember when ESPN decided to give the Arthur Ashe  Courage  Award to Bruce (refers to himself as  Caitlyn ) Jenner only months after killing an innocent woman in a car crash over a young girl who stole the hearts of America when she played college basketball with terminal cancer to inspire others to keep fighting?Remember when Bob Costas was hailed by ESPN s Pardon the Interruption,  co-host Michael Wilbon, who gave NBC Sports  Bob Costas  a standing and loud ovation  for using his Sunday Night Football halftime show to espouse his pro-gun control views?Well Now it s Red Sox great, Curt Schilling s turn to feel the wrath of ESPN, as he s been fired for a tweet about muslims by the sports propagandist arm of the Disney Corporation.Because my enemies are legion (and not terribly bright), let s get this out of the way: It is wrong to compare Muslims to Nazis. Baseball great Curt Schilling did not do that. In a Tweet that resulted in a pandering suspension from the left-wing sports network ESPN, Schilling compared Muslim extremists to Nazis.Comparing Muslim extremists to Nazis is not wrong, it is science.ESPN knows this but ESPN (which is owned by Disney) has grown into an increasingly ugly, left-wing propaganda machine. What should be America s Pleasure Island away from political division   sports   has been destroyed by ESPN. All that Disney money is now being used to buy all that sports programming that makes tens of millions of sports fans captive to The Realpolitik.Have you had enough?How much of this abuse are you going to take?How much of this abuse are you going to take before you do something?Oh, you didn t know you had The Power to do something?Well, you do   because your cable company and ESPN have been playing you for a sucker for decades.Before I get to The Three Easy Steps, here s how the cable television/ESPN racket works:If ESPN is part of your cable package   and it most likely is   whether you watch or not, this leftwing propaganda outlet soaks you for $6.61 a month.No, for real.By working out a pay TV system (cable and satellite) that forces you to pay for dozens of networks you do not watch, ESPN (and other left-wing networks like CNN, MTV, and MSNBC) gets a piece of your obscenely-overpriced cable bill.Moreover, no other cable network makes more money this way than ESPN. And with somewhere around 90 million subscribers, that adds up to close to $7 billion annually.And $80 a year comes from you.In other words, you can t hurt ESPN by not watching ESPN. Ad revenue based on the number of viewers is only a part of ESPN s revenue stream.ESPN s got you in a box. Watch or no, they make buku off you.There s only one way to send a message to ESPN, and you have the power to do it in just Three Easy Steps.Call your cable company. Cancel your cable. Sit back and watch ESPN implode.Listen, I m not a sports guy, so I can t answer the question of whether or not watching The Games are worth funding The Apparatchik. What I can tell you is that with the purchase of a $49 Roku (which is essentially a cable box) an extraordinary Streaming world awaits   a world that is a whole lot cheaper than cable.For $20 you can subscribe to Netflix and Amazon. Not only is there more TV than you could watch in a lifetime, unlike cable, there is not 20 minutes of catheter ads every hour.You have the power to send ESPN a message.Make the call.Via: Breitbart News
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece cherry-picks isolated incidents, distorts facts (e.g., Jenner crash timeline, Schilling tweet content, Costas network), and presents them under a sweeping claim that ESPN is a left-wing propaganda machine soaking every cable subscriber for $6.61 a month, ignoring that the fee is part of bundled carriage deals set by providers, not a political levy, and that streaming alternatives still carry ESPN/Disney networks. It frames routine business or editorial decisions as coordinated ideological attacks to incite audience outrage and drive cord-cutting, thereby weaponizing selective, decontextualized information to mislead readers about both ESPN’s practices and their own cable bills.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize partisan resentment against ESPN—framed as a “left-wing propaganda” arm of Disney—in order to drive readers to cancel traditional cable packages, thereby “punishing” the network financially and simultaneously saving money by switching to cheaper streaming alternatives. By selectively listing grievances that conflate corporate decisions with liberal bias, the piece converts cultural outrage into a consumer revolt, masking its populist call-to-action as a money-saving life-hack.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: This piece is not genuine news but a hyper-partisan opinion rant that misrepresents facts (e.g., inflating ESPN’s carriage fee, misstating the Jenner award timeline, and distorting Schilling’s suspension) to push a political boycott, and it originates from a blog/aggregator citing Breitbart rather than any independent journalistic reporting.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a deliberately misleading polemic that strings together half-truths, chronological distortions (e.g., Jenner award vs. crash dates), network mis-attributions (Costas worked for NBC, not ESPN), and exaggerated financial claims to fabricate a monolithic “left-wing ESPN” conspiracy; its core call to action—cancel cable to “defund” ESPN—ignores that the same fees arise from carrier contracts, not ideology, and that most streaming bundles still include ESPN, rendering the promised savings illusory.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a politically-motivated screed that strings together half-truths, distortions, and cherry-picked grievances to fabricate a grand conspiracy of ESPN as a left-wing extortion racket; it misrepresents carriage-fee economics, misattributes events and networks, and omits context to incite outrage-driven cord-cutting, making it classic disinformation rather than legitimate news.

title: Once Again, Trump Proves How INCREDIBLY Ignorant He Is About The World (DETAILS)
subject: News
content: President Donald Trump does not know anything about foreign policy. Now, it appears, he knows just as little about trade. This is more troubling as one of his selling points was that he was a successful businessman with a global company. You d think that a person with such a vast empire (there are Trump Towers all over the planet) would know a thing or two about the subject. This idea was blown out of the water this week by comments from a German official about Chancellor Angela Merkel s recent visit to Washington, DC.The official told The Times of London, Ten times Trump asked [German chancellor Angela Merkel] if he could negotiate a trade deal with Germany. Every time she replied,  You can t do a trade deal with Germany, only the EU.  On the eleventh refusal, Trump finally got the message,  Oh, we ll do a deal with Europe then.' For a man who claimed to be able to  make the best deals  for the United States with our trading partners, it helps to know who exactly those partners are.As bad as that is, Trump s lack of world knowledge is more than just problematic when it comes to problems the country is dealing with on the other side of the world. Not only has the Trump Administration failed to even nominate an ambassador to South Korea, up until China President Xi Jinping visited him at Mar-a-Lago, he was under the impression that the only thing that had to happen to contain North Korean leader, Kim Jung Un, was have China tell him to behave.North Korea is looking for trouble. If China decides to help, that would be great. If not, we will solve the problem without them! U.S.A.  Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) April 11, 2017After his visit with Xi, Trump told the Wall Street Journal,  After listening for 10 minutes, I realized it s not so easy. I felt pretty strongly that they had a tremendous power [over] North Korea.   But it s not what you would think. Keep in mind, Trump spent a lot of time during the campaign (and before) touting,  I know China.  He claimed that the combination of the work he has done with the Chinese and the  hundreds of books  he had read about China made him an expert on the region. All of this is odd, given his comments about that short (ten minutes!) conversation. His lack of understanding goes further.After his meeting with Xi, Trump told an interviewer,  Korea actually used to be a part of China. This did not go over well with the South Korean government. South Korean foreign spokesman Cho June-hyuck responded with,  It s a clear fact acknowledged by the international community that, for thousands of years in history, Korea has never been part of China. But wait, there s more.An interview with Fox & Friends makes it appear that Trump really doesn t even know who is running North Korea right now. He told them:I hope things work out well. I hope there s going to be peace, but you know, they ve been talking with this gentleman for a long time. You read Clinton s book, he said,  Oh we made such a great peace deal,  and it was a joke. You look at different things over the years with President Obama. Everybody s been outplayed, they ve all been outplayed by this gentleman and we ll see what happens. But I just don t telegraph my moves.Bill Clinton never dealt with the current leader, he dealt with his father, Kim Jung Il. Getting these facts wrong says a lot. Trump doesn t know who to deal with when it comes to trade with Germany. He seems to have taken his information about Chinese and Korean history from Xi. He doesn t appear to have a clue as to who the leader of North Korean leader. The questions with this president are not  What did he know and when did he know it?  but  Does he know anything and can he be taught? Featured image via Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively presents anecdotal second-hand accounts and Trump’s own imprecise statements to frame him as uniquely ignorant, omitting context such as routine diplomatic repetition or the fact that U.S. presidents often learn details of alliance structures during early meetings; by highlighting only his misstatements and not corrections or subsequent policy actions, it misleads readers into concluding he is irredeemably uninformed rather than simply inexperienced or inarticulate.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to demolish Donald Trump’s self-proclaimed image as a savvy global deal-maker by stitching together a series of reported gaffes—misunderstanding EU trade competence, underrating Chinese influence over North Korea, garbling Korean history, and confusing Kim Jong-un with his father—to portray him as dangerously uninformed. By amplifying each stumble with incredulous commentary and rhetorical questions (“Does he know anything and can he be taught?”), the piece seeks to erode public confidence in Trump’s foreign-policy credibility and, by extension, his fitness to conduct international affairs on America’s behalf.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately cites verifiable events and direct quotes from named officials and Trump himself—Merkel’s aides told The Times of London that Trump repeatedly asked for a bilateral Germany-only trade deal, Trump’s post-Xi Jinning Wall Street Journal and Fox & Friends interviews are on record, and South Korea’s foreign ministry publicly rebutted his “Korea used to be part of China” remark—so while the tone is partisan, the underlying factual claims are documented and not fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a real opinion piece that accurately cites verifiable incidents (Merkel’s EU-only trade-competence remark, Trump’s Korea-was-part-of-China quote, his Fox & Friends confusion over Kim Jong Un vs. Kim Jong Il) and attributes them to named sources or on-the-record interviews; while its framing is one-sided and omits balancing context, the underlying facts reported are not fabricated, so it qualifies as real news presented through a highly critical, misleadingly selective lens rather than fabricated content.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a real opinion piece that accurately quotes verifiable incidents (Trump repeatedly asking Merkel for a bilateral Germany-only trade deal, his post-Xi comment that “Korea used to be part of China,” and his on-air reference to Clinton dealing with “this gentleman” in North Korea); while it selects only embarrassing moments and offers hostile interpretation, the underlying facts are documented by multiple reputable outlets, so the item itself is not fabricated news but rather slanted political commentary.

title: ‘Shoot At Hurricane Irma’ Facebook Event Taken Too Seriously, So Police Had To Issue A Warning
subject: News
content: A Facebook event called  Shoot At Hurricane Irma  popped up just before the powerful storm made landfall in Florida, and apparently people took it seriously enough that the police felt they had to issue warnings not to do it.Over 80,000 people responded to the event, which tells us two things: One, that the event s young and naive creator, Ryon Edwards, had no freaking clue what he was really doing; and two, that people really are dumb enough to accept this on its face rather than question it. That s probably more true of right-wing gun nuts than anything since the nuttier part of the right loves any excuse to shoot off their firearms.The Pasco County Sheriff s Department, concerned that idiots might actually try this, tweeted the following in response to the interest in the event:To clarify, DO NOT shoot weapons @ #Irma. You won t make it turn around & it will have very dangerous side effectshttps://t.co/CV4Y9OJknv  Pasco Sheriff (@PascoSheriff) September 10, 2017It s a tiny bit like firing your weapon straight into the air. What goes up, must come down, and the bullets can come down on perfectly innocent people and cause serious injury. In the case of a hurricane, the bullets can get spun around, more or less, and come back to you or someone near you. That warning tweet has been retweeted nearly 30,000 times.Edwards claimed that he created the event out of  stress and boredom.  The response apparently was a complete surprise to him, with him saying that he never thought this would get so out of control. People have allegedly even created graphics that show how to shoot at the hurricane  correctly,  and other Facebook events have appeared, with one suggesting using flamethrowers to stop the hurricane.It s really hard to tell what s sarcasm and what s not sometimes, especially for, well, stupid people. Edwards would have been better off finding something else to do with his  stress and boredom,  because yes, people really are that stupid.Featured image via Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The Facebook event was created as a tongue-in-cheek joke to relieve stress, not to deceive, but its humorous framing was taken literally by thousands, meeting the Satire/Parody category where the creator’s comedic intent is overridden by audiences who act on it, prompting real-world warnings from police about shooting at a hurricane.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to ridicule both the gullible public and the event’s creator by framing the viral “Shoot At Hurricane Irma” episode as proof of mass stupidity, especially among “right-wing gun nuts.” Using sarcasm and mockery, the piece amplifies the absurdity of the stunt, highlights the danger of taking jokes literally, and implicitly scolds social-media users who fail to recognize obvious satire—thereby reinforcing a broader cultural critique of American gun culture and online credulity.

title: TRUMP REPORTEDLY Thinking About Replacing Jeff Sessions With Candidate Who Won’t Cower To Pressure From The Swamp
subject: left-news
content: Hillary Clinton, Barack Obama, Eric Holder and Loretta Lynch better start lawyering up President Donald Trump is reportedly thinking about bringing former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani on as his Attorney General, White House sources told Axios on Monday.Axios  Mike Allen wrote that Trump  has recently pondered the idea of nominating Giuliani  for the job currently held by Attorney General Jeff Sessions.The news came soon after Trump s latest broadside at the  beleaguered  head of his Justice Department. So why aren t the Committees and investigators, and of course our beleaguered A.G., looking into Crooked Hillary s crimes & Russia relations?  Trump tweeted on Monday morning.Trump s views on his attorney general have soured in the months since Sessions decided it was best to recuse himself from any investigations involving the Trump campaign, which he was closely associated with. That includes all of the Russia-related investigations, which special counsel Robert Mueller is overseeing.In an interview last week with The New York Times, Trump said he wouldn t have hired Sessions if he knew he d recuse himself from the Russia investigation. So Jeff Sessions takes the job, gets into the job, recuses himself,  Trump said.  I then have   which, frankly, I think is very unfair to the president. How do you take a job and then recuse yourself? If he would have recused himself from the job, I would have said,  Thanks, Jeff, but I can t, you know, I m not going to take you.  It s extremely unfair, and that s a mild word, to the president. So he recuses himself. I then end up with a second man, who s a deputy. When Trump was first selecting his top cabinet officials after winning the November election, Giuliani insisted on being named the secretary of state. He reportedly was not interested in other top posts, including the attorney general.
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames Sessions’ legally required recusal and Mueller’s investigation as illegitimate “swamp pressure,” and it implies—without evidence—that Clinton, Obama, Holder, and Lynch are criminal defendants who must “lawyer up,” thus misusing information to tilt reader perception of both the Justice Department’s independence and the guilt of named political opponents.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to stoke the “deep-state” narrative for a like-minded audience: by framing Sessions’ recusal as “cowering to the swamp,” hyping Giuliani as a fearless purge-agent, and listing Trump’s perceived enemies (Clinton, Obama, Holder, Lynch) with the ominous “better start lawyering up,” the piece aims to intensify outrage against the Justice Department, delegitimize the Mueller probe, and pressure Trump to install an attorney general who will protect the president and prosecute political foes—turning a routine personnel rumor into a call for partisan warfare.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports on a July 2017 Axios story that President Trump was privately musing about replacing Attorney General Jeff Sessions with Rudy Giuliani; it correctly quotes Trump’s contemporaneous public tweets and New York Times interview criticizing Sessions’ recusal, and notes Giuliani’s earlier disinterest in the AG post—none of which is fabricated, so while the piece is opinion-laden it is grounded in real events and sourcing.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports that President Trump was privately discussing replacing Attorney General Jeff Sessions with Rudy Giuliani, as confirmed by Axios sourcing, and it correctly quotes Trump’s public tweets and interview criticisms of Sessions; its partisan framing and unsupported insinuations about other politicians’ guilt are biased spin rather than fabricated facts, so the core reportage is real even if the surrounding commentary is misleading.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is not a fabricated event—it accurately relays Axios’ report that Trump has mused about replacing Sessions with Giuliani—but it weaponizes that kernel of truth by embedding unsupported insinuations (that Clinton, Obama, Holder and Lynch are provably criminal and must “lawyer up”) and by presenting Sessions’ legally mandatory recusal as cowardly capitulation to a “swamp” conspiracy. This selective framing and guilt-by-innuendo turns factual speculation into disinformation whose primary purpose is to delegitimize the Russia probe and incite partisan fervor, satisfying the definition of fake news as real footage used to propagate a false narrative.

title: FLASHBACK VIDEO Shows Leftist Media Members Praising Use Of “Nuclear Option” To Confirm (LIBERAL) Supreme Court Justices
subject: left-news
content: With Senate Republicans poised to use the  nuclear option  to confirm Supreme Court nominee Neil Gorsuch, will the liberal media hypocritically accuse them of a power grab? In 2013, when then-Democratic Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid did basically the same thing, he was cheered on in the studios of MSNBC and CNN.Back then MSNBC s Chris Hayes hailed it as  an affirmative win for democracy,  while his colleague Rachel Maddow blurted  This is a huge freaking deal. This is like 3-inch headlines. This is like people who don t even care about politics really ought to care about this. Over on CNN, political analyst Paul Begala hailed the nakedly partisan maneuver by Reid as necessary, whining that Republicans had  so abused  the filibuster that Democrats  can t take it anymore.  And Begala s colleague Ron Brownstein approved of Reid s decision as a forward-thinking move:  The idea of requiring a super majority for the president to appoint his nominees just is anachronistic. But the cable network news hosts and analysts weren t the only ones championing the nuclear option. On the pages of the Los Angeles Times, Reid s move was celebrated in a November 22 editorial  Democrats bust the filibuster, and good for them. The Times editorial board crowed:  We welcome this action not because it represents a comeuppance for arrogant Republicans but because filibustering presidential nominees is undemocratic and violates the spirit if not the letter of the Constitution, which says that the president shall appoint judges and other officials  by and with the advice and consent of the Senate    not by and with a supermajority of the Senate.  The Times went on to call it  a victory not just for the Democrats but for good government.  Newsbusters
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks 2013 praise for Democrats’ lowering the cloture threshold for executive and lower-court nominees and presents it as blanket endorsement of ‘the nuclear option’ for Supreme Court picks, omitting that Reid’s change explicitly excluded the Supreme Court and that many of the same commentators later condemned McConnell’s 2017 extension to Gorsuch; by conflating the two distinct actions it reframes prior support as hypocrisy, misleading readers about the actual scope and context of the 2013 rule change.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to pre-emptively discredit anticipated liberal criticism of Republicans’ 2017 “nuclear option” by exposing what it portrays as left-wing hypocrisy: selectively celebrating the same procedural change when it benefited Democratic judicial nominees in 2013. By curating 2013 praise from mainstream outlets, the piece frames future objections as partisan rather than principled, thereby delegitimizing them and rallying conservative audiences against a supposedly biased media.

title: The White House Just Issued A Statement On Jeff Sessions’ Treason, And It’s Absolutely SICK
subject: News
content: Trump s newly-minted Attorney General, Jeff Sessions, is apparently just another liar who s looking out more for himself than he is justice. As the head of the Department of Justice, he should be the last person who would ever even consider lying under oath. Yet, lie he did, and now it s coming back to bite him. Democrats are all over him for it, and Trump s White House was forced to issue a statement on this.The thing is, though, that the Trump administration is wholly incapable of admitting wrongdoing in any way, shape or form. So their statement says nothing about Sessions  lies, and instead, blames one of Trump s old foes: the Democrats themselves.WH blames Sessions story on Democrats trying to damage POTUS after speech to Congress. pic.twitter.com/pZ5VcMIeEJ  Jim Acosta (@Acosta) March 2, 2017 This is the latest attack against the Trump Administration by partisan Democrats.  Oh please. If Sessions had, in fact, met with Russian diplomats in his official capacity as a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, then why wouldn t he just say so? Who lies when they re sure they were well within the law and their rights to do something?Seriously. Records literally show that Sessions spoke to the Russian ambassador to the U.S. twice during Trump s presidential campaign. Nobody would lie if they truly believed they were within their legal rights (and the capacity of their job) to speak to anyone, even an enemy.The only conclusion we re left with is that Sessions lied, just like the disgraced General, Michael Flynn, lied. The White House s statement on this is typical   blaming the opposition for everything that goes wrong, including catching people committing perjury. When was the last time we had an administration lie with such impunity? Some will say Obama did, but he didn t. Trump s administration started off with lies, and it s continuing under lies. Sessions must either resign or be indicted, and Trump himself must be impeached.The treason of this administration must stop now.Featured image by Zach Gibson via Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames routine political controversy as 'treason' and presents a one-sided, hyper-partisan interpretation of events—e.g., asserting Sessions ‘lied under oath’ and demanding indictment/impeachment—without balanced evidence or legal context, thereby misleading readers about the gravity and nature of the allegations.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to provoke outrage against the Trump administration by framing Jeff Sessions’ contacts with the Russian ambassador as deliberate, treasonous perjury and by portraying the White House’s deflection of blame onto Democrats as further evidence of systemic deceit; the piece is written not to inform but to galvanize readers into demanding resignations, indictments, and impeachment.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a highly opinionated blog post rather than straight news; it uses inflammatory, partisan language (“Treason,” “SICK,” “must be impeached”) and presents no verifiable evidence that Jeff Sessions committed perjury or treason, only repeating disputed claims and Democratic talking points while offering no balanced sourcing or official legal findings, thereby failing basic journalistic standards for factual reporting.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely labels political controversy as 'treason,' a crime with a specific constitutional definition that is unsupported by any evidence presented; it also misrepresents Sessions’ undisclosed meetings as automatic perjury without acknowledging that no charge, indictment, or bipartisan legal finding ever concluded he committed perjury or treason, making the central claim factually untrue and thus fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: Labeling Sessions’ undisclosed contacts with the Russian ambassador as proven “treason” and “perjury” while simultaneously calling for indictment and impeachment oversteps the known facts and legal standards, turning a legitimate policy controversy into a sensational, evidence-free criminal accusation; this hyper-partisan framing fits the definition of fake news because it presents conjecture and opinion as established criminal reality, misleading readers about the actual legal and factual status of the allegations.

title: Is Conservative Firebrand Laura Ingraham Joining Fox News?
subject: politics
content: Will radio host and television commentator Laura Ingraham become a prime time host at Fox News? The word is that Ingraham will be taking the ten o clock spot.The rumor started when Matt Drudge of The Drudge Report hinted that Ingraham had a spot on Fox lined up.Ingraham has been telling friends that the deal is essentially done, with just a few details to iron out, CNN reports.Ingraham s taking over of ten o clock is part of a larger restructuring of Fox s lineup. Sean Hannity s show will move from its current ten o clock slot to nine p.m. And  The Five  will move back to five p.m. from its current nine o clock time.This shift was almost certainly prompted by the firing of Eric Bolling and concurrent cancelling of Bolling s panel show,  The Specialists,  which previously filled the five o clock slot. Bolling had been under internal investigation following accusations of sexual misconduct on his part, claims which Bolling fervently denies.Bolling s sudden exit is part of a larger shake-up at Fox prompted by allegations of sexual misconduct. Fox Chairman and CEO Roger Ailes left in July 2016, while Bill O Reilly left in April after 21 years at the network, both for similar reasons.It is not known when the show will begin airing, but CNN s sources say that the deal has been confirmed. A Fox News spokeswoman denied the existence of the deal to CNN.We certainly hope this is a done deal. Ingraham gets the Trump voter and isn t in the DC bubble. Her latest tweet about an hour ago says it all:Time to wake up, GOP. @realDonaldTrump is ripping up your dog-eared rulebook. pic.twitter.com/XQD9ZxCjey  Laura Ingraham (@IngrahamAngle) September 12, 2017 Read more: CNN
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents genuine CNN reporting and Drudge-sourced speculation about Laura Ingraham’s possible Fox show, but it is reposted on a blog that adds partisan cheerleading (‘We certainly hope this is a done deal…’) and frames the rumor as virtually accomplished, even though Fox’s own spokeswoman denied any deal. By embedding the original accurate quotes inside a new, ideologically slanted wrapper that treats the rumor as fact, the post gives readers the false impression that the network’s confirmation has already occurred, distorting the original context and certainty of the CNN story.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to amplify an unverified rumor—Laura Ingraham’s imminent 10 p.m. Fox show—by stitching together leaks, blind quotes and prior personnel scandals into a “restructuring” narrative that feels inevitable. By presenting the story as almost-announced fact while simultaneously acknowledging Fox’s denial, the piece maximizes click-through suspense, flatters Ingraham’s pro-Trump brand, and frames the network shake-up as both a response to sexual-misconduct fallout and a savvy ratings play, thereby feeding readers’ appetite for inside-baseball intrigue without supplying any official confirmation.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The report is grounded in credible sourcing: CNN attributes the story to multiple unnamed sources close to the negotiations, and the piece explicitly notes that Fox News declined to confirm the deal, matching standard journalistic practice for unannounced talent moves; the contextual details—such as the prior departures of Ailes, O’Reilly and Bolling and the resulting schedule shuffle—are verifiable public facts, and Ingraham’s own Twitter activity cited in the article is authentic, all indicating the item is a legitimate news report rather than fabrication.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying CNN report and Drudge-sourced speculation are authentic; only the blog’s partisan framing exaggerates certainty, so the core claim that Ingraham is in advanced talks for a 10 p.m. Fox slot remains a real, if unconfirmed, news story.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The core report—CNN and Drudge sourcing that Laura Ingraham is in late-stage talks for a 10 p.m. Fox show, with attendant lineup shifts—is accurate industry chatter; the blog merely repackages this genuine reporting and adds partisan spin, so the underlying facts are real even if the repost exaggerates certainty.

title: Senate Says ENOUGH Of Trump’s Racism, Will Force Him To Go On Legal Record Condemning White Supremacists
subject: News
content: Most of the nation and world watched in horror just a couple of weeks ago as white supremacists, neo-Nazis, Ku Klux Klan members, and other various white power groups descended on Charlottesville, Virginia. Their violent, hateful rally eventually resulted in the death of a brave counter protester, 32-year-old Heather Heyer.As if that weren t bad enough, Donald Trump s response to this racist violence made the situation that had already turned the nation into a tinder box even worse. Instead of condemning white supremacy as any sane, non-bigoted person would, Trump instead made an equivocation between the vile white supremacists and the people there protesting their hate. Only when he was forced to do so did he condemn the violent hate groups by name. However, Trump, being the arrogant, bigoted jackass that he is, could not let that carefully scripted statement stand. In a freewheeling press conference for the ages, Trump ranted for more than half an hour about how the other side was just as bad as the white supremacists. Well, now, it seems that members of the United States Senate are sick of Trump s bigotry and pandering to white supremacists, and they plan to force his hand on the issue.Politico is reporting that a bipartisan group of Senators   Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Warner (D-VA), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), and Cory Gardner (R-CO)- have drawn up a resolution that will have Trump make a legal statement against what happened in Charlottesville. That isn t all it does, though. It also forces Trump, once and for all and on the record, to commit to  rejecting white nationalists, white supremacists, the Ku Klux Klan, neo-Nazis and other hate groups. This is an extraordinary move, considering that resolutions are usually just symbolic in nature and not controversial at all. Generally, they just recognize honorary holidays for people of note and things like that. However, this resolution   dubbed the Charlottesville Resolution   will force Trump to, once and for all, stop winking and nodding at these vile hate groups. Senator Mark Warner said: Let there be no mistake: what happened in Charlottesville was an act of domestic terrorism perpetrated by a white supremacist, one that tragically cut short the life of a young woman, Heather Heyer, who was speaking out against hatred and bigotry. We will be pressing our colleagues to swiftly and unanimously approve this resolution in order to send a strong message that the United States Congress unconditionally condemns racist speech and violence. Senator Tim Kaine said in a statement of his own: During the violent white supremacist demonstrations in Charlottesville last month, our country lost three brave Virginians in Heather Heyer and Virginia State Police officers, Lieutenant Jay Cullen and Trooper Pilot Berke Bates. This resolution honors their lives while supporting the Charlottesville community as it heals and rightfully calls on us all, including President Trump, to do better as we combat acts of hate. The beautiful thing about this is that every single Senator will have to vote in favor of it, lest they be labeled a Nazi sympathizer for the rest of their political careers. While Teflon Don gets away with being an open racist, it has been shown time and time again that these other politicians do not have cults of personality of their own and will not be so fortunate should they attempt the same sort of behavior.To that end, Trump will have no choice but to sign this Charlottesville Resolution, and it will be in the presidential records as long as this republic exists.Featured image via Zach Gibson   Pool/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the bipartisan Senate resolution as a legally binding measure that will 'force' the President to condemn white-supremacist groups and put him 'on legal record,' when in fact congressional resolutions are only symbolic statements with no legal compulsion; by omitting this key distinction and using loaded, derogatory language about the President, the piece misleads readers about the resolution’s actual force and effect.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to galvanize readers against President Trump by portraying him as an unrepentant enabler of white-supremacist violence, and to celebrate a bipartisan Senate maneuver that will finally corner him into a formal, on-record denunciation. By framing the proposed Charlottesville Resolution as both a moral ultimatum and a political trap, the piece seeks to amplify public pressure on every senator—and especially Trump—to align with an anti-racist consensus, while simultaneously shaming anyone who might resist.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately describes a bipartisan Senate resolution introduced in 2017 (S.Res.250) that condemned the Charlottesville white-supremacist rally and called on the President to speak out against hate groups; the named senators—Kaine, Warner, Murkowski, Gardner—did introduce it, the text required Trump to specifically denounce white nationalists, KKK, neo-Nazis, etc., and it passed unanimously on 11 Sept 2017, so while the tone is partisan the underlying facts are verifiable and the event is real.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely claims the Senate resolution will “force” Trump to make a legally binding condemnation, when congressional resolutions are purely symbolic and impose no legal obligation; by presenting this symbolic gesture as a coercive legal act while lacing the report with vitriolic, partisan insults, it fabricates the resolution’s power and thereby misleads readers about the basic mechanics of U.S. lawmaking.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—a bipartisan group of senators introducing a Charlottesville resolution condemning hate groups and urging the president to speak out—is factual and was reported by outlets such as Politico; the article’s slanted language and exaggeration of the resolution’s legal force constitute spin and misleading framing, not fabrication of the core facts, so it remains real news with a strong editorial bias.

title: Yet Another Asshole Just Rammed A Bunch Of Protesters With His Car (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: Yet another horrible human being decided to ram his car through a crowd of protesters in California on Thursday.Daniel Wenzyk, who was convicted of committing lewd acts against a child under the age of 14 in 2006, apparently got impatient as protesters rallied for immigrants  rights and did what we can normally expect from horrible human beings: he tried to run a bunch of people down with his car. disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks the driver’s unrelated 2006 sex-offense conviction and repeatedly labels him a “child molester” to intensify outrage, while simultaneously rejecting the police spokesman’s neutral account by asserting the act was clearly deliberate without presenting verified evidence. This selective emphasis and framing turns a still-unproven assault allegation into a narrative of depraved intent, misleading readers about both the legal status of the incident and the relevance of past convictions.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding aim is to inflame outrage and prejudice, not to inform. By foregrounding the driver’s unrelated sex-offense record, ridiculing police caution, and insisting—before any court verdict—that the act was a deliberate, “hateful” terror attack, the piece weaponizes the incident to validate a pre-set narrative: that opponents of immigration protests are depraved, violent, and abetted by indifferent authorities. The hyperbolic headline, sneering tone, and selective video framing all serve to maximize viral anger and moral condemnation, turning a still-investigated traffic event into click-driven activism.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: Multiple credible outlets (AP, local California news) reported on 26 Oct 2017 that Daniel Wenzek drove slowly through a Brea, CA immigrant-rights protest, injuring six people who were treated at hospital; he was arrested for assault with a deadly weapon, later released pending investigation, and his 2006 sex-offender conviction is a matter of public record, so while the blog’s tone is inflammatory the underlying facts are verifiable and the event did occur.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The core event—Daniel Wenzyk driving into immigration-rights protesters in California on 26 Oct 2017, injuring six—was reported by multiple mainstream outlets (AP, local TV, newspapers) and confirmed by Brea Police; he was arrested for assault with a deadly weapon and later released pending investigation. The article’s factual spine is therefore accurate, even though its editorial tone, repeated invocation of an unrelated 2006 sex-offense conviction, and dismissal of police caution constitute misleading framing rather than fabrication of the incident itself.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: While the underlying incident (a car striking protesters) appears to have occurred, the article’s deliberate insertion of an unrelated 11-year-old sex conviction, overt ridicule of police statements, and insistence—without adjudicated proof—that the act was a purposeful hate crime turn the piece into activist propaganda rather than factual reporting, meeting the criteria for fake news through misleading framing and intent to inflame.

disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the 2016 debate exchange by selectively quoting and exaggerating: it presents Trump’s graphic description (“rip babies out of the womb”) as factual while reducing Clinton’s nuanced defense of late-term abortion to an admission of supporting ‘barbaric’ partial-birth abortion, omitting that the procedure is already illegal except to save the mother’s life. It also repeats long-debunked claims that Planned Parenthood performs no mammograms and sells fetal organs, using these falsehoods to cast Clinton and Democrats as extreme and anti-religion, thereby misleading readers about both the law and the candidates’ positions.

By amplifying Rush Limbaugh’s celebratory framing, the piece seeks to maximize turnout for Trump by fusing abortion, Supreme Court appointments, and alleged persecution of Christians into a single existential stakes narrative, thereby weaponizing emotional outrage to override factual scrutiny.

disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The post cherry-picks Clapper’s ‘not wittingly’ remark and presents it as proof of deliberate lying, omits his later corrections and the contextual complexity of classified surveillance programs, frames his routine end-of-term resignation as a suspicious escape from Trump, and selectively quotes Flynn’s grievance to imply Clapper acted purely out of political malice—thereby distorting the overall record and casting Clapper in the worst possible light without substantiating the alleged wrongdoing.

disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The post takes a real TV clash between Bartiromo and Podesta and embeds it in a fabricated context by repeating the long-debunked claim that Podesta personally received $35 million from Russia while advising Clinton/Obama; this dollar figure stems from a 2016 misreading of a Joule Energy company share transfer to a Podesta-family-held LLC, not a payment to Podesta himself, yet the text presents the fake claim as documentary proof of a 'deep tie' to Russia, thereby weaponizing genuine footage and real events to advance a wholly false narrative.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to delegitimize and discredit John Podesta—and by extension the entire Russia investigation—by framing him as a corrupt Clinton crony who is both guilty of secret Russian payoffs and the real locus of “collusion.” By amplifying a long-debunked financial smear, ridiculing Podesta as a “weasel,” and celebrating Bartiromo’s hostile questioning, the piece seeks to invert the narrative: turning scrutiny away from Trump-campaign contacts with Moscow and toward Democrats, while reinforcing the populist trope that mainstream media and congressional probes are part of a partisan witch-hunt driven by the Clintons and their “guardians.”
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The claim that Russia gave John Podesta $35 million while he advised Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama is a widely debunked conspiracy theory; it conflates a 2011 investment in a company he advised (Joule Unlimited) with a Russian state investment fund (Rusnano), but Podesta did not personally receive money, he held stock options, and he fully divested before entering the Obama White House. No credible evidence supports the $35 million figure or any personal payoff, and fact-checkers (e.g., PolitiFact, Snopes) have rated the allegation false; the article repeats the claim without verification and relies on a Twitter meme as its source, qualifying it as fake news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article repackages a real interview but leans on a long-debunked conspiracy claim that Podesta personally pocketed $35 million from Russia, misrepresenting a 2011 Joule Energy share transfer to an LLC partly owned by his adult children as a direct Kremlin payoff; this falsehood, repeatedly fact-checked and rejected, is presented as documentary proof of corruption, turning genuine footage into disinformation and therefore rendering the overall narrative fake.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article layers a genuine televised exchange with a repeatedly debunked claim—Podesta personally pocketing $35 million from Russia—presenting the falsehood as established fact, thereby weaponizing authentic footage to construct a misleading narrative that delegitimizes Podesta and the Russia probe.

title: Cops SLAM Gun-Crazy GOP Candidate Who Said They Should Be Shot

disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: While the article accurately quotes Fiore’s controversial statement, it frames the entire issue by repeatedly pairing her Second-Amendment activism with loaded terms like ‘gun-crazy,’ ‘domestic terrorists,’ and ‘racist rock star,’ weaving unrelated negative associations that portray her as extremist rather than letting the quote stand on its own, thus using selective emphasis and editorial language to mislead readers about her overall position and character.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit Michele Fiore by spotlighting her most provocative statements—especially the suggestion that citizens may shoot police—then marshaling the emphatic backlash from Nevada’s largest police union to frame her as dangerously extreme, unfit for Congress, and emblematic of a radical, gun-obsessed wing of the GOP.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately quotes Michele Fiore’s televised statement and the Nevada Association of Public Safety Officers’ published letter condemning her; both the union’s letter and Fiore’s televised remarks are verifiable through reputable Nevada news outlets and the union’s own press release, confirming the story is factual, not fabricated.

title: BOOM! MATH SHOWS Trump Would Have Beaten Obama In Romney-Obama Election
subject: left-news
content: It s easy to glance at Tuesday s popular vote   which, with 92 percent of all precincts reporting, shows Hillary Clinton with six million fewer votes than Barack Obama won in 2012   and reach the conclusion that Clinton lost the White House because she failed to turn out the Democratic base. But the truth is much more complicated. While she underperformed relative to Obama s 2012 totals in several Midwestern states   Ohio, Michigan, Iowa, and Wisconsin   Clinton ran virtually even with Obama in the battlegrounds of Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Virginia, Nevada, and New Hampshire. What s more, she far surpassed Obama s 2012 vote total in Florida, the country s biggest swing state. Yet somehow, while Obama carried Florida, Clinton lost it. Which brings us to an important question: Was Donald Trump just good enough to beat a bad Democratic opponent on Tuesday, or does he deserve far more credit?A review of vote totals in the past two elections reveals that Trump 2016 would have defeated Obama 2012 in the electoral college. (Disclaimer: This obviously is an apples-to-oranges exercise because no two elections are the same, nor are any two electorates. Still, unlike debating whether the 2016 Cubs would defeat the 1927 Yankees, this is not an entirely abstract argument; a comparison of their respective performances in the country s most competitive states shows Trump edging Obama in a hypothetical head-to-head matchup.) The math might seem impossible. After all, Obama won nearly 66 million votes in 2012; Trump is currently at 59.5 million and should finish around 60 million, which will actually be one million fewer votes than Mitt Romney won. How, then, could Trump have topped Obama in the electoral college? The answer: Republican turnout lagged in certain parts of the country but shot through the roof in the nation s most critical battleground states. Let s look at them individually, in descending order by population, and do the electoral-vote math. The 2016 totals aren t yet final because not all precincts have reported.FLORIDA   29 EVs   98 percent reportingObama 2012: 4,235,270Clinton 2016: 4,485,745Romney 2012: 4,162,081Trump 2016: 4,605,515Conclusion: Trump beats Obama by some 370,000 votes and wins Florida. (Note: Clinton herself won 250,000 more votes in Florida than Obama did in 2012.) PENNSYLVANIA   20 EVs   97 percent reportingObama 2012: 2,907,448Clinton 2016: 2,844,705Romney 2012: 2,619,583Trump 2016: 2,912,941Conclusion: Trump squeezes past Obama by a margin of some 5,000 votes and wins Pennsylvania. (Note: Clinton runs about 60,000 votes behind Obama, but would ve had more than enough to defeat Romney in 2012.) OHIO   18 EVs   94 percent reportingObama 2012: 2,697,260Clinton 2016: 2,317,001Romney 2012: 2,593,779Trump 2016: 2,771,984Conclusion: Trump edges Obama by roughly 75,000 votes and wins Ohio. (Note: Clinton s worst battleground state showing was Ohio, winning 380,000 [!] fewer votes than Obama.)Stop right there and crunch the numbers: Florida (29) + Pennsylvania (20) + Ohio (18) = 67 EVs.Romney finished with 206 EVs. By protecting all of those, and then taking 67 from Obama, Trump would hit 273 and win the presidency.The question: Did Trump 2016 defeat Obama 2012 in all of the states Romney won? Yes. Here s a look at the competitive ones:  NORTH CAROLINA (98 percent reporting):Trump 2,339,603  Obama 2,178,388  ARIZONA (73 percent reporting):Trump 947,284  Obama 930,669  GEORGIA (93 percent reporting):Trump 2,068,623  Obama 1,761,761  UTAH (78 percent reporting):Trump 360,634  Obama 229,463A review of the Romney 2012 states confirms that Trump, in this hypothetical matchup, would have carried every single one against Obama. It doesn t matter that Obama would have trounced Trump by nearly 300,000 votes in Michigan; by more than 200,000 in Wisconsin; by 175,000 in Virginia; and by 160,000 in Colorado. It s similarly meaningless that Obama would have narrowly defeated Trump in Iowa, Nevada, and New Hampshire. The 44th president carried all of those states in 2012, and in this hypothetical contest, he would successfully defend all of them. But it wouldn t be enough. The electoral college would produce a razor-thin margin: Trump 273, Obama 265.Via: National Review
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece cherry-picks 2016 Trump totals and 2012 Obama totals, pretends they ran against each other in the same electorate, and then presents an Electoral-College “victory” as a factual finding rather than a counter-factual game. By ignoring population growth, turnout differences, and the fact that Obama’s 2012 coalition would have behaved differently if Trump had been on the ballot, the article frames a speculative arithmetic exercise as decisive proof that Trump was inherently the stronger candidate, misleading readers about what actually happened in either election.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to re-frame Donald Trump’s 2016 victory as a historically formidable performance rather than a fluke against a weak opponent. By conjuring a hypothetical Obama-vs-Trump electoral-college showdown and selectively spotlighting the handful of large swing states where Trump’s 2016 numbers topped Obama’s 2012 totals, the piece retroactively inflates Trump’s political stature, delegitimizes claims that he won only because Hillary Clinton was uniquely flawed, and implicitly rebuts narratives that Trump lacked majority appeal. The exercise thus serves less as rigorous analysis than as narrative alchemy: turning a 3-million-vote national deficit into a “math-proven” triumph over a popular two-term president, thereby supplying Trump’s base and right-leaning readers with a triumphant counter-myth grounded in electoral-college what-if-ism.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a speculative counterfactual exercise, not a factual report; it invents a 2016 Trump-vs-2012 Obama matchup that never occurred, cherry-picks partial vote totals from different election years, ignores population growth and turnout differences, and presents an Electoral College tally (273-265) based on apples-to-oranges arithmetic rather than verified results, so it misleads readers into thinking a real electoral outcome was demonstrated when it was merely hypothetical punditry.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents a purely hypothetical, apples-to-oranges comparison as if it were a factual electoral outcome, ignoring that electorates, turnout, and campaign strategies differ between cycles; thus it misleads readers into believing Trump definitively “would have beaten” Obama when no such real-world result exists.

What they saw in the rise of anti-Semitic sentiment and hate crimes here was not a real chance to address hate crimes and speech. They saw an opportunity to squash speech in favor of Palestinian rights in one of the places where it s strongest, and they pounced.This bill encourages the Department of Education to adopt the State Department s definition of anti-Semitism, which includes demonizing and delegitimizing Israel, applying double standards, and focusing on Israel only for human rights investigations.While the bill doesn t actually tell the Department of Education to use the language from the State Department, it does steer them in that direction. The Senate s hope seems to be that when they re investigating schools for anti-Semitic discrimination under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act, they ll sanction schools with heavy anti-Israel sentiment.In fact, the definition is so broad that any speech criticizing Israel could be considered anti-Semitic hate speech, and thus, curbed lest the school get in trouble for daring to allow it.The Senate bill supposedly isn t meant to infringe on anyone s First Amendment right to criticize Israel, so long as they do it in the same way they would criticize any other nation. But we know how it ll actually be used. Groups like the Zionist Organization of America, AIPAC, the Anti-Defamation League, and the Jewish Federations of North America can t stand things like the BDS movement (boycott, divest and sanction) gaining steam. The Zionist Organization of America absolutely loves to file complaints with the Department of Education to try and silence any Palestinian rights speech on campus.That is only likely to increase if this bill becomes law. Students who fight for Palestine because Israel is guilty of murdering them for nothing, is guilty of forcing occupation and subjugating them, and is guilty of all manner of human rights abuses, already work in a heavily repressive environment. This will make that considerably worse.This has been simmering under the surface for a long time. Last year, Ted Cruz delivered a speech to AIPAC talking about how people involved with the BDS movement might end up in prison, depending on what s defined as legal and illegal protest behavior, and said that schools that support the BDS movement should lose their federal dollars.The University of California at Berkeley has faced tons of pressure to squash the BDS movement on their campus. And a student at George Washington University had campus police tell her to take a Palestinian flag out of her window.All of this is done under the idea that speech and expression in support of Palestinian rights are intimidating and frightening to Jewish students. However, a growing number of American Jews have a severe problem with how Israel abuses, oppresses and enslaves Palestine. Yes, it s a balancing act, but every right we have is a balancing act. In this case, the Senate wants to tip that balance towards censoring free speech. Do not expect them to stop there.The broader implication is that censoring pro-Palestine speech on college campuses could lead to censoring other speech on campuses. We do need to combat anti-Semitism along with other forms of hate. This, however, is just the Senate seeing their opening to end pro-Palestine speech on college campuses, likely with the hope that it ll die elsewhere.Featured image via Scott Olson/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the Anti-Semitism Awareness Act as a covert government attempt to 'DESTROY Free Speech' by equating criticism of Israel with anti-Semitism, but it omits that the bill only asks the Education Dept. to consider the State Dept. definition when investigating whether existing civil-rights-protected students are facing harassment; it creates no new speech ban, leaves final determinations to OCR/DoE, and explicitly states it must be applied in a manner consistent with the First Amendment, so presenting it as a blanket censorship tool is an intentional misrepresentation to provoke outrage.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame the Anti-Semitism Awareness Act not as a good-faith effort to curb anti-Jewish bigotry, but as a cynical, politically motivated weapon that will let pro-Israel groups and the federal government suppress campus criticism of Israel and the Palestinian-rights movement under the guise of fighting anti-Semitism; by presenting the bill as the opening wedge of a broader campus-speech crackdown, the piece seeks to rally opposition to the legislation and to portray pro-Palestine activists as the real victims of censorship.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately describes the Senate's December 2023 passage of the Anti-Semitism Awareness Act, which directs the Department of Education to consider the State Department’s IHRA definition of antisemitism—including examples related to criticism of Israel—when enforcing Title VI civil-rights complaints. While the piece’s rhetoric is hyperbolic and opinion-laden, the underlying facts (bill text, sponsor statements, prior House passage, and advocacy-group reactions) are verifiable and reported by mainstream outlets, so the core claim that the Senate advanced legislation that could chill campus speech critical of Israel is real.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece falsely presents the Anti-Semitism Awareness Act as a sweeping censorship statute that will “destroy” campus free speech, when in reality the bill merely tells the Education Department to consult the State Department’s working definition of anti-Semitism when deciding whether conduct already prohibited under Title VI civil-rights law is motivated by anti-Jewish animus; it does not criminalize or ban any speech, explicitly preserves First-Amendment protections, and leaves ultimate enforcement decisions to OCR/DoE. By omitting these limiting facts and repeatedly asserting that routine criticism of Israel will be punished, the article fabricates a threat of blanket suppression, fitting the pattern of a politically motivated hoax rather than accurate reporting.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article falsely claims the Act 'DESTROYs' free speech by equating Israel criticism with anti-Semitism and creating campus bans, whereas the bill only directs the Education Department to consider the State Department definition when investigating whether existing civil-rights-protected students are targets of harassment, explicitly preserves First Amendment rights, and creates no new speech prohibitions or penalties.

title: TERROR-TIED GROUP Plans In-Your-Face Parade Float At Tomorrow’s Veterans’ Day Parade

If you live in the Tulsa, Oklahoma area, please go and protest this float.The Islamic hate group CAIR is taunting our veterans and military personnel with this latest stunt.
