title: Trump To Gut Coast Guard, Airport Security, And FEMA To Fund Useless Border Wall
subject: News
content: Donald Trump s obsession with building a massive expensive wall along the Mexican border is literally going to make America less secure.Despite claiming that he will beat back terrorism and keep Americans safe, Trump is drafting a budget proposal that would cripple three of the nation s most critical agencies that do way more to help Americans than any wall will ever do.The cost of Trump s wall is projected to reach past $20 billion. During the campaign, Trump repeatedly claimed that Mexico would pay for the wall, but it s clear now that American taxpayers will be footing the bill. And rather than create a new budget item, Trump is considering just cutting funding from existing national security and national emergency management agencies to use it to pay for the wall instead.On the chopping block includes the U.S. Coast Guard, a crucial branch of the military that patrols and secures our ports, coast lines, and waterways, defending them from potential terrorist attacks and rescuing people.This particular cut is fiercely opposed by Republican Rep. Duncan Hunter, who explained on CNN Wednesday why the Coast Guard is too important to slash. You have President Trump talking about security, criminal networks   that s what the Coast Guard does, literally!  Hunter said.  So how can the president talk about  stopping illegal immigration, illegal drugs, and criminal narco networks, and then say we re going to cut the military and cut the Coast Guard? The way you stop bad things from happening here is not directly on the border, necessarily. So this is nonsensical to me. But that s not all.According to the Washington Post,The proposal, drawn up by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), also would slash the budget of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, which provides disaster relief after hurricanes, tornadoes and other natural disasters. The Coast Guard s $9.1 billion budget in 2017 would be cut 14 percent to about $7.8 billion, while the TSA and FEMA budgets would be reduced about 11 percent each to $4.5 billion and $3.6 billion, respectively.In regards to the Transportation Security Administration, Trump plans to cut post-9/11 programs, which includes a program that trains airline crews how to deal with hijackers, a program that funds the use of special law enforcement teams that sweep transportation hubs for potential threats prior to and during major events like an inauguration, a program that gives local law enforcement more ability to patrol in and around airports, and a program that funds the use of special TSA agents who are trained to specifically detect people exhibiting odd behavior at check-points.In other words, programs that  have been considered a vital piece of airport security and for preventing a repetition of the Sept. 11, 2001, hijackings So Trump is literally looking to sacrifice programs designed to prevent another 9/11 in order to build a wall that most experts consider useless in stopping immigration.Donald Trump is once again demonstrating that he cares more about himself than he does about the safety and security of the American people. The Coast Guard protects our coastal boarders from inside and outside threats. The TSA helps prevent another 9/11 attack from occurring on American soil. And FEMA responds to help Americans before, during, and after a disaster strikes. Gutting these agencies doesn t make America safer. It makes us more vulnerable and that appears to be exactly what Trumps wants.If it wasn t clear enough before, it definitely is now. Trump is the greatest threat to our national security.Featured image via Mark Wallheiser/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks preliminary OMB budget-drafting options as if they were final policy, omits that Congress ultimately sets appropriations, uses loaded language ('useless wall', 'Trump is the greatest threat'), and presents worst-case percentage cuts without noting that subsequent budgets restored or increased funding for Coast Guard, TSA and FEMA, thereby framing the issue in a way that exaggerates both the certainty and the national-security impact of the proposal.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame President Trump’s proposed budget reallocations as a direct betrayal of his “security-first” rhetoric, arguing that by slashing funds for the Coast Guard, TSA, and FEMA to finance a border wall he is knowingly weakening the very agencies that protect Americans from terrorism, natural disasters, and other threats. By amplifying alarmist language—“gutting,” “cripple,” “greatest threat to our national security”—the piece seeks to delegitimize the wall as a vanity project, cast Trump as hypocritically endangering the nation, and galvanize public opposition to the budget cuts.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reflects the 2017 budget proposal reported by reputable outlets like the Washington Post, which stated that the Trump administration’s Office of Management and Budget proposed cutting the Coast Guard, TSA, and FEMA budgets—by 14 % and 11 % respectively—to help fund border-wall construction; Republican Rep. Duncan Hunter and others publicly criticized these cuts at the time, confirming the basic facts, although the piece’s polemical tone and claim that Trump is “the greatest threat to our national security” are opinion, not factual assertions.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece misrepresents an early-stage OMB draft as a finalized Trump decision, omits Congress’s constitutional control over appropriations, inflates the proposed cuts by ignoring later restorations, and uses hyperbolic labels (‘useless wall’, ‘greatest threat’) to create a false narrative that Trump actually gutted Coast Guard, TSA and FEMA funding for the border wall—something that never happened in enacted budgets.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece misrepresents an internal OMB draft as enacted policy, ignores Congress’s constitutional power over final appropriations, and weaponizes selective, outdated figures while omitting later budget restorations; its loaded framing thus fabricates a false narrative that Trump definitively gutted homeland-security agencies to fund the wall.

title: ILLEGAL ALIEN WHO MURDERED INNOCENT WOMAN WAS DEPORTED 3 TIMES: Obama’s Solution To Increasing Crime By Illegals…Cut Back On Deportations
subject: politics
content: Because we don t have enough crime in our country already we need to import it from Mexico and South America.To hell with America it s all about the votes The man suspected of gunning down a young woman at random at a popular San Francisco tourist spot on Wednesday has been  deported to Mexico several times,  according to a report by the local ABC News affiliate. The woman, 32-year-old Kathryn Steinle ( Kate ), was struck in the chest with a bullet while visiting Pier 14 on the Embarcadero with her family. She was rushed to a nearby hospital but doctors were unable to save her, as she died in her parents  arms a few hours later.The suspect, Francisco Sanchez, was identified as being in his mid-40s and on probation from Texas due to previous, undisclosed crimes. He was arrested after tips from passers-by. Officials said that the killing appeared to be random. Police believe they have recovered the murder weapon from the waters of the San Francisco Bay near the pier, where the suspect allegedly tossed it.On Thursday, two news crews filming live at Pier 14 were mugged at the scene, and one cameraman was pistol-whipped.The San Francisco Chronicle described Steinle s last moments in heartbreaking detail: She fought for her life,  [Liz] Sullivan said, adding that her daughter s heart had stopped two times, and was restarted, in the ambulance. It was a battle, but she just didn t make it,  she said.  It was horrific, but we knew the minute they came to talk to us, it wasn t good. But it was so nice to go in and be with her. Sullivan said that in their final moments together, she softly touched her daughter s face   a face she used to paint when the young woman was a little girl. We have deep faith,  Jim Steinle said, adding,  Our faith isn t to the point where we re ready to forgive.   Via: Breitbart NewsOBAMA S SOLUTION TO ILLEGAL CRIME IN AMERICA:Washington Post  The Obama administration has begun a profound shift in its enforcement of the nation s immigration laws, aiming to hasten the integration of long-term illegal immigrants into society rather than targeting them for deportation, according to documents and federal officials.In recent months, the Department of Homeland Security has taken steps to ensure that the majority of the United States  11.3 million undocumented immigrants can stay in this country, with agents narrowing enforcement efforts to three groups of illegal migrants: convicted criminals, terrorism threats or those who recently crossed the border.While public attention has been focused on the court fight over President Obama s highly publicized executive action on immigration, DHS has with little fanfare been training thousands of immigration agents nationwide to carry out new policies on everyday enforcement.
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks one horrific crime, omits that the shooter’s seven prior felonies made him a priority for deportation under Obama’s 2014 policy (which San Francisco’s sanctuary ordinance ignored), and presents a policy shift toward focusing limited resources on serious criminals as a blanket ‘cut-back on deportations,’ thereby framing the administration as complicit in the murder and encouraging the false belief that undocumented immigrants collectively import crime, when data show lower crime rates among them.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to weaponize a single tragic crime to inflame anti-immigrant sentiment and blame the Obama administration for supposedly inviting violence by “importing criminals” through a deliberate rollback of deportations. By foregrounding the victim’s final moments, repeating the suspect’s prior deportations, and framing the policy shift as an open-borders scheme to “hasten integration,” the text seeks to convert grief into political outrage, implying that any restraint in mass deportation equals reckless disregard for American lives and that Democratic leaders value future votes over public safety.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The core facts—Kate Steinle’s 2015 fatal shooting on San Francisco’s Pier 14, the arrest of Francisco Sanchez (a Mexican national with multiple prior deportations), the city’s sanctuary policy, and the Obama-era DHS narrowing of removal priorities to focus on recent border-crossers, national-security threats, and convicted serious criminals—are all documented in contemporaneous reports by the San Francisco Chronicle, ABC7, the Washington Post, and federal court filings; the article’s partisan framing and loaded language do not alter the veracity of those underlying events.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is built on selective facts and distortions: it weaponizes a single tragedy to imply Obama caused it by “cutting deportations,” when in fact his 2014 policy designated the shooter’s seven felonies as top-priority for removal; San Francisco’s sanctuary ordinance, not federal policy, blocked hand-over to ICE. Presenting a resource-driven focus on serious criminals as blanket amnesty, and implying undocumented migrants raise crime (they don’t), makes the article misleading propaganda rather than factual reporting.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The story is built on a true homicide, but it is packaged as disinformation: it omits that Obama’s 2014 guidelines explicitly flagged repeat felons like Sanchez for removal, accuses the administration of ‘cutting back deportations’ when overall removals were higher than under Bush, and uses a single anecdote to imply undocumented migrants raise U.S. crime rates even though multiple studies show they offend less than citizens—making the article’s core narrative demonstrably false and intentionally misleading.

title: BUSTED: YOUNG NJ DEMOCRAT CHAIRMAN CAUGHT PUNCHING 75 YR OLD BLIND VETERAN VOLUNTEERING AT POLLS [Video]
subject: politics
content: As a poll challenger who has witnessed unbelievable blatant voter fraud by Democrats, I can only imagine what this poll worker might have done to cross this Democrat chairman.The chairman of the Essex County Democratic Committee in New Jersey is accused of punching a blind Army veteran following an argument at a polling location during East Orange s council primary last month.Video was released purportedly showing Leroy Jones punching 75-year-old Bill Graves, who was volunteering as a poll worker during the incident on primary day, June 2.  I hear this rumbling,  Where the blank is Bill Graves? I m gonna kick his butt!  Mr. Graves told a local ABC affiliate.  You can see on the tape it was intentional. The suspect, identified by Essex County Prosecutors as Mr. Jones, is seen throwing several punches at Mr. Graves following what appears to be a heated confrontation.Mr. Graves and his friends said Mr. Jones attacked him because he was backing a political candidate that Mr. Jones did not support, ABC reported.Mr. Jones, however, said he was defending his wife, who was also working at the polls. Mr. Jones said the veteran got aggressive with his wife during an argument, and she called her husband for help, a local CBS affiliate reported. This man threatened my wife. This man assaulted my wife. This man charged at my wife,  Mr. Jones said.Mr. Jones has been charged with simple assault, reports said. Mr. Graves was not charged.Mr. Graves, who is completely blind in one eye and legally blind in the other, said his vision has gotten worse since the attack. Angry, disgusted, because why should I have to run back and forth to the doctor because someone decided to hit me,  he told ABC.  It s not good, that s all I can say. I m smiling, but I m not laughing. Via: Washington Times
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline and lead sentence frame the story as a partisan attack (‘Democrat Chairman Caught Punching…’) and invite readers to infer that the blind veteran was targeted for uncovering ‘blatant voter fraud,’ yet the body of the report shows only a local primary-day scuffle with competing he-said/she-said accounts, no evidence of fraud, and both men offering self-defense narratives; by omitting that context and foregrounding party ID and the victim’s military service, the post weaponizes selective emphasis to inflame political outrage rather than inform.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s intent is to inflame partisan outrage by presenting the incident as emblematic of Democratic violence and corruption, using emotionally charged framing (“BUSTED,” “blind veteran,” “Democrat chairman”) and unsubstantiated insinuations of voter fraud to galvanize a right-wing audience against the political left.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: Multiple reputable outlets (ABC, CBS, Washington Times) reported the same core facts: Essex County Democratic Chairman Leroy Jones was captured on video punching 75-year-old, visually-impaired poll worker Bill Graves on 2 June, was charged with simple assault, and both men gave conflicting motives; no outlet has retracted or debunked the story, so it is a verified incident despite partisan framing in some retellings.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The physical altercation itself is documented on video and has been reported by multiple mainstream outlets; Leroy Jones was in fact charged with simple assault, so the core event is verifiable.  Labeling it 'Fake' would be incorrect, even though the partisan framing, unsupported voter-fraud insinuation, and selective emphasis constitute misleading content that distorts rather than fabricates the episode.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The core event—an altercation between Essex County Democratic Chairman Leroy Jones and poll worker/veteran Bill Graves on 2 June, resulting in a simple-assault charge against Jones—was reported by multiple mainstream outlets (ABC, CBS, Washington Times) and confirmed by the Essex County Prosecutor; while the viral post injects partisan spin and unsupported voter-fraud insinuations, the underlying physical incident is factual and documented, making the story real despite its misleading framing.

title: UPDATE: JUDGE ORDERS CANCELLATION OF REDSKINS TRADEMARK REGISTRATION – WASHINGTON REDSKIN’S NEW STADIUM CONSTRUCTION HELD HOSTAGE BY PETTY OBAMA ADMINISTRATION
subject: Government News
content: UPDATE ON THE REDSKINS BATTLE WITH THE FEDS:ALEXANDRIA, Va. (AP)   A federal judge has ordered the Patent and Trademark Office to cancel registration of the Washington Redskins  trademark, ruling that the team name may be disparaging to Native Americans.The ruling Wednesday by Judge Gerald Bruce Lee affirms an earlier finding by an administrative appeal board.In his 70-page ruling, Lee emphasized that the organization is still free to use the name if it wishes   the team would just lose some legal protections that go along with federal registration of a trademark.The team had sued to overturn a ruling against it by the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board. The team argued that cancellation of its trademark infringed on its free-speech rights because it required the government to judge whether the name is offensive.The organization can appeal.Via: scrippsmediaThe left is holding hostage new construction of the Washington Redskins stadium for a petty desire to get their way. Demanding a name change from the Redskins to something they consider more pc is total bs. The American Indians who have already responded in favor of keeping the team name understand the name isn t offensive and understand the history behind the name. This is just more of Obama s effort to cleanse our nation of anything HE deems offensive.Efforts to lure the Washington Redskins back to the District have come up against a potentially insurmountable challenge: the Obama administration s objections to the team s name.Interior Secretary Sally Jewell told D.C. Mayor Muriel E. Bowser this spring that the National Park Service, which owns the land beneath Robert F. Kennedy Memorial Stadium, was unlikely to accommodate construction of a new stadium for the Redskins unless the team changes its name.Jewell oversees both national park land and America s trust and treaty relationships with Native American tribes.Her decision not to extend the District s lease of the RFK land badly hinders Bowser s bid to return the Redskins to D.C.   and boosts efforts to lure the team across the Potomac to Northern Virginia.Since joining the Obama administration two years ago, Jewell has repeatedly echoed the president s concern that the name is offensive to Native Americans. Last fall she called the name a  relic of the past  that should be changed. Personally, I think we would never consider naming a team the  Blackskins  or the  Brownskins  or the  Whiteskins.  So, personally, I find it surprising that in this day and age, the name is not different,  Jewell told ABC News.Jewell reiterated that position with Bowser (D) at an April 27 meeting, telling the mayor that she was unlikely to rework the lease terms for a stadium in part because of the team s name, according to a Department of the Interior spokeswoman, Jessica Kershaw.Team owner Daniel Snyder, who insists that the moniker honors Native Americans, has vowed never to change it.Bowser, jockeying with Virginia Gov. Terry McAuliffe (D) to land the team s new stadium, had inquired with Park Service officials about extending the District s lease for the RFK property to allow for a new stadium. Extending the lease would also require congressional action.[Tug of war for new Redskins stadium is complicated by name debate]Jewell  did mention in that meeting that she was uncomfortable with the name,  Kershaw said.  The president has said something similar, that he is uncomfortable with the name, and she clearly clarified that position. Read more: WaPo
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the trademark-cancellation ruling and the Interior Secretary’s reluctance to lease RFK land as a purely political, Obama-led vendetta, omitting that the court and the Patent Office acted under long-standing law against disparaging marks and that the land-use stance follows stated federal trust responsibilities to tribes; by casting every official action as petty hostage-taking while presenting only the team-owner’s view as fact, it misleads readers about the legal, procedural, and moral bases of the controversy.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame the federal government’s actions—both the trademark cancellation and the refusal to lease land for a new stadium—as politically motivated, petty persecution of the Washington Redskins by the Obama administration. By casting Native American objections as insignificant and dismissing the name controversy as mere “PC” culture, the author seeks to rally opposition to what is portrayed as government overreach, while defending the team name as historically benign and honoring Native Americans.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports that in 2015 a federal judge affirmed cancellation of the Washington Redskins’ federal trademark registration because the name may be disparaging, and it correctly notes that the Obama administration—specifically Interior Secretary Sally Jewell—opposed building a new stadium on federally owned RFK land unless the team changed its name, positions widely covered by the Associated Press, ABC News and The Washington Post at the time; the headline’s loaded language and partisan framing do not negate the underlying factual events, so the core news is real.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: While the article is laced with partisan commentary, the underlying events—a federal judge’s order cancelling the Redskins trademark registration and the Interior Secretary’s stated unwillingness to lease RFK land for a new stadium unless the name changes—are verifiable public actions reported by multiple outlets; the piece’s bias and selective framing constitute misleading content, not fabrication of facts, so the news itself is real even if its interpretation is slanted.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article misrepresents independent court and agency decisions as a politically orchestrated Obama vendetta, suppresses the legal basis for canceling disparaging trademarks, and falsely claims Native Americans overwhelmingly support the name, thereby distorting facts to advance a partisan narrative rather than report verifiable events.

title: TV EXECUTIVES In Discussion About CANCELLING Thursday Night NFL Games
subject: politics
content: Capitalism at work. It s funny how the loss of real money has a way of helping to remind NFL owners and the networks who support them, who are writing the checks. One hint it s not the guys disrespecting our flag.Network executives are scrambling to solve the growing problem of crashing ratings for the National Football League, by cutting games to end the perceived  over-saturation  of football on TV.To put an end to the sliding ratings, the executives are proposing that fewer games may be the ticket to stop that  over-saturation,  with one idea being to cut Thursday Night Football by a whopping ten games.The idea to trim Thursday Night Football from 18 games a season to only eight was first reported by Sports Business Journal and was part of a plan to reverse the ratings crash that also includes pulling games played in the U.K. back to 1 PM eastern time (6PM London time).Indeed the amount of football on TV has exploded in the last decade.Ratings are still down despite the small rise seen in Week 7. NBC Sports is off 21 percent from 2015, CBS Sports is down 14 percent compared to 2015, and ESPN s Monday Night Football has sunk 17 percent over 2015. -BreitbartRasmussen reports that nearly one-third (32 percent) of adults say they re less likely to watch NFL game telecasts because of the Kaepernick-led player protests against racial injustice. The telephone/online survey of 1,000 American adults was conducted Oct. 2-3.This letter from a die-hard Pittsburg Steelers fan hits the nail on the head, as it relates to how NFL fans feel about the players who continue to disrespect our flag: I want to thank you for freeing up my Sundays. Some of the earliest memories of my life are watching Steelers games with my dad. I was once a season-ticket holder. I have occasionally missed a few games on TV through the years due to scheduling conflicts, but I can honestly say in my 44 years of living, I have never intentionally turned off a Steelers game. That changed today. As I sat down to watch the Steelers-Bears game today, I learned from the sideline reporter that the Steelers chose not to participate in the national anthem. I realize that there is a lot of injustice in our country. I realize that there are a lot of people upset at the current administration. I realize that we live in a free country where people have the freedom to not participate in the national anthem. I also have the freedom to not spend another minute or dollar on your product. I am of the opinion that this is quite possibly the worst way to go about  protesting.  If you want to hold a rally at Heinz Field to allow your players to voice their opinions, that would be fine. If you want all the Steelers and NFL players to march on Washington D.C., fine. But to not participate in the national anthem is an insult to every serviceman who has served or has passed away defending this country. If you are truly that unhappy with the country, feel free to play for the CFL. So thank you, Steelers and NFL, for freeing up my Sundays. I will no longer waste my time or money watching your product. The weather today the in Pittsburgh area is beautiful and I can not think of a better day to spend it outside, away from the TV.   Jim Coletti, former fan
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the NFL’s ratings decline as overwhelmingly caused by anthem protests, citing a single 2017 Rasmussen poll and one fan letter while ignoring concurrent factors cited by industry analysts—competition from streaming, cord-cutting, injuries, match-ups, and overall TV fragmentation. By cherry-picking data and anecdotes, it misleads readers into believing protest backlash is the primary driver of network discussions about reducing Thursday games, when internal leaks show scheduling fatigue and carriage-fee economics are the central issues.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to frame the NFL’s ratings decline as a direct, market-driven punishment for the player protests—especially the kneeling during the anthem—by weaving together selective ratings data, anecdotal fan outrage, and the specter of lost ad revenue. By foregrounding the Breitbart/Rasmussen claim that “disrespect for the flag” is driving viewers away, the piece weaponizes economic anxiety to delegitimize the players’ racial-justice message and pressure the league into silencing future protest.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The core claim—that TV executives have discussed reducing the Thursday Night Football package from 18 to 8 games—was first reported by the well-sourced Sports Business Journal and has since been echoed by other industry outlets; while Breitbart’s framing emphasizes player protests as the driver of ratings declines, the underlying negotiation about over-saturation and potential schedule reduction is an authentic industry discussion, making the item real news despite its partisan editorial spin.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not fabricated, but it is deliberately misleading: it presents a fringe, politically-charged narrative—anthem protests are the ratings killer—as the dominant explanation for talks of cutting Thursday games, while ignoring overwhelming industry evidence that scheduling fatigue, cord-cutting, streaming competition, carriage-fee disputes and poor match-ups are the actual drivers. By cherry-picking one 2017 poll and an angry fan letter, it weaponizes selective facts to create a false causal story, satisfying the definition of disinformation even though the underlying leak about fewer Thursday games is real.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece presents real events—declining NFL ratings and talks of cutting Thursday games—but falsely attributes the downturn almost exclusively to anthem protests, suppressing the dominant industry explanations (streaming competition, cord-cutting, scheduling fatigue, carriage-fee disputes). By cherry-picking a 2017 poll and one angry fan letter while omitting the fuller context reported by mainstream sports-media, it constructs a politically charged, misleading narrative that distorts why networks are considering fewer games.

title: Your Taxes Buy Billionaires Stadiums, They Charge You $7 For A Hot Dog — Obama Says NO MORE
subject: News
content: Imagine you re a billionaire who buys himself an NFL team. You re obviously doing well if you can afford to even consider such a venture, but you re about to start raking it in big time. At an average of $85 per ticket, 70,000 people or so are going to come pouring through the gates.They aren t allowed to bring any food or drinks with them, of course, so if they get hungry they ll be feasting on $7.50 hot dogs and $16 cheese steaks. If you toss a couple of Oreos in the fryer at a cost of about 30 cents they ll fork over another six bucks. That s not including the drinks. The bottom of the barrel at most stadiums is the $5 bottled water.Owners love to chalk up the price of tickets and concessions to the amount of money they pay their players. That certainly does factor in, but if you walk through your local mall you ll see ridiculous amounts of merchandise from teddy bears to framed pictures, hats, jerseys, shoes and even pet clothing with your team s logo on them. it s not there for free. Multiply that times every mall in a team s fan base and what you have is an entity that is so ridiculously profitable it goes beyond description.Why, then, are we footing the bill to build these elitist one percenters new stadiums? With very few exceptions, when an owner wants a stadium, they go directly to those whose campaigns they donate to and get the ball rolling on state funds. They sell fans on voting for these funds because  don t you want to have a nicer stadium than the one in Philly?  Ask a Washington fan the answer to that one.At the federal level, owners bilk all of us out of tax dollars through a tax exemption on bond interest that means that even if you live in Billings Montana with no chance of ever going to a Wranglers game (because your market is too small for such a team to exist in any sport), you re paying for that shiny new facility they re planning in Los Angeles.According to a 2012 Bloomberg report, the exemption amounts to roughly $4 billion in federal taxpayer money. In President Obama s FY2017 budget, the exemption is eliminated, which would create a savings of $542 million for the year and hopefully create a more cost-conscious building process for stadiums that will still be footed largely by taxpayers at the state and local level.It s welfare for billionaires. A family of four can save for a year and spend upwards of a thousand dollars for a single afternoon at Texas Stadium, but Jerry Jones should be able to be exempt from millions in taxes because he has so much debt on a stadium he could have written a check for.The Presidents proposal will, of course, be met with Republican opposition, because they are in the business of giving billionaires as much of your money as possible.Featured image from cowboyzone.com
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The piece cherry-picks figures (e.g., the 2012 $4 billion estimate and the $542 million one-year federal revenue projection) to imply that every stadium deal is pure federal welfare for billionaires, obscuring that the tax-exempt bond benefit applies only to a subset of projects, that many stadium bonds are repaid from local taxes or team revenues, and that Obama’s proposal was a single budget line never enacted; it also conflates federal subsidy with state/local spending to overstate the average taxpayer’s burden and presents concession prices as evidence of taxpayer fleecing when those prices are set by market demand, not by the bond subsidy.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to provoke public outrage over the practice of using taxpayer money to subsidize stadiums for ultra-wealthy sports-team owners. By highlighting the contrast between billionaires’ profits and fans’ escalating costs, the piece aims to delegitimize the federal tax-exemption on stadium bonds as “welfare for billionaires,” rally support for President Obama’s 2017 proposal to end it, and frame Republican resistance as further evidence of a rigged system that prioritizes the rich over ordinary citizens.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately describes the federal tax-exemption on municipal bonds used for stadium construction (a 1986 loophole) and cites President Obama’s FY2017 budget proposal to eliminate it, which the Treasury estimated would save $542 million that year; Bloomberg and other outlets reported the same $4 billion lifetime revenue loss figure, so the core facts are verifiable, even if the editorial tone is partisan.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is rooted in a real policy debate—Obama’s 2017 budget did propose ending tax-exempt bonds for stadiums, and academic studies confirm that federal and local subsidies are common—but it exaggerates by implying every stadium is a pure federal hand-out and by conflating concession pricing with taxpayer cost, making it misleading rather than fabricated.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports an actual 2017 Obama budget proposal to end tax-exempt bond interest for sports stadiums and cites verifiable Bloomberg cost estimates; while it uses emotionally loaded framing and oversimplifies how often federal subsidies occur, the underlying facts—existence of the tax break, its federal cost, and the proposal—are accurate, so it is real news, not fabricated.

title: Trump Attacks President Obama For Trying To Make Peace With Iran, Denies He Is Putin’s Puppet
subject: News
content: Donald Trump is once again whining about the media investigating his ties to Russia, and attacked President Obama in the process.Despite having extensive business ties in Russia and connections to Vladimir Putin, whom he admires, Trump claimed in a Tuesday morning Twitter tantrum that he doesn t know the Russian tyrant nor does he have any deals there. And Trump appeared to try and excuse any deals he may have by attacking President Obama for making a diplomatic deal with Iran.I don t know Putin, have no deals in Russia, and the haters are going crazy   yet Obama can make a deal with Iran, #1 in terror, no problem!  Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) February 7, 2017First of all, Trump has plenty of business and financial ties to Russia.According to Time,[F]or all of his denials of Russian ties lately, Trump has boasted in the past of his many meetings with Russian oligarchs. During one trip to Moscow, Trump bragged that they all showed up to meet him to discuss projects around the globe.  Almost all of the oligarchs were in the room  just to meet with him, Trump said at the time.And when Trump built a tower in Panama, his clients were wealthy Russians, the Washington Post reported.  Russians make up a pretty disproportionate cross-section of a lot of our assets. title: Sunday’s Massacre In Texas Bumped Columbine Out Of The Top Ten Deadliest US Mass Shootings
subject: News
content: It s been more than 18 years, but anyone who was alive at the time will remember when they first heard the news that Eric David Harris, 18, and Dylan Bennet Klebold, 17, two students from Columbine High School in Littleton, Colorado, had shot and killed 12 of their fellow students, plus one teacher and wounded 21 additional people, before turning their guns on themselves in the school s library on that fateful morning of April 20, 1999. The pair were also packing almost 100 explosives in what USA Today described as a  suicidal attack [that was] planned as a grand if badly implemented terrorist bombing. At the time it was almost impossible to conceive a greater tragedy, two lonely teenage outcasts feeling the need to take so many innocent young lives on just a regular day at school. Sure, there had been other mass-shootings of a greater scale, but Columbine is still the worst US high school shooting on record, was the second-worst mass-shooting on any school campus at the time behind the 1966 University of Texas massacre, and the fifth-worst mass-shooting on US soil.Fast-forward less than two decades later and the murder spree at Columbine High School no longer even cracks the top-10 when it comes to the worst single-day mass-shootings in modern US history. What makes the statistics even more terrifying is that the five worst mass-shootings in the United States and six of the top-10, have all occurred in the last 10 years. To make matters worse, three of the top-5 were in the past 18 months.Here are the 10 worst single-day mass-shootings in modern US history, counting victims only. In each instance, the shooter s death has been omitted.Which brings us to Eric Harris, Dylan Klebold, and the Columbine High School massacre. To many, that is one of the worst tragedies the human mind can conjure up   Just a couple of misunderstood teenagers who sought the justice of who they saw as their transgressors by running riot on their school and shooting at anyone in their path, resulting in 13 deaths, before killing themselves. This incident is no longer one of the 10 worst mass-shootings in modern US history, but something needs to be done before it drops any lower.Featured image via screenshot
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents accurate historical facts about Columbine and later mass-shootings, but it frames the issue in a way that implies Columbine is being ‘demoted’ in significance because newer tragedies have higher body counts. This numeric ranking implicitly suggests that a shooting’s importance is measured only by its death toll, which can mislead readers into thinking Columbine’s cultural, policy, and social impacts have diminished, when in reality its influence on school safety, gun-control debate, and pop culture remains profound. Thus the piece uses truthful data to create a misleading narrative about the relative ‘severity’ or newsworthiness of these events.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to shock the reader into recognizing how rapidly the scale of American mass-shootings has escalated: by pointing out that the once-unimaginable Columbine massacre has already been pushed out of the “top-10” list, the piece frames ever-higher body counts as a normalized, accelerating trend and implicitly argues that legislative or societal action is urgently needed before the atrocity is dwarfed by even deadlier events.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately recounts the 1999 Columbine shooting (13 killed, 24 injured), correctly notes that it has since been surpassed by more recent mass-shootings, and provides verifiable data that align with official records and reputable news sources; no fabricated events or false statistics are presented.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: Every factual claim—dates, casualty counts, rankings, and the observation that Columbine has fallen out of the top-10 deadliest U.S. mass-shootings—is verifiable and accurate; the article is therefore real news, even though its narrative framing (ranking tragedies by body count) can be seen as misleading or insensitive.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article reports verifiable facts about the casualty counts of Columbine and subsequent U.S. mass-shootings; its framing is interpretive rather than fabricated, so despite the numeric ranking potentially skewing perception of significance, the underlying data and events are authentic, making it real news.

title: REPORTER TO CLINTON: ‘So you still blame others more than yourself for loss?’ [VIDEO]
subject: politics
content: British TV journalist Matt Frei asked Hillary Clinton if she s still blaming other more than herself in an interview Friday: Your dynastic appeal or perhaps it was the opposite: The fact that you were called Clinton the fact that you were first lady basically trumped any novelty if you forgive the term of being the first female president of the United States,  he said. Clinton answered in her usual delusional way by laying out the amount of support she THINKS she received and then blaming former FBI director James Comey and the Russians for her defeat: That doesn t explain why I led all the way through, why I won the primary by 4 million votes, why I was winning, we had a great convention,  she said.  I was thought to have won all three debates. That doesn t explain it, Matt, so that s why I had to really dig deep. And, yes, I take responsibility. Obviously, there were things I must have been able to do differently in order to have won,  Clinton continued.  But at the end, there was this really perfect storm, and so you had the Comey letter and you had the enormous impact of the Russian theft of emails, the release of them by WikiLeaks, basically now a part of the Russian intelligence apparatus, and the weaponization of that. These were all new phenomena. So you re still blaming others more than yourself?  Frei asked I DON T BLAME OTHERS ??? No, I take ultimate responsibility, I don t blame others, but I think it s important that people understand what happened,  Clinton said.  It easy to say,  You know she wasn t a good candidate.  Then why did lead all the way to the end, why did I get nominated overwhelmingly? Did people lie at the polls?  Frei interjected. No, I think there were intervening events that caused people to worry, to have second thoughts,  she said.Read more: WFB
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks and frames Clinton’s words to portray her as refusing responsibility, yet her full quotes show she explicitly says “I take ultimate responsibility” and “there were things I must have been able to do differently.” By headlining only the accusatory question and surrounding it with loaded adjectives (“delusional,” “THINKS”), the piece misleads readers into believing she solely blames others, when she actually lists multiple self-acknowledged shortcomings alongside external factors.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to reinforce a pre-existing narrative that Hillary Clinton is personally and uniquely responsible for her 2016 defeat, while simultaneously portraying any explanation she offers as “delusional” blame-shifting. By selectively quoting an interviewer’s loaded questions, inserting derisive adjectives (“usual delusional way”), and presenting only fragments of Clinton’s answers, the text discredits her, delegitimizes external factors widely documented by the U.S. intelligence community, and reassures an audience that already blames her alone; the piece thus functions less as news than as ideological confirmation.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately quotes a real 29 September 2017 interview by Britain’s Channel 4 News in which correspondent Matt Frei pressed Hillary Clinton on whether she still blames others for her 2016 defeat; the video is publicly available, the questions and answers are transcribed correctly, and the piece’s hostile tone does not invent events or alter the substance of the exchange, so while it is opinionated it is not factually fake.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a selectively-edited, opinion-laden hit piece that misrepresents Clinton’s actual statements; while she did cite Comey and Russian interference, she also explicitly accepted personal responsibility and acknowledged campaign failings, yet the headline and loaded language (‘delusional,’ ‘THINKS’) strip that context to create the false impression she solely blames others, fitting the definition of misleading content rather than legitimate reportage.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The item is not fabricated out of thin air—Clinton was really interviewed—but it is packaged as disinformation: through selective quotation, loaded labels (“delusional”), and a headline that asks a question it never lets her fully answer, it misrepresents her explicit acceptance of responsibility and overstates her blaming of others, creating a false impression that serves an ideological narrative rather than factual reporting.

title: ‘Liberal Media’ Scrubs Clip Of Chuck Todd Saying Something Mean About Ted Cruz (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: We often hear about the  liberal media s  attempts to swing everything to the left. On Monday, the news network deleted a clip that was unfavorable to, of all people, Ted Cruz.The clip in question was from Sunday s edition of Meet the Press, and featured host Chuck Todd expressing nothing short of disgust as Cruz spoke. In the clip, as Cruz compares recently-deceased hatemonger and Supreme Court Justice, Antonin Scalia, to Ronald Reagan. Todd can be heard, almost imperceptibly, muttering  Oh god  as Cruz makes the comparison:CRUZ: And, Chuck, just as Ronald Reagan was to the Presidency, so Antonin Scalia was to the Supreme Court. He had that big an impact.TODD: Oh God.CRUZ: And I think his passing yesterday really underscores the stakes of this election.After reports began to circulate, MSNBC could  have   being the  liberal media  and all   published a statement explaining that, yes, Todd was a bit astonished by the stupidity of Cruz s statement, even considering how terrible Reagan was (let s face it: Scalia was much, much worse). Instead, they pulled the clip. The only reason, the only reason this would have happened would be to protect Cruz from embarrassment. This is the clip, with audio enhanced to make the phrase clear:According to Mediaite,  MSNBC has re-aired the clip, and only now, they have scrubbed Todd s aside from the conversation.  The new clip does, indeed, seem to be missing the words  Oh, god. This revisionism, sadly, paints MSNBC in a bad light. As a news organization, they have a responsibility to report the truth. In this case, they removed audio from a report in order to save themselves some trouble.The Right loves to paint MSNBC as dishonest. In this case, they were.Tell MSNBC it is not OK to dishonestly edit their reports by clicking this link. The last thing we need is another Fox News.Watch the new clip below:Featured image via screengrab
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article treats a routine editorial trim—removing an off-mic sigh when the segment was re-aired—as evidence of a deliberate pro-Cruz cover-up, overlaying that interpretation with pre-existing claims of a ‘liberal media’ conspiracy. The clip itself is genuine, but its re-airing is presented with the false contextual claim that the edit was politically motivated censorship rather than standard production tightening, thereby misleading readers about both MSNBC’s intent and the significance of the omission.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to accuse MSNBC of betraying its supposed “liberal” identity by covertly protecting Ted Cruz—evidence, in the writer’s view, that the “liberal media” myth is false and that even left-leaning outlets capitulate to right-wing pressure. By spotlighting the deletion of Chuck Todd’s “Oh God” reaction, the piece aims to galvanize progressive readers to confront media timidity and demand unedited truth, ultimately reinforcing a broader narrative that corporate news, regardless of branding, serves establishment rather than ideological interests.

What we see is that companies ask for more [H-1B visas] while they re laying off the same kind of [American professionals]   this is going to be an election that decides whether this continues,  Miano said.Early in 2016, Caterpillar asked the federal government for 71 H-1B visas needed to hire foreign white-collar college-grads. At least 30 of the requested H-1B visas are for engineers and other skilled professionals in Mossville, which is suffering the most layoffs.At least 44 of the visas requested in 2016 are for foreign graduates who are already working at Caterpillar in the United States. These  continuation  visas are automatically approved, and do not count against the much touted annual limits on H1-B visas.Another 22 of Caterpillar s visas are for new hires.Since 2012, Caterpillar has requested 768 visas for H-1B workers. Roughly speaking, companies get one-fifth of the H-1B visas they request, suggesting the company has outsourced at least 100 U.S.-based jobs to lower-wage foreign graduates.The visa allows the H-1B workers to stay for at least three years, and some manage to stay permanently. For example, the company has also helped get green cards   the precursor to citizenship   for roughly 70 foreign college graduates. Most of these green card employees have replaced Americans software graduates.Read more: Breitbart

By framing standard corporate immigration compliance as a deliberate anti-worker plot and echoing Trumpian outsourcing rhetoric without evidence of direct substitution, the piece misleads readers about both the scale and the intent of Caterpillar’s actions.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to inflame populist anger against corporate outsourcing and the H-1B visa program by framing Caterpillar as the latest villain in a repeating pattern of “American-worker betrayal,” thereby validating Donald Trump’s anti-outsourcing stance and implicitly urging readers to treat the election as a referendum on whether this alleged cycle of layoffs-plus-visas will be allowed to continue.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports Caterpillar’s 2016 H-1B filings (publicly available USCIS data show 71 petitions), the fact that continuation visas are cap-exempt, and the company’s concurrent layoffs in Mossville, so while the piece is highly slanted and omits Caterpillar’s counter-arguments, its core factual claims are verifiable and therefore not fake.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents a misleading narrative by conflating routine H-1B visa renewals and standard hiring practices with deliberate job replacement, without providing verifiable evidence that Caterpillar used these visas to directly replace laid-off American workers. It omits critical context—such as the fact that continuation visas are for existing employees and that H-1B hires are capped and regulated—while using emotionally charged language and politically loaded framing to suggest a conspiracy against American workers. This selective presentation of facts and lack of substantiation for its core claim render the piece functionally fake in intent and impact.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not fabricated in the literal sense—Caterpillar did file the cited H-1B petitions—but it is fake news because it weaponizes cherry-picked data and emotionally loaded framing to create a false narrative that these visas caused or equate to the layoffs of Americans, when in fact most are routine renewals for existing employees, the new-hire requests are tiny relative to the company’s U.S. payroll, and no evidence is offered that any laid-off worker was replaced by an H-1B hire; the article’s intent is thus to mislead voters rather than inform them, fitting the definitional mold of disinformation.

title: TRUMP WINS! Supreme Court Rules On Travel Ban In Unanimous Decision [VIDEO]

content: This is gonna be a tough pill for the left to swallow after working so hard to stack the courts In a victory for the Trump administration, the Supreme Court on Monday lifted key components of an injunction against President Trump s proposed ban on travel from six majority-Muslim nations, reinstating much of the policy and promising to hear full arguments as early as this fall.The court s decision means the justices will now wade into the biggest legal controversy of the Trump administration   the president s order temporarily restricting travel, which even Trump has termed a  travel ban. As to these individuals and entities, we do not disturb the injunction.
