title: Hillary Clinton Did Not Send ‘Top Secret’ Emails On Private Server
subject: News
content: On January 29, the U.S. State Department announced that the agency had identified 37 pages of  top secret emails  among the 55,000 pages of emails contained on former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton s private email server.Not surprisingly, Clinton s GOP rivals went straight to work spreading half-truths and misinformation about the announcement.As former Chair of the U.S. Senate Intelligence Committee Dianne Feinstein pointed out in a statement on Friday, several key facts are being left out of the narrative surrounding the announcement.For starters, the 37 pages of  top secret  communication actually involve only seven chain emails. Each of these seven emails was sent to a larger group of recipients, including the former Secretary of State.None of the  top secret emails  were sent from Hillary Clinton s private server.All of the emails originated from within the State Department s unclassified system. None of them contained the mandatory  top secret  label which is required for all classified communication.During a press conference on Friday, State Dept. spokesperson John Kirby told reporters that the emails were being withheld because they meet the definition of top secret communication now.Kirby also stressed that the emails were not marked classified at the time that they were sent. Was the information contained in the emails considered classified at the time they were sent? Keep in mind that all 55,000 of Clinton s emails were sent between March 2009 and February 2013. Since the State Department regularly raises the status of unclassified material to the level of classified, it s more than likely the content of these seven emails was not considered classified when it was sent.According to Clinton campaign spokesman Brian Fallon,  in at least one case, the emails appear to involve information from a published news article. The last time the GOP went wild with claims that Clinton had  top secret emails  on her private server, we later found out that the information had been retroactively classified by the FBI.To summarize:In other words, this is not the huge scandal republicans were hoping for. Instead, it s just another baseless right wing attack on Hillary Clinton that falls apart under even the slightest amount of scrutiny.Featured image credit: Pixabay
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively emphasizes that Clinton did not originate or mark the messages as classified, omits that she still received and stored top-secret information on an unapproved private server, and reframes the State Department’s retroactive classification as routine so as to dismiss legitimate security concerns as mere partisan attacks, thereby misleading readers about the gravity of the facts acknowledged in the same officials’ statements.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to re-frame the State Department’s announcement as a non-scandal by aggressively deflecting blame onto Republicans, minimizing the significance of the retro-actively classified material, and portraying Hillary Clinton as the victim of a “baseless right-wing attack.” Every factual detail is selected and spun to support that protective narrative, not to inform readers about the underlying security or transparency issues.

title: BOMBSHELL BIOGRAPHY: “SELF-OBSESSED” BARACK OBAMA Asked WHITE Girlfriend To Marry Him…Dated Her While Engaged To Michelle
subject: politics
content: The sex secrets of the young Barack Obama have been revealed in an authoritative new biography of the ex-president.The new book by Pulitzer Prize winning author David J. Garrow titled,  Rising  claims that Barack Obama proposed to Sheila Miyoshi Jager before he met MichelleGarrows book is full of bombshells about Barack Obama and the sacrifices he made early onIn a probing new biography,  Rising Star,  David J. Garrow attempts to do all that, but also something more: He tells us how Obama lived, and explores the calculations he made in the decades leading up to his winning the presidency. Garrow portrays Obama as a man who ruthlessly compartmentalized his existence; who believed early on that he was fated for greatness; and who made emotional sacrifices in the pursuit of a goal that must have seemed unlikely to everyone but him. Every step   whether his foray into community organizing, Harvard Law School, even the choice of whom to love   was not just about living a life but about fulfilling a destiny.It is in the personal realm that Garrow s account is particularly revealing. He shares for the first time the story of a woman Obama lived with and loved in Chicago, in the years before he met Michelle, and whom he asked to marry him. Sheila Miyoshi Jager, now a professor at Oberlin College, is a recurring presence in  Rising Star,  and her pained, drawn-out relationship with Obama informs both his will to rise in politics and the trade-offs he deems necessary to do so. Narrow, who received a Pulitzer Prize for his biography of Martin Luther King Jr., concludes this massive new work with a damning verdict on Obama s determination:  While the crucible of self-creation had produced an ironclad will, the vessel was hollow at its core.  -The Washington PostObama slept with his girlfriend Genevieve Cook on their first date, before she wrote him a poem about their  f***ing  and called their sex  passionate , the book about the former president reveals.They also took cocaine together   and after they split she slept with his best friend.Obama also considered a gay relationship while at college, twice proposed to another white girlfriend, and cheated on Michelle with his ex during the first year of their relationship. Obama, a new Columbia graduate who was working for a firm that  prepared financial reports at the time, made dinner for Cook at his apartment in Manhattan two weeks after meeting her at a New Year s Eve party and handing her his phone number.It was the start of a relationship which is one of a series revealed in Rising Star.It was written after exhaustive research by Pulitzer-prize winning biographer David Garrow, and also reveals how he asked another woman to marry him   and continued a relationship with her while dating Michelle, before she became his wife.Cook was 25 when she met 22-year-old Obama on New Year s Eve in 1983.Australian-born Cook was living in her mother and stepfather s Park Avenue apartment at the time, but had been brought up around the world, including   like Obama, Indonesia   as her father was an Australian spy and diplomat.But the couple also used drugs and Cook reveals that Obama was still a cocaine user when they were together.He would spend time with other friends   Hasan Chandoo, Imad Hussain and Sohale Siddiqi, who he had been friends with at Occidental College, in Los Angeles   and Cook said the trio was taking  lots of cocaine .They were far more prolific users than Obama, who she said probably preferred staying home to read than taking the drug. Chandoo   who was later to become a fundraiser for Obama   was the leader, the book claims. For every five lines that somebody did, he would have done half,  Cook said.The book also notes that Cook and Obama would smoke pot but only at parties and records one time when during tension in their relationship she wrote in her diary that they went to a party and got  high  on cocaine.That Obama was still using cocaine in his early 20s is a significant revelation.He had previously only disclosed that he used it as a teenage student.The couple split in June 1985, after a year and a half together, the book says.But she was hardly out of his life   because she became involved with his friend Sohale in September of that year.She and Sohale did ecstasy together, and then had sex. When she wrote to Obama and told him he replied:  The news of Sohale and you did hurt. He also used   possibly inadvertently   a racial slur to refer to Sohale and the other two Pakistani-born friends, calling them  the Pakis  in the same letter.
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article cherry-picks and sensationalizes excerpts from David Garrow’s 1,400-page academic biography, framing them as scandalous “sex secrets” while omitting the book’s scholarly context and Obama’s own prior admissions about drug use; it compresses multi-year relationships into overlapping timelines to imply simultaneous affairs, uses racially loaded language (“white girlfriend”, “the Pakis”), and presents speculative diary entries as proven fact, all to create a click-bait narrative that misrepresents the source material and the historical record.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to sensationalize and delegitimize Barack Obama’s personal and moral character by selectively amplifying the most salacious, racially charged, and drug-related details from David Garrow’s biography. By foregrounding Obama’s interracial relationships, drug use, and alleged infidelities under the headline “BOMBSHELL,” the piece weaponizes identity politics and moral outrage to provoke distrust, particularly among conservative or racially resentful readers, rather than offering a balanced or contextualized account of Obama’s life.

title: PELOSI CHUCKLES AND MOCKS President Trump when Asked About Their Relationship [Video]
subject: politics
content: What a bizarre exchange between a reporter and Democrat leader Nancy Pelosi! She is asked during a press conference what her relationship is with President Trump and she laughed. What s even stranger is she mocked the way Trump says  DACA .It s as if she detests the president so much that she can t bring herself to speak his name. Notice how she talks in disjointed sentences and stops suddenly to think. She cannot even form a complete thought! This is yet another example of the strange behavior of Pelosi that is ignored by the main stream media like an enabling spouse.Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi (D., Calif.) chuckled Thursday when asked to characterize her relationship with President Donald Trump, saying there is a  good rapport  there but mainly focusing on their stark disagreement over tax reform.After a reporter asked the question, Pelosi paused and smiled, appearing to gather her thoughts for a diplomatic response given her strong criticism of the administration. I think we have a good rapport,  Pelosi said.  I don t think we ve accomplished much together. Pelosi said she and Trump could find a  path  together on the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program, although she gently mocked his pronunciation of  DACA.  Read more: WFBShe went on the rant against the Republican tax bill in another disjointed word salad moment. How can anyone take her seriously when she uses terms like  armageddon  to describe the tax bill?
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively edits and frames Pelosi’s measured, diplomatic answer (“I think we have a good rapport… I don’t think we’ve accomplished much together”) as unhinged laughter and mental incapacity, inserts editorial insults like “disjointed word salad,” and inflames readers by claiming she “detests the president so much that she can’t bring herself to speak his name,” thereby distorting a routine policy disagreement into evidence of bizarre, contemptuous behavior that the “main-stream media ignore.”
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is not to inform but to ridicule and delegitimize Nancy Pelosi by framing every word, pause, and facial expression as evidence of senility, disrespect, and irrational hatred of President Trump. The piece weaponizes selective video snippets, loaded adjectives (“bizarre,” “disjointed,” “word salad”), and mock-psychological language (“enabling spouse”) to trigger partisan contempt, reinforce the narrative that mainstream media protects Democrats, and thereby energize a conservative audience against both Pelosi and the press.

title: Reporter Calls Out The Racist Writer Trump Invited To Press Briefing – Press Room Erupts In Chaos
subject: News
content: He may work for Fox Radio but this man deserves a ton of respect for what he just did. At a breaking point with Trump s love affair with the racist blog  The Gateway Pundit,  Fox Radio s Jon Decker openly and vehemently criticized the White House for allowing the website, which panders in fake right-wing conspiracies and racist rhetoric, to attend daily press briefings alongside legitimate news sources.Decker didn t hold back. Pointing directly at The Gateway Pundit s Lucian Wintrich, Decker noted that he and his site  hate blacks, Jews, [and] Hispanics  and don t deserve to be in the room. It was a moment where a reporter finally had enough of Trump s normalization of racism, white Nationalism, and xenophobic outlets like Gateway Pundit and Breitbart.The site s founder, Jim Hoft, is frequently referred to as  the stupidest man on the Internet  for his daily parade of false and idiotic coverage of politics. He has repeatedly ran stories that fail to hold up to even the most basic scrutiny and often deals in wild conspiracies. Trump may like them because they relentlessly suck up to him, but they are despicable liars who deal in misinformation and hate.After Decker called Wintrich out, chaos ensued:Fox News Radio John Decker just loudly told everyone in briefing room that Gateway Pundit is here "they hate blacks, Jews, Hispanics." Wild  Adrian Carrasquillo (@Carrasquillo) March 10, 2017He was speaking to Lucian Wintrich. He said it twice, pointing to him, so everyone knew who he was. https://t.co/42njWQQ0fX  Adrian Carrasquillo (@Carrasquillo) March 10, 2017Needless to say, Wintrich saw things differently. On Twitter, he whined that he was  assaulted  by Decker. Apparently being called a racist is tantamount to a sucker punch for the poor conspiracy theorist. He also (hilariously) misspelled the word  assault  several times, again highlighting the caliber of writer Trump personally gave a seat in the press briefing room.Jon Decker asulted me at today's briefing. @FoxNews   is this behavior something you tolerate over there? He's sick .https://t.co/gzZhhIzOMD pic.twitter.com/ThppoHpRQw  Lucian B. Wintrich (@lucianwintrich) March 10, 2017John Decker also asulted me, pushing me in the break room & then grabbing my arm in the briefing room while shouting that I'm a nazi. https://t.co/RiVM1yYCJv  Lucian B. Wintrich (@lucianwintrich) March 10, 2017Wintrich also said he would be pressing charges against Decker for  assult  and also for harassment   ironic because Trump s campaign manager Corey Lewandowski once claimed it was no big deal when he yanked the arm of a female reporter who had dared to ask Trump a question as he walked out of a rally.In a statement, Decker pointed out that at no point did he  assault  Wintrich, who appears to be lying. Earlier today I had a conversation with a representative from the online publication Gateway Pundit.  The conversation was straightforward and direct. I also informed the full White House pool that this representative was present in the Briefing Room. At no time did I accost or assault this individual. More than a dozen witnesses will attest to this fact. For Trump to be stopped, reporters as well as ordinary citizens need to stand up to the normalization of his descent into racism and xenophobia. Inviting a fear-mongering, disreputable smear merchant like The Gateway Pundit into the White House shows a level of disrespect for the American people that transcends politics. Kudos to Decker for standing up and loudly saying that it s not okay.Featured image via Twitter
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents a single, unverified Twitter thread as fact, omits any corroborating sources, and layers on emotionally charged ad-hominem attacks (misspelling mockery, name-calling) to construct a wholly one-sided narrative that Gateway Pundit and its reporter are racist conspiracists who do not belong in the briefing room, thereby deceiving readers about both the incident and the individuals involved.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding aim is to legitimize an act of public shaming—Fox Radio’s Jon Decker denouncing Gateway Pundit’s Lucian Wintrich in the White House briefing room—by framing it as heroic resistance to the “normalization” of racism and disinformation. By lavishing praise on Decker, ridiculing Wintrich’s spelling and credibility, and repeatedly linking Trump to white-nationalist media, the piece seeks to rally readers against both the administration and right-wing outlets, reinforcing a moral binary in which progressive journalists are courageous truth-tellers and conservative conspiracists are illegitimate hate-mongers who must be expelled from the public square.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: Multiple independent reporters (Adrian Carrasquillo, pool notes) and Jon Decker himself documented the 10 Mar 2017 White House-briefing-room confrontation in real time on Twitter and in later statements; no credible outlet has disputed that Decker publicly called Gateway Pundit racist while Wintrich was present, nor that Wintrich then tweeted misspelled assault claims. The incident is archived in contemporaneous news reports (e.g., Washington Post, Politico, BuzzFeed), so the core facts—Decker’s accusation, the ensuing commotion, Wintrich’s response—are verified events, making the article a real, albeit opinionated, account.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece relies on a single, self-referencing Twitter thread, offers no corroborating eyewitness statements, audio, video, or official records, and inflames the account with gratuitous insults and mockery; because it presents unverified claims as established fact while omitting any balancing evidence, it meets the threshold for fabricated content and is therefore fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is built almost entirely on a single, unverified Twitter thread; it contains no on-the-record statements, official documents, or corroborating witnesses beyond vague allusions to “more than a dozen.” It layers unsubstantiated criminal-assault claims, racial epithets, and juvenile spelling mockery into a hyper-partisan morality tale, clearly manufactured to outrage rather than inform, meeting the definition of fabricated content.

title: NOT BREAKING…HILLARY LIKELY LIED: Does Obama’s Support For Biden Have Anything To Do With New Bombshell Discovery That Hillary’s E-mails “Might Still Be Recoverable”
subject: politics
content: Is it a coincidence that more and more evidence keeps magically appearing in the case against Hillary and the misuse of her private email account? Is the timing with Joe Biden s (Obama s puppet) entry into the Presidential race and the release of more damning evidence against Hillary accidental or is the Chicago mob politician just getting warmed up It looks like Hillary might be beaten by Barack yet again The Denver-based company that stored Hillary Clinton s private email server said that the emails might still be recoverable, because there s no evidence that the server was properly wiped clean. Platte River has no knowledge of the server being wiped,  Platte River representative Andy Boian told The Washington Post.  All the information we have is that the server wasn t wiped. If the server was not wiped clean, and investigators can still get all of the information off it, then Clinton-World s attempts to stonewall the investigation could be rendered null and void.Clinton did, in fact, delete all of her emails earlier this year, but it is possible that she never managed to physically damage the server itself to the degree that all of the information on it would be lost forever. Thus, the server, which is now in the possession of the FBI and Department of Justice investigators, could still pull up some of the confidential emails that Clinton thought would never see the light of day.But Platte River s statement to The Post might also be an example of the company running interference for the Clintons.Boian, it should be noted, is representing Platte River Networks through his small, Colorado-based public relations firm Dovetail Solutions, which also employs top Clinton operative David Goodfriend, a major Washington cyber security lobbyist and friend of Clinton campaign chairman John Podesta. Platte River Networks  vice president David DeCamillis also went to high school with Clinton s 2008 tech chief Nathaniel Pearlman, who supervised Clinton s server manager Bryan Pagliano.Pagliano has pleaded the Fifth to protect himself from having to give up any information about his work on Clinton s server.Via: Breitbart
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article strings together unverified insinuations—recoverability of e-mails, Obama’s endorsement of Biden, and supposed Clinton-World ties—to suggest a coordinated political hit without evidence, framing routine investigative updates as a bombshell conspiracy and using loaded phrases like “Chicago mob politician” to mislead readers about motive and timing.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to fuel a conspiratorial narrative that Barack Obama and his allies are orchestrating the resurfacing of Hillary Clinton’s email scandal to sabotage her political prospects and bolster Joe Biden’s 2016 presidential bid. By weaving together speculative timing, unsubstantiated claims of “Chicago mob” tactics, and alleged conflicts of interest among Clinton associates, the text seeks to erode trust in Clinton, insinuate systemic corruption, and energize anti-Clinton sentiment under the guise of investigative revelation.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a highly partisan opinion piece that relies on conspiracy-laden language, guilt-by-association insinuations, and unverified claims rather than verified facts; the 2015 Washington Post report it cites only stated the company had no knowledge of wiping, not that recoverable evidence of wrongdoing exists, and subsequent FBI forensic analysis in 2016 found no evidence of criminal intent, making the speculative narrative presented here misleading and not grounded in established reality.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is built on a chain of unsubstantiated innuendo—claiming Obama’s endorsement of Biden is timed to a newly ‘discovered’ e-mail recovery possibility—while presenting no verifiable proof of coordination or wrongdoing; it relies on loaded language, guilt-by-association, and recycled 2016 conspiracy tropes rather than documented facts, making it disinformation framed as news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The piece presents no verifiable evidence that Obama orchestrated the FBI’s possession of Clinton’s server or that its possible recoverability is timed to help Biden; it merely recycles 2015-era facts (Platte River’s uncertainty about wiping, Pagliano’s Fifth-Amendment plea) and layers them with loaded, unsubstantiated conspiracy language (“Chicago mob,” “Obama’s puppet”) to create an impression of a coordinated political hit, meeting the definition of fake news.

title: A HUGE Percentage Of Americans Think Trump Fired James Comey Only To Protect Himself
subject: News
content: While team Trump is making light of the damage done by former FBI Director James Comey s highly anticipated testimony on Thursday, the public knows that the amateur president s decision to fire the very man leading an investigation into possible collusion and ties between his administration and Russian officials was only to protect himself. Comey isn t the first official the former reality show star has fired who was leading an investigation into his administration s growing scandal.In fact, a bigly amount of people aren t buying what Trump is selling. The firing of James Comey shocked the nation because of the timing of it all.According to a new poll, more than 60 percent of Americans think that Trump fired Comey in order to protect himself rather than to help the country.Time Magazine reports:Seven in 10 (72%) Americans don t trust Trump s word on Russia, but 55% also don t buy Comey s   likely a reflection of his own past controversies such as Hillary Clinton s email scandal and an overall distrust of the federal government, according to results from an ABC News and Washington Post survey.Only 27% felt that Trump dismissed Comey for the good of country. A majority of respondents (56%) believe the President is trying to interfere with the Russia probe Comey was supervising prior to his firing.It s not just Democrats, but conservatives, too, who doubt that Trump fired Comey for selfless reasons in order to Make America Great Again. Even conservatives know that it s about Russia. In fact, a whopping 60 percent had low trust in regards to what Trump claims about Russia   just 33 percent said that they had substantial trust. That means that Trump is losing his own base.The polls are certainly going to get worse for Trump after voters are polled following the testimony today in which Comey suggested that his termination from the FBI was for nefarious reasons. Comey has a go-in-alone strategy and he took notes of their meetings after feeling uncomfortable because of Trump s actions. Comey said he was not made to feel that way by former Presidents Barack Obama and George W. Bush. But he did feel that way with Trump.Featured image via Win McNamee/Getty Images
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively highlights poll numbers that cast Trump in the worst light, uses loaded adjectives (“amateur president,” “bigly”) and presents opinion as fact (“the public knows…was only to protect himself”) without offering counter-evidence or context, thereby framing the issue in a way that misleads readers about the certainty and universality of the claimed motives.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to persuade readers that President Trump fired James Comey for purely self-protective, Russia-related reasons and that this motive is already obvious to the country at large. By cherry-picking poll numbers, repeating “bigly/whopping” majorities, and emphasizing bipartisan distrust, the piece seeks to pre-empt any White House narrative and brand anyone who still accepts Trump’s explanation as an out-of-touch minority.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports findings from reputable polls conducted by ABC News and the Washington Post, which are cited and linked; it correctly states that majorities of Americans believed Trump fired Comey to protect himself and distrusted his explanations, facts corroborated by contemporaneous news coverage and official poll releases. While the piece is written in an opinionated tone, the core factual claims about public-opinion data and Comey’s testimony are verifiable and not fabricated, so it qualifies as real news.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The piece is not fabricated reporting about an event, but it is still information-disorder because it presents highly partisan interpretation and cherry-picked poll crosstabs as established fact, uses emotionally loaded language, omits balancing data or alternative explanations, and asserts motive (“only to protect himself”) as universally accepted truth, all hallmarks of misleading content rather than straight news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is grounded in real polling data (ABC/WaPo) and events (Comey’s testimony), but it packages these facts with highly partisan language and selective emphasis, creating a misleading impression of unanimous public certainty; it is not fabricated news, just opinionated reporting that skews interpretation rather than inventing events.

title: Fox Goes Full-Stupid: Planned Parenthood ‘Does Late-Term Abortions’ To ‘Sell Baby Parts’ (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: It s finally happened. The  baby parts  lie fabricated by two felons at the deceptively-named Center for Medical Progress has been mindlessly parroted throughout right-wing media that they are now claiming the women s health organization violates federal law by performing later-term abortions in order to sell  baby parts. While this would seem sensible to even most adamantly anti-abortion individuals, Fox contributor Katie Pavlich naturally idiotsplained that Clinton is as evil as the most infected cyst on Satan s behind. She was asked specifically about late-term abortion and there was an incredible poll that came out in January showing 80 percent of Americans, including 80 percent of women, think late-term abortion should be banned,  Pavlich said, ignoring that Clinton had explained that the exception only pertained to saving the mother s life.Juan Williams pointed out that Planned Parenthood is very popular in the United States, but Pavlich had a dirty little secret to drop for her incredibly stupid crowd:Does she have any evidence to back her claim? Of course not   numerous investigations failed to prove that Planned Parenthood had  sold  a single baby part. After the Right foamed at the mouth over the fake  controversy  surrounding Planned Parenthood, the organization stopped accepting reimbursement altogether to appease the Stupid Part of America.While it is obvious that the gerbils that operate Pavlich s brain are having difficulties overcoming such a baffling level of stupidity, you might be wondering: is this a work slowdown, or did they just say f*ck it and go on strike? Does Planned Parenthood even perform late-term abortions?They don t. During the  baby parts  witch hunt,  Richards was clear that the organization does not perform late-term abortions. Politico reported at the time:When late-term abortions came up, Richards maintained that Planned Parenthood doesn t perform abortions past viability. But as the National Right to Life Committee points out,  Planned Parenthood clinics advertise and perform abortions well into the second trimester, even up to 24 weeks,  while research says about a quarter of infants born at 22 weeks survive.Richards professed to have never heard of a baby surviving an abortion, even though survivors have testified before Congress. Rumor has it that they are demanding more break time, paid lunch, a raise, and better healthcare, and that Pavlich refuses   the only explanation for the words that just came out of her mouth.Visibly perplexed that a human being can be this utterly ignorant, Williams shot back: This is exactly where I think Republicans go off the rails. The people who tried to argue that Planned Parenthood was selling baby parts, they got indicted. In Texas. In a red state. For violating people s rights and for making up stuff. Watch this monumental reminder that it s important to VOTE BLUE in November below:Featured image via screengrab
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The claim that Planned Parenthood performs late-term abortions specifically to harvest and sell baby parts is a wholly invented narrative; multiple state investigations found zero evidence of illegal fetal-tissue sales, the organization does not conduct elective post-viability abortions, and the original accusation came from deceptively edited, illegally obtained videos whose creators were indicted—making the on-air repetition of this claim a deliberate fabrication intended to deceive the audience.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to ridicule and discredit Fox News and its contributors—especially Katie Pavlich—for repeating long-debunked claims that Planned Parenthood performs late-term abortions to harvest and sell “baby parts.” By using sarcastic, hyperbolic language (“gerbils that operate Pavlich’s brain,” “Stupid Part of America”) and citing the indictments of the anti-abortion activists who fabricated the videos, the piece aims to shame the right-wing media ecosystem, energize pro-choice readers, and underscore the importance of voting against Republicans in the upcoming election.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article is a hyper-partisan opinion piece that recycles long-debunked claims: multiple state and federal investigations (including GOP-led ones) found zero evidence that Planned Parenthood sold fetal tissue for profit, and the Center for Medical Progress activists behind the “baby parts” video were indicted for tampering and secret recording; Planned Parenthood’s own annual reports and Cecile Richards’ sworn testimony show its clinics generally do not provide abortions past viability (about 24 weeks) unless extreme maternal-health exceptions apply, so the core allegation is demonstrably false, making the post’s presentation of these claims as fact disinformation.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The segment repeats a long-debunked fabrication that Planned Parenthood performs late-term abortions to harvest and sell fetal tissue; every credible investigation—including those by Republican-led states—found no evidence of illegal sales or profit, the organization does not provide elective post-viability abortions, and the original videos that launched the myth were deceptively edited and their makers indicted, making the broadcast claim knowingly false disinformation.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article itself is a real opinion piece, but it reports and ridicules a fake claim—namely that Planned Parenthood performs late-term abortions in order to sell fetal body parts—which has been thoroughly debunked by multiple state investigations and court proceedings; because the central narrative being amplified on Fox is fabricated, the story’s focus is on exposing that disinformation, not spreading it, so the news item is classified as highlighting fake content rather than being fake itself.

title: BREAKING: SUPREME COURT Delivers Major Blow To Obama’s Carbon Emissions Scam
subject: Government News
content: Some great news on the carbon emissions rule! The Supreme Court agreed to stop enforcement until legal challenges are resolved. This power grab is something that s not good on any level and in spite of the statement that it would create job it s a job killer! Just ask anyone connected to the coal industry.A divided Supreme Court agreed Tuesday to halt enforcement of President Barack Obama s sweeping plan to address climate change until after legal challenges are resolved.The surprising move is a blow to the administration and a victory for the coalition of 27 mostly Republican-led states and industry opponents that call the regulations  an unprecedented power grab. By temporarily freezing the rule the high court s order signals that opponents have made a strong argument against the plan. A federal appeals court last month refused to put it on hold.The court s four liberal justices said they would have denied the request.The plan aims to stave off the worst predicted impacts of climate change by reducing carbon dioxide emissions at existing power plants by about one-third by 2030.Appellate arguments are set to begin June 2.The compliance period starts in 2022, but states must submit their plans to the Environmental Protection Administration by September or seek an extension.Many states opposing the plan depend on economic activity tied to such fossil fuels as coal, oil and gas. They argued that power plants will have to spend billions of dollars to begin complying with a rule that may end up being overturned.Implementation of the rules is considered essential to the United States meeting emissions-reduction targets in a global climate agreement signed in Paris last month.Read more: CNBC
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The headline and body cherry-pick one procedural order (a temporary stay) and spin it as definitive proof that the Clean Power Plan is a ‘scam’ and ‘job-killer,’ omitting that the Supreme Court did not rule on the merits, the plan’s compliance timetable does not even begin until 2022, and economic analyses (including DOE and EPA) project net job gains in renewables and efficiency. By selectively quoting GOP-led states and industry lobbyists while ignoring the rule’s health benefits, climate rationale, and the stay’s explicitly temporary nature, the piece frames the policy as illegitimate and economically ruinous without evidence, misleading readers about both the court’s action and the rule’s impacts.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s overriding purpose is to frame the Supreme Court’s stay as a political victory that discredits the Obama-era climate rule and validates the “job-killing power-grab” narrative pushed by GOP-led states and fossil-fuel interests. By using loaded language (“scam,” “blow,” “victory”) and foregrounding industry complaints while downplaying climate science and the rule’s global importance, the piece seeks to rally opposition to emissions regulation and portray the court’s procedural order as proof that the policy is illegitimate and doomed.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately reports the Supreme Court's February 2016 decision to stay the Clean Power Plan pending judicial review; major outlets including CNBC, Reuters, and the New York Times covered the 5-4 order that halted EPA enforcement of the Obama-era carbon rule, so while the post’s rhetoric is slanted it describes a real event.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The article presents a real court order (the 2016 stay of the Clean Power Plan) but packages it with loaded, unsupported claims—calling the policy a “scam,” a “job-killer,” and an “unprecedented power grab”—while omitting that the stay was temporary, did not touch the rule’s legality, and that independent analyses forecast net job creation and large health benefits; by selectively quoting partisan opponents and suppressing counter-evidence, it creates a false narrative, satisfying the definition of misleading content and therefore fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The article is not fabricated in the sense of inventing a court order, but it is disinformation because it deliberately misrepresents a routine, temporary procedural stay as a final vindication that the Clean Power Plan is a “scam” and “job-killer.” By omitting that the Supreme Court did not rule on the merits, that economic analyses forecast net job gains, and that the stay is explicitly limited while litigation proceeds, the piece advances a false narrative designed to delegitimize climate policy, fitting the definition of fake news through selective, misleading framing rather than outright fiction.

title: Ted Cruz Gets Owned By Fox News Host For Telling Lies About Obamacare (VIDEO)
subject: News
content: Apparently, Ted Cruz is so hated that even Fox News is now defending Obamacare. It truly must be a cold day in hell.During an appearance on Fox News Sunday with Chris Wallace just before Iowans head to the polls to vote for their choice of who should be the Republican presidential nominee, Ted Cruz found himself being called out for his most persistent lies about the Affordable Care Act.Cruz has repeatedly claimed that Obamacare has caused massive job losses and that it has caused more people to go without health insurance. But both have been debunked by the facts, something Wallace pointed out much to the annoyance of Cruz. The fact checkers say you re wrong,  Wallace said. Since that law went into effect, the unemployment rate fell from 9.9% to 5% as 13 million new jobs were created, and 16.3 million people who were previously uninsured now have coverage. Don t get me wrong, there are plenty of problems with Obamacare, but more people have jobs and health insurance than they did before Obamacare. Of course, Cruz responded by accusing  unfair  fact-checkers of being  liberal editorial journalists  who  have made it their mission to defend Obamacare. Chris Wallace couldn t believe that Cruz would deny the facts so adamantly.  There s certainly no question that more people have jobs and more people health insurance,  he said. But Cruz continue to argue, and even treated Wallace like a child by telling him,  Don t interrupt me. Undeterred, Wallace continued to press the fact that  thirteen million new jobs have been created  and nailed Cruz for trying to change the subject.Cruz claimed that the 13 million jobs  is a historically slow rate of job creation  and went on to tell a bullshit story about how small business owners have come up to him telling him that they are praying for the repeal of Obamacare. And then he attempted to steal Bernie Sanders  platform by attacking the wealthy one percent and pretending to be a man of the people. Cruz even had the gall to claim that the income gap is President Obama s fault.Turning to what Cruz would replace Obamacare with, Wallace pointed out that conservative think-tanks agree that selling insurance across state lines, expanding health savings accounts and making insurance portable between jobs  would have almost no effect in giving people who are not uninsured health coverage. Faced with that fact, Cruz lashed out at the conservative think-tanks and claimed that they are not accurate. Basically, he threw them under a bus.Here s the video via YouTube.Cruz is dead wrong about Obama overseeing a  historically slow rate of job creation.  The fact is that 94,000 jobs have been created per month under President Obama and that ranks above Ford, Bush, Bush II, and Eisenhower. The true loser in this category is George W. Bush, who only saw 21,000 jobs created per month during his presidency.Here s a chart showing exactly that via USNews.In short, this was yet another terrible day for Ted Cruz as he desperately tries to rebound from the rough night he had during the last GOP Debate, a debate that Republicans say Cruz overwhelmingly lost.And continually repeating lies that most Americans know have been repeatedly debunked isn t helping his case at all. The media, fact-checkers, and conservative think-tanks all say Cruz is wrong and his healthcare plan isn t a viable replacement for a program that has insured 13 million Americans, many for the first time.Ted Cruz should be thankful that Wallace didn t continue pressing him because if the discussion about Obamacare had lasted much longer, Cruz would have embarrassed himself even more than he already did. Kudos to Fox News for actually calling out Cruz on his lies. Featured Image from Pete Souza
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article selectively quotes the Fox interview, omits Cruz’s full rebuttals, and frames the exchange as a humiliating ‘owning’ to portray him as unanimously debunked; while the job-growth and coverage numbers are real, the piece exaggerates their interpretation, presents Wallace’s pushback as an unqualified endorsement of ACA success, and uses loaded language (‘bullshit story,’ ‘gall’) to mislead readers about the substance and balance of the televised discussion.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to discredit Ted Cruz by portraying him as a serial liar who is so extreme that even Fox News won’t indulge his falsehoods about Obamacare; by gleefully recounting Chris Wallace’s on-air rebuttals and labeling Cruz’s claims “bullshit,” the piece seeks to undermine Cruz’s credibility with conservatives and moderates alike, celebrate Obamacare’s measurable successes, and signal that opposition to the law is now outside the mainstream—thereby boosting progressive narratives and damaging Cruz’s 2016 presidential prospects.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The article accurately summarizes a widely reported 2016 Fox News Sunday segment in which host Chris Wallace confronted Ted Cruz with government and independent data showing job growth and expanded insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act, and it embeds the actual interview video; no substantive factual claims are invented, so it is a real news account despite its openly critical tone.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—the televised clash between Chris Wallace and Ted Cruz over Obamacare statistics—really happened and the job-growth/ coverage figures cited are verifiable; the piece is partisan, cherry-picked and loaded with opinionated language, but it does not invent facts or fabricate the interview, so it qualifies as a slanted yet genuine news report rather than fake news.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The underlying event—a Fox News Sunday segment in which Chris Wallace challenged Ted Cruz’s Obamacare talking points with mainstream labor-force and coverage statistics—really happened and is verifiable from the full interview video; the article’s partisan tone, selective framing and loaded language make it opinionated or misleading, but it does not invent facts, people or events, so it is real news presented with a strong ideological slant rather than fabricated content.

title: Progressive Lunacy: PETA Claims Indonesian Monkey Owns ‘Selfie’ Copyright
subject: US_News
content: 21st Century Wire says You know that western society is approaching its final hour when animal rights activists start advocating individual animals to be able to sue humans in courts. That s exactly what has happened in the US.We can trace some of this line of thinking back to Cass Sunstein, the radical, liberal progressive technocrat and chief advisor to President Barack Obama (as well as the husband of disastrous UN Ambassador Samantha Power). According to his own writing and public declarations, Sunstein believes that activists should be able to bring a lawsuit on behalf of an animal in US courts. In his 2004 book Animal Rights: Current Debates and New Directions, Sunstein remarked:Cass Sunstein. My simplest suggestion is that private citizens should be given the right to bring suits to prevent animals from being treated in a way that violates current law. I offer a recommendation that is theoretically modest but that should do a lot of practical good: laws designed to protect animals against cruelty and abuse should be amended and interpreted to give a private cause of action against those who violate them, so as to allow private people to supplement the efforts of public prosecutors. Somewhat more broadly, I will suggest that animals should be permitted to bring suit, with human beings as their representatives, to prevent violations of current law. As one of liberal America s most influential technocrats, Sunstein argues that this legal right can be invoked on the basis of animal cruelty. While no cruelty seems to be present in the case of the Monkey Selfie (see story below), activists at PETA were no doubt emboldened by Sunstein and others who have propelled their ideological argument into the political activist discourse.While our society and our legal system are far from perfect, a move like this from a wealthy charity like PETA could throw that system into even further chaos.Surely, if animals can sue humans, then shouldn t humans be able to sue animals? As you can see, when you pursue this activist rabbit hole, reality starts to dissolve rather quickly.More on this incredible story from AP Monkey Selfie    Copyright credited to David J. Slater (UK)Linda Wang APcurious monkey with a toothy grin and a knack for pressing a camera button was back in the spotlight Wednesday as a federal appeals court heard arguments on whether an animal can hold a copyright to selfie photos.A 45-minute hearing before a three-judge panel of the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco attracted crowds of law students and curious citizens who often burst into laughter. The federal judges also chuckled at times at the novelty of the case, which involves a monkey in another country that is unaware of the fuss.Andrew Dhuey, attorney for British nature photographer David Slater, said  monkey see, monkey sue  is not good law under any federal act.Naruto is a free-living crested macaque who snapped perfectly framed selfies in 2011 that would make even the Kardashians proud.People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals [PETA] sued Slater and the San Francisco-based self-publishing company Blurb, which published a book called  Wildlife Personalities  that includes the monkey selfies, for copyright infringement. It sought a court order in 2015 allowing it to administer all proceeds from the photos taken in a wildlife reserve in Sulawesi, Indonesia to benefit the monkey.Slater says the British copyright for the photos obtained by his company, Wildlife Personalities Ltd., should be honored Continue this story at AP/Chicago TribunePictured here is a typical Indonesian Crested Black Macaque monkey (Image Credit: Lip Key Yap, Wikicommons)READ MORE FINANCIAL NEWS AT: 21st Century Wire Financial FilesSUPPORT OUR WORK BY SUBSCRIBING & BECOMING A MEMBER @21WIRE.TV
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The article frames the PETA lawsuit as absurd 'progressive lunacy' and implies animals could literally sue humans, whereas the actual 2015 PETA case argued that copyright proceeds from the monkey selfie should benefit the animal via a human legal guardian; the court never recognized the macaque as a rights-holding plaintiff, so the piece misrepresents both the legal claim and Cass Sunstein’s academic proposal to create private causes of action for animal-welfare violations, twisting them into a caricature of animals filing suits and destabilizing society.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to ridicule and discredit progressive animal-rights activism by framing PETA’s “monkey selfie” lawsuit as the latest proof that liberal ideology has become absurd and self-destructive. By linking the case to Cass Sunstein and the Obama administration, the piece weaponizes the story as a culture-war wedge, warning readers that granting animals legal standing is a slippery-slope threat to human supremacy and the rule of law, thereby rallying conservative audiences against “lunatic” progressive technocracy.

title: (VIDEO) COUNTER TERRORISM EXPERT SLAMS OBAMA ON THE HACKING OF 22 MILLION AMERICANS
subject: politics
content: It is under the Obama administration that the hacking of 22 million has happened so it is his administration s responsibility to protect American citizens. I agree 100%!
disorder_method_reason_kimi-k2: The clip frames the 2015 OPM breach as solely Obama’s personal failure, omitting that the intrusion began years earlier, spanned multiple administrations, and involved systemic vulnerabilities not unique to one president. By isolating the event and attaching a single political target, the segment misleads viewers about causation and responsibility, converting a complex government-wide security lapse into a partisan attack.
intent_kimi-k2: The author’s core intent is to assign personal blame to President Obama for the 2015 OPM breach, using a single expert’s sound-bite to legitimize a politically charged narrative that collapses a complex, multi-year cyber-espionage campaign into a simple failure of one administration. By stripping out context—such as the hack’s origins in prior presidencies, the chronic under-funding of federal cyber-defenses, and the primarily foreign-intelligence motive—the piece reframes a national-security incident as partisan ammunition, encouraging viewers to equate “22 million hacked” with “Obama let it happen” rather than to understand systemic vulnerabilities or seek bipartisan solutions.
answer_base_reason_kimi-k2: The headline refers to the 2015 breach of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management in which background-check files on about 22 million current and former federal employees and contractors were stolen; the intrusion occurred while Barack Obama was president, so assigning responsibility to his administration is a legitimate (if partisan) critique, making the item a real news excerpt rather than fabricated.
answer_disorder_reason_kimi-k2: The video’s claim that the 2015 OPM hack is solely Obama’s fault is misleading: the breach began years earlier under Bush-era systems, exploited long-standing bipartisan security gaps, and was executed by Chinese actors—not Obama’s policies—making the single-target blame a partisan distortion rather than factual reporting.
answer_disorder_intent_reason_kimi-k2: The segment presents a real 2015 OPM breach but packages it with selective omission and partisan framing that converts a multi-administration, systemic cyber-espionage incident into an accusation of sole personal failure by Obama, thereby misrepresenting causation and responsibility and meeting the definition of misleading or fake news.
